k: Only the registration name with its top-level domain needs to be registered; hostnames can be created by the owner.

items.tz: DNS 伺服器与名称解析
k: A DNS server translates domain names into IP addresses; this process is called name resolution.
A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) identifies the specific location of a resource on the Internet. It consists of the network protocol, the FQDN/IP address, the port number and the path.
More than one application may run on the same host, so a port number is used to identify a specific application. Default ports: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443.
A path is the specific location of a resource relative to the root. If no file name is specified, index.html is loaded by default.

items.t: Folder paths and checking if a URL is valid
items.tz: 文件夹路径与判断 URL 是否有效
k: The path refers to the location of the resource relative to the root directory of the host.
name the type and give the reason by its format, e.g. "IPv6, because it uses hexadecimal groups separated by colons."
HTTPS is a secure version of HTTP that uses SSL/TLS to encrypt data during transmission, ensuring confidentiality, so intercepted data cannot be read.

items.tz: HTTP 请求-回应与状态码
k: GET requests a resource from the server; POST submits data to the server for processing. 404 means the requested resource cannot be found on the server.

SMTP is used to send emails to the email server. POP3 downloads emails to the local computer so they can be read offline; IMAP keeps emails on the server and synchronises them across multiple devices.

items.t: Email protocol misconceptions: POP3 deletion and webmail
items.tz: 电邮协定误解：POP3 删除与网页电邮
k: Web-based email is delivered from the mail server to the browser using HTTP/HTTPS, not POP3/IMAP.

items.t: FTP and application protocols on TCP/IP
items.tz: FTP 与 TCP/IP 上的应用协定
k: FTP is used to transfer files between a client and a file server over a network; user authentication is usually required. HTTP, SMTP, POP3, IMAP and FTP are application protocols on top of TCP/IP.

mc.q: At home, Mary cannot access the HKEAA's web site by entering http://www.hkeaa.edu.hk, but she can do it by entering http://210.0.205.228. Why?
o: The DNS server is out of service.
The web server is out of service.
Her web browser needs an extra plug-in.
The router used at home is out of order.
mc.e: The IP works, so only domain-name resolution (DNS) fails.

mc.q: A company develops an internal email system. It adopts HTML format instead of plain text for the email because
o: the POP protocol can be used.
mc.e: HTML email supports fonts, colours, etc.; plain text can't.

mc.q: In an email system, what is the use of IMAP and SMTP?
o: IMAP and SMTP are application programs that regulate email transmission.
IMAP and SMTP are the part of the operating system that manages email resources.
IMAP and SMTP are utility programs that improve the efficiency of email transmission.
IMAP and SMTP are sets of rules that determine how email is transmitted.
mc.e: Protocols are sets of rules for communication.

mc.q: When browsing a web page, which of the following will be involved?
mc.e: Browsing uses a URL and travels over IP (with HTTP); FTP is not needed.

mc.q: In an email application, the settings of __X__ and __Y__ are used for receiving email and sending email respectively.
mc.e: IMAP/POP receive mail; SMTP sends it.

mc.q: The smart thermostat connects to the Internet through a wireless connection. What is the advantage of this?
o: It is convenient for installing and controlling the thermostat.
The data can be encrypted before transmission.
Customers are required to enter a password to control the smart thermostat.
mc.e: No cables needed, so it is easy to install anywhere; the other points apply to wired links too.

mc.q:
Peter is going to set up a web site for his new company so that customers can access his web site through any one of the following links:

web.goodcompany.hk
www.goodcompany.hk
www.goodcompany.com.hk
www.goodcompany.com
web.goodcompany.com

How many domain names does he need to register?
mc.e: goodcompany.hk, goodcompany.com.hk and goodcompany.com; www/web are just host names under them.

mc.q: Which of the following is not an email protocol?
mc.e: FTP is for file transfer; IMAP, SMTP and POP are email protocols.

mc.q: Amy can browse the web site of ABC School through its IP address, but not its URL. What is the possible reason for this?
o: The corresponding web pages have not been uploaded onto the web server.
The domain name system (DNS) server is temporarily out of service.
The browser in use is not the latest version.
Some plug-ins for the browser in use have not been installed.
mc.e: The site works by IP, so only the name-to-IP lookup (DNS) is failing.

mc.q: When watching videos from a web site using streaming technology, which of the following will be involved?
mc.e: The domain name is resolved by DNS and data travels over IP; streaming does not use FTP.

mc.q:
An IP address (IPv6) consists of 8 groups of 4-digit hexadecimal numbers separated by colons, as shown in the following example:
2001:08AB:2347:AFF0:1234:CC23:98D2:1A45
How many possible addresses are there in this IP addressing?
mc.e: 8 × 4 = 32 hex digits, each with 16 values: 16^32.

mc.q:
The following two URLs can be used to access the same web site:
'http://202.8.88.24' and 'http://www.hkedcity.net'
Which of the following statements about the two URLs is/are correct?
st: (1) The DNS server may translate 'www.hkedcity.net' to '202.8.88.24'.
(3) The web pages accessed through the IP address are more secure.
mc.e: DNS maps the domain to the IP; URLs can use other protocols and using an IP is not more secure.

mc.q: Which of the following protocols is/are involved when browsing https://www.gov.hk?
mc.e: DNS resolves the name and IP carries the packets; FTP is not used.

mc.q: Which of the following can be used to identify a host computer on the Internet?
mc.e: An IP address uniquely identifies a host on the Internet.

mc.q: Which of the following about HTTP is/are correct?
st: It is used to transfer hypertext documents.
It is used to translate URLs into IP addresses.
It is used to store the browsing history.
mc.e: DNS translates domain names to IP. The browser stores history.

mc.q: Which of the following describe(s) the URL, https://www.abc.edu.hk/en/ ?
st: en is a path on the web server.
The web site is registered as an educational institution in Hong Kong.
mc.e: /en/ is a path, and .edu.hk means a Hong Kong education site. The domain name is www.abc.edu.hk, not just abc.

mc.q: Which of the following about the use of HTTP is correct?
o: It can convert a domain name into an IP address.
It can distinguish a wireless network from a wired network.
It can retrieve a web page from a web server.
It can encrypt and decrypt data through a secure channel.
mc.e: HTTP transfers web pages. DNS converts names and HTTPS/SSL encrypts.

mc.q: Mary uploads a photo to her social media account through a browser. Which of the following protocols will probably be involved?
mc.e: DNS finds the server, HTTP(S) carries the upload and IP routes the packets: all three.

mc.q: Which of the following about IP addresses is/are correct?
st: They contain location information and make network devices accessible for communication.
They are used to reassemble the data received back into the original order.
They can be used with both the Internet and Intranet.
mc.e: IP addresses locate devices and work on both Internet and intranet. Reassembling packets is TCP's job.

mc.q: Which of the following is the common input and output of a domain name system (DNS) server?
o: Input: IP address, Output: MAC address
Input: Domain name, Output: MAC address
Input: Domain name, Output: IP address
mc.e: DNS turns a domain name into an IP address.

mc.q: If the Government establishes an ‘Anti-drugs Authority’ in Hong Kong, which of the following domain names would be appropriate for it?
mc.e: .gov.hk is for HK government bodies.

mc.q: When browsing a simple web page over the Internet, how will the content of the web page normally be transmitted?
o: The content will be divided into several packets that are probably sent through a single physical path.
The content will be divided into several packets that are probably sent through different physical paths.
The content will be encrypted and sent through a single physical path.
The content will be encrypted and sent through different physical paths.
mc.e: Packet switching: packets may take different routes. A simple page (HTTP) is not encrypted.

mc.q: The hardware address of a network device consists of 48 bits. Which of the following is a valid address in hexadecimal numbers?
mc.e: 48 bits = 12 hex digits. C has 'G', not a hex digit.

mc.q: Mr. Chan wants to register a domain name using his name, 'Chan Tai Man'. Which of the following domain names is not valid?
mc.e: .com.org is not a real second/top-level combination. Domain names are case-insensitive.

mc.q: Amy owns a domain name, 'amycomp.com'. Which of the following URLs is not owned by Amy?
mc.e: amycomp.com.hk is a different domain.

mc.q: A protocol is best described as
o: a set of rules for the format and order of data exchanged
mc.e: Protocols specify format and order of data.
mc.ez: 协定规定数据格式和次序。

mc.q: Why can devices with different operating systems communicate on the Internet?
mc.e: Standard protocols make OS irrelevant.

mc.q: Which protocol divides data into packets and reassembles them?
mc.e: TCP divides, numbers, reassembles.

mc.q: Which protocol adds the destination address and selects the path?
mc.e: IP handles addressing and routing.

mc.q: Why are packets numbered?
o: So they can be reassembled in the correct order
mc.e: Numbers restore order.

mc.q: Main advantage of dividing data into packets:
o: Only a corrupted packet needs to be resent
mc.e: Only the damaged packet is resent.

mc.q: Packets of one message may arrive out of order because
o: IP may route them along different paths
mc.e: Routing can choose alternative paths.

mc.q: Correct order of TCP/IP transmission steps:
mc.e: Division, IP addressing, routing, reassembling.

mc.q: In the five-layer stack, which layer adds the network header containing IP addresses?
mc.e: Network layer adds NH.

mc.q: Which layer maps an IP address to a MAC address?
mc.e: Data Link layer.

mc.q: Which layer transmits bit streams over cables?
mc.e: Physical layer.

mc.q: Adding headers layer by layer at the sender is called
mc.e: Encapsulation.

mc.q: Which is an advantage of Internet communication stated in the book?
mc.e: Fast, low cost, multimedia.

mc.q: An IP address is
o: a changeable numerical address identifying a device in a network
the same as a domain name
mc.e: Changeable, numerical, unique in network.

mc.q: Who ultimately assigns IP addresses (through ISPs)?
mc.e: ICANN via ISP.

mc.q: How many bits in an IPv4 address?
mc.e: 32 bits.

mc.q: How many IPv4 addresses are possible?
Which IPv4 address is valid?
mc.e: Four octets 0–255.

mc.q: Which IPv4 address is INVALID?
The binary of 148 is

k: IoT refers to a network connecting different objects. The connected objects share collected data and provide new functionalities. IoT collects the data; cloud computing stores and processes it in real time; objects then act automatically.
Everything in the cloud is stored in remote servers hosted by a third party and is accessible through the Internet.
name the type, then say what is on the server: "the program runs on the cloud server, so no installation is needed on the local computer" .
"Members can edit the same document simultaneously in real time; there is only one up-to-date version, avoiding version inconsistency."
sensors collect data → sent to cloud → analysed → automatic action in real time → name the area (e.g. Smart Mobility).

items.t: Smart Economy: online banking and payment
items.tz: 智慧经济：网上银行与支付
k: "faster, contactless payment; no need to handle cash" vs "customers who prefer cash cannot pay; widens the digital divide" .
always say who (employer/employee) gets the pro or con.

items.t: Smart living, government, mobility, people, environment
items.tz: 智慧生活、政府、交通、教育、环境
k: for a scenario, list Internet services as search (database access), update records, store data, calculate .
"Email is a cross-platform communication method; users can send email to anyone regardless of the email service provider."
"Use Bcc when sending bulk email so that recipients' email addresses are not disclosed to each other (protect personal data)."
"Reply All sends to the sender and all recipients in the To and Cc fields; Bcc recipients are not included."
"The email only contains the URL, so it does not take up storage space in the mailbox."
"Mark the email as spam to improve the accuracy of the spam filter"; "add the sender to the whitelist".
"Only the screen image is sent to the client; the program runs on the host computer."

items.t: Benefits and limitations of remote logon
items.tz: 远程登入的好处与限制
k: "The program is executed on the remote computer, so the user can make use of its hardware and software licence."
"Online chat allows real-time communication with an individual or a group using multimedia."
forum = topic-based Q&A ; SNS = stay connected by sharing experiences .

items.t: Blogs, vlogs and how SNS absorbed them
items.tz: 博客、Vlog 与 SNS 的整合
k: In a blog only the owner can initiate topics, while in a discussion forum any user can start a discussion on a subject.
justify with the factor: "large file size → cloud storage; confidential → network drive over VPN" .

items.t: File transfer methods: pros, cons and limits
items.tz: 文件传送方法：优缺点与限制
k: Cloud storage supports large files without compression and auto-sync, but files are only available offline after download.
"SEO is the process of improving website traffic by increasing the rankings and visibility in search results."

items.t: Four steps of information search; paid vs organic results
items.tz: 搜寻资讯四步骤；付费与自然结果
k: Organic results are ranked by the search algorithm according to relevance, while paid results are advertisements from sponsors.

Databases contain published content evaluated for accuracy by publishers, so they are a more reliable source for academic research. Search engine results can be contributed by any Internet user and may change at any time.
Choose keywords (use synonyms / more specific keywords) → choose source type → use Boolean operators → refine the search (e.g. time range, usage rights filter).
Use "-" to exclude a keyword; use OR to include either term (widens results); use quotation marks for an exact match; use site: to search a specific website or domain.
Evaluate the reliability, credibility and timeliness of the information: verify with other sources, check the domain and the author, and check the publish date.

items.t: Fake news, content farms and private browsing
items.tz: 假新闻、内容农场与私密浏览
k: Before spreading information, verify it with the official website or other credible sources, because false information may lead others to make wrong decisions.
Misinformation may cause unnecessary panic, reputational damage, monetary loss and distrust in media, and lead others to make wrong decisions. Confirm the primary source before forwarding.

items.t: Internet vs library as information sources
items.tz: 互联网与图书馆作资料来源
k: The Internet allows searching anywhere and anytime and its information is more likely to be up to date; however, anyone can publish online, so the information must be evaluated, and it is still protected by copyright.
Lossless compression offers the best quality but uses much more transmission data and slows down loading time; choose suitable file formats to reduce file size for faster transmission.

JPG uses lossy compression with small size and highest compatibility; PNG uses lossless compression and supports transparency; GIF supports animation but only 256 colours; WebP gives a smaller file size with the same quality.

Vector graphics (SVG) store shapes as mathematical descriptions, so they can be scaled to any size without losing quality – suitable for icons on devices with different resolutions. Raster images become pixelated when enlarged.
MP3 is the most compatible lossy format; AAC gives better sound quality at a lower bitrate; FLAC is lossless with large file size; WAV is usually uncompressed and used as the original for editing.
A codec is an encoding and decoding scheme. MP4 is the most compatible; WebM gives a smaller file with similar quality; provide both so that browsers can fall back to MP4.
A plug-in is a program that enables a browser to support extra formats, codecs or functions. Plug-ins should be kept up to date to fix security vulnerabilities.
A media player is software for the playback of audio and video files; it fails to play the content if the supporting codec is missing, so install the codec or update the player.

items.t: Plug-in and media player examples; codec packs
items.tz: 插件与媒体播放器例子；codec pack
k: If the media player cannot play a file, update the player or install the missing codec (e.g. a codec pack).
Streaming delivers media over the Internet as a continuous flow of data, so users can play and download the media simultaneously without waiting for the entire file.
Streaming allows playback in real time without downloading the entire file and saves storage space, but it cannot be played offline and the quality depends on the network bandwidth.
The client plays the media while it continues to download and buffer the remaining content; if the buffer runs out the playback pauses.

items.t: Voice mail: voice calls and voice messages
items.tz: 话音邮件：语音通话与语音讯息
k: Voice calls use VoIP to enable real-time communication like phone calls; voice messages can be delivered and received anytime as an alternative to text messages.

Video conferencing supports two-way real-time interaction for a relatively small group, suitable for private events; webcasting broadcasts live or pre-recorded media mainly one-way to a large audience, suitable for public events.
A unique meeting code and password prevent unauthorised people from entering; end-to-end encryption protects data during transmission.

items.tz: 影响串流质素的技术因素
k: Higher bitrate, resolution and frame rate give better quality but need more bandwidth; if bandwidth is insufficient, latency and pixelisation occur. Adaptive streaming adjusts quality according to the user's network.

items.tz: 低延迟模式与直播问题
k: Low latency mode lets viewers watch nearly in real time, suitable for interacting with viewers' comments, but the smaller buffer makes playback more likely to pause on an unstable network.

mc.q: When using Internet search engines, it is better to include operators like ‘+’ in search strings because
o: the search time can be shorter.
the search results include the titles of web pages only.
the search results can be more relevant.
the search results can include both local and foreign web sites.
mc.e: Operators narrow the search, so results are more relevant.

mc.q: John can view an online video on the computer at home but not on the computer in his school. Why?
o: The operating system does not support the video playback.
The browser does not support the video playback.
The video is not in HTML format.
The maximum data transfer rate of the school network is low.
mc.e: The school browser may lack the needed plug-in/codec support for the video.

mc.q: Peter watches a webcasting video at home using streaming technology and finds that the video does not play smoothly. Which of the following are the possible causes?
mc.e: Streaming depends on the connection type and bandwidth, not the video's length.

mc.q: Which of the following activities transfers minimal data through the Internet?
o: Sending an email of 10 KB with a 2 MB audio file to 50 receivers
Uploading and converting an image of 10 MB to JPG format using an online tool
Updating a web page of 10 KB containing a hyperlink to a 2 GB file
Watching a 60-minute video of 500 MB online using streaming technology
mc.e: Only the 10 KB page is sent; the linked file is not transferred.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about streaming technology is/are correct?
st: (1) A music performance can be viewed live.
(3) Illegal distribution of movies can be controlled.
mc.e: Streaming allows live viewing; it can run over HTTP and does not stop piracy.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about the use of video streaming technology is/are correct?
st: The data transfer rate can be increased.
The video can be watched before the file is completely downloaded.
The video quality can be enhanced.
mc.e: Streaming lets you play while downloading; it does not speed up the link or improve quality.

mc.q: Which best describes the Internet of Things (IoT)?
o: A network connecting different objects that share collected data
mc.e: IoT connects objects that share data and provide new functions.
mc.ez: IoT 连接不同物件并分享数据。

mc.q: Which wireless technologies are commonly used in IoT?
mc.e: IoT uses Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID and NFC.

mc.q: Why is cloud computing important for IoT?
o: IoT generates huge amounts of data that must be stored and processed instantly
mc.e: Cloud stores and processes the massive IoT data.
mc.ez: 云端储存和处理大量 IoT 数据。

mc.q: Which is NOT a benefit of cloud services?
mc.e: Cloud services need Internet access.

mc.q: Google Docs Editors is an example of which cloud service?
mc.e: Use the software from the cloud server without installing.

mc.q: Microsoft Azure renting powerful computing to run tasks is an example of
o: Operating system (run tasks on virtual machines)
mc.e: Running tasks on powerful virtual machines.

mc.q: Which is the main advantage of cloud collaboration over passing a USB drive?
o: Members can edit the same document simultaneously in real time
The file is encrypted by USB
mc.e: Real-time co-editing with one version.

mc.q: A smart city mainly aims to
o: address urbanisation challenges and improve quality of life using data
mc.e: Better decisions via IoT data and AI.
mc.ez: 以数据应对城市化问题。

mc.q: Which is NOT one of Hong Kong's six smart city areas?
mc.e: Six: Economy, Living, Mobility, Environment, People, Government.

mc.q: Real-time adaptive traffic signals belong to
mc.e: Traffic = mobility.

mc.q: Fill-level sensors in rubbish bins to plan collection routes belong to
mc.e: Waste management = environment.

mc.q: Which platform lets Hong Kong citizens log in to government services with one digital identity?
mc.e: iAM Smart.

mc.q: A shop accepts only mobile payments. A possible social disadvantage is
mc.e: Excludes customers without/unfamiliar with mobile payment.

mc.q: Which is a risk for employers when staff work from home (SOHO)?
o: Data breaches due to insecure connections outside the office
mc.e: Home networks may be insecure.
mc.ez: 家中连线不安全，可能外泄数据。

mc.q: Which is an advantage of email over instant messaging?
o: Email is cross-platform regardless of provider
mc.e: Email works across providers and apps.

mc.q: In tom@abcss.edu.hk, 'abcss.edu.hk' is the
mc.e: After @ is the domain name.

mc.q: To send a newsletter to 300 parents without revealing their addresses, use
mc.e: Bcc hides addresses.

mc.q: Which field is used for recipients who only need to be informed and whose addresses can be seen by others?
mc.e: Carbon copy, for information.

mc.q: Sender A emails To: B, Cc: C, Bcc: D. B clicks Reply All. Who receives B's reply?
mc.e: Reply All = sender + To + Cc; Bcc excluded.
mc.ez: 寄件人及 To/Cc，不含 Bcc。

mc.q: Sender A emails To: B, Cc: C, Bcc: D. What does D see in the header?
mc.e: A Bcc recipient sees To, Cc and their own address.
mc.ez: Bcc 收件人看到 To、Cc 及自己。

sec: 4.1 Basic Components of a Web Page

items.t: Three components of a web page: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
k: HTML uses markups (tags) to describe the structure and content of a web page. CSS describes the appearance/style of HTML elements. JavaScript is a programming language embedded in HTML that adds dynamic and interactive functions.

items.t: HTML is a markup language, not a programming language
items.tz: HTML 是标记语言，不是编程语言
k: Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is a standard markup language used to write web pages. It is not a programming language but a cross-platform language used to define the elements in a web page.

items.t: CSS and why it is useful
k: Cascading Style Sheet (CSS) is used to describe the style of HTML elements. A style can be applied to different pages of the website at the same time without setting them one by one, making the website easier and more efficient to create and maintain.

HTML5 added new semantic elements and attributes such as <header>, <footer> and <section>. Elements that only change appearance, such as <center>, <font> and <frame>, were removed and replaced by CSS.

items.t: How a browser gets a web page (HTTP)
k: The client (browser) sends an HTTP request to the web server; the server returns an HTTP response with a status code and the HTML file; the browser interprets the HTML and displays the web page.

items.t: HTML editors: text editor vs web authoring tool
items.tz: HTML 编辑器：文字编辑器与网页制作工具
k: A text editor is available in all operating systems and produces concise HTML code. A web authoring tool is WYSIWYG, so users can design pages without knowing HTML.

items.t: Viewing source code, online previewers and drag-and-drop builders
items.tz: 查看源代码、在线预览器与拖放式建站工具
k: Inspecting a web page in the browser shows HTML code such as <html>, <body> and <img src="...">, not program statements like print().
The <html> element is the root element. <head> contains information about the file, such as the title and scripts. <body> is the container for all the visible content of the web page.
An element consists of a start tag, content and an end tag. Attributes are written in the start tag to provide additional information about an element.

items.t: Headings, paragraphs, line breaks and horizontal rules
items.tz: 标题、段落、换行与水平线
k: <h1> to <h6> define headings, <p> defines a paragraph, <br> inserts a line break and <hr> inserts a horizontal line. Extra spaces and line breaks in the source code are ignored by the browser.
Comments <!-- … --> are not displayed by the browser. The <pre> element displays preformatted text, keeping all spaces and line breaks.
<b>, <i> and <u> make text bold, italic and underlined; <sup> and <sub> display superscript and subscript.

items.t: The style attribute: font, size and alignment
items.tz: style 属性：字体、大小与对齐
k: The style attribute applies CSS properties to an element, e.g. style="font-family:Arial; font-size:24px; text-align:center".

items.t: Colours: color, background-color and hex codes
items.tz: 颜色：color、background-color 与十六进制代码
k: Colours can be given as hexadecimal RGB codes #RRGGBB, where each pair (00–FF) represents the intensity of red, green and blue.

items.t: Combining styles, background images, audio and video
items.tz: 组合样式、背景图片、声音与影片
k: Multiple style values are separated by semicolons; multimedia such as audio and video can be embedded with <audio> and <video>.
<ul> creates an unordered (bulleted) list and <ol> creates an ordered (numbered) list; each item is defined by <li>.
<table> defines a table, <tr> a table row, <th> a header cell and <td> a data cell. Padding is the space between the cell content and its border; border-spacing is the space between cells.

items.tz: 合并储存格：colspan 与 rowspan
k: colspan specifies the number of columns a cell should span; rowspan specifies the number of rows a cell should span.

items.t: Images: img, src, alt, width and height
k: The src attribute specifies the path of the image; the alt attribute provides alternative text that is displayed if the image cannot be shown and can be read by screen readers.

items.tz: 用 anchor 标签建立超连结
k: A hyperlink is created with the anchor element <a>; the href attribute specifies the destination URL, and the content between the tags is the clickable part.
If the destination is an anchor on the same page, the symbol "#" must be added before the anchor name in href, e.g. href="#part2".
An iframe (inline frame) embeds another HTML document within the current web page; src specifies the page and width/height set the size of the frame.

items.tz: HTML 电邮与纯文字电邮
k: Emails can be written in HTML format, which allows text formatting, images and hyperlinks, making them more attractive.

items.tz: 网站结构：线性、层次、矩阵
k: A linear structure links pages one after another in sequence; a hierarchical structure organises pages in a tree from the homepage to categories and sub-pages; a matrix structure interlinks pages so users can jump freely between them. A well-organised architecture strengthens the user experience.

UI refers to the graphic design and appearance of a web page, including buttons, icons and other visual elements. UX refers to users' impression of the website and their overall experience when browsing it.
Before actually creating a web page, sketching a wireframe helps us plan the content and layout of the page.

items.t: Website navigation: navigation bar and sitemap
items.tz: 网站导航：导航栏与网站地图
k: A navigation bar lets visitors quickly understand how information is arranged and move between pages; a sitemap lists all sections of the website to help visitors and search engines locate information quickly.

items.tz: 跨平台与响应式网页设计
k: Responsive web design makes web content adapt to different screen sizes, platforms and device orientations, so the site displays well on all devices without creating separate layouts.

Readability refers to the extent to which the content of a web page is easy to read and understand. It can be improved by using lists and tables, multimedia elements, suitable font sizes and high colour contrast between text and background.

items.t: Colour schemes and the mood they create
k: Low colour contrast between text and background makes reading difficult, e.g. yellow text on an orange background.
Users can only select from specific values, which ensures that the data entered is within expectations and reduces input errors; it is also faster and easier, especially on touch screens.

items.t: Exam-style input design: dates, ▲▼ buttons and kiosk layouts
items.tz: 考试式输入设计：日期、▲▼ 按钮与自助机版面
k: Users can only select from valid values, which reduces input errors and shortens input time. A drop-down list does not use a check digit and does not raise the character limit.

Web accessibility design makes the information on a website accessible to everyone, including people with visual impairment, hearing impairment and physical disability, e.g. by providing alternative text for images, font size options and captions.
Images should be compressed (e.g. converted from BMP to JPG) to reduce file size and shorten loading time; pages should keep a consistent layout and suit the target audience.
Wix is a drag-and-drop web authoring tool that provides free web hosting; the website must be published before others can access it through its URL.
Free web hosting providers usually limit storage space and browsing speed. Purchasing a hosting plan allows a large number of users to visit at the same time and increases storage space and speed.

mc.q: When constructing tables in a web page, which of the following attributes of the tables can be set?
mc.e: Tables have border and alignment attributes; page margin belongs to the page.

mc.q: Mary creates a file in HTML format instead of text format. Why?
st: (3) Videos can be displayed when opening the file.
mc.e: HTML can hold hyperlinks and embed video; plain text is also cross-platform, so (1) is false.

mc.q: John edits the font colour of a web page. How many different colours can he choose?
mc.e: Web colours are #RRGGBB: 256 levels for each of R, G, B.

mc.q: When placing a table in a web page, which of the following is not a table setting?
mc.e: HTML tables have no formulas; that's a spreadsheet feature.

mc.q: Colour codes are used when defining the background colour on a web page. What is the range of hexadecimal values for the colour codes?
mc.e: Each of R, G, B uses one byte: 00 to FF.

mc.q: A web page displays some images. In addition to the names of the image files, what other information will be included in the HTML code of the web page?
st: (1) The paths of the image files
(2) The size of the image files
(3) The IP address of the server that stores the HTML file
mc.e: holds the path to the file; file size and the server's IP are not written in the HTML.

mc.q: In HTML, which of the following are the attributes of a table (TABLE)?
st: (1) URLs of the contents of cells
(3) Media types of the contents of cells
mc.e: TABLE has attributes such as cellspacing and bgcolor.

mc.q: A supermarket will provide an online platform for customers to buy food. Which of the following should be considered when designing the user interface?
mc.e: All three affect usability for different customers.

mc.q: Which of the following should be considered when designing web pages?
st: The time for loading web pages
mc.e: Loading time, ease of use and colours all matter in web design.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about constructing traditional frames in a web page is/are correct?
st: More than one HTML file is needed.
A table with more than one column or row is needed.
More than one background colour is needed.
mc.e: Each frame shows a separate HTML file, plus a frameset file. No table or colours needed.

mc.q:
In the following HTML code, what are the six digits after ‘#’?

<BODY BGCOLOR="#112233">
st: They represent three values for the colours red, green and blue.
They are used to transfer to DNS for web browsing.
They refer to three hexadecimal values.
mc.e: #RRGGBB: three hex values for red, green, blue. Nothing to do with DNS.

mc.q: Which of the following actions should not be carried out when constructing a web page?
o: Insert multimedia elements but not photos.
mc.e: HTML is interpreted by the browser, never compiled.

mc.q: Which technology describes the structure of a web page?
mc.e: HTML uses markups to describe structure.

mc.q: Which technology adds interactive behaviour such as responding to a button click?
mc.e: JavaScript is a programming language that adds dynamic programs.

mc.q: Which statement about HTML is correct?
o: It is a cross-platform markup language
It is a programming language with loops
mc.e: HTML is a cross-platform markup language, not a programming language.
mc.ez: HTML 是跨平台标示语言。

mc.q: What is the main advantage of using CSS for a multi-page website?
o: One style can be applied to many pages at once
mc.e: A shared style updates all pages, easier maintenance.

mc.q: Which element was REMOVED in HTML5?
mc.e: <font>, <center>, <frame> were removed; CSS replaces them.

mc.q: In an HTTP response, 'status: 200' means
Which element was ADDED in HTML5?
mc.e: <header>, <footer>, <section> are new in HTML5.

mc.q: Which is an advantage of a web authoring tool over a text editor?
mc.e: Authoring tools are WYSIWYG.

mc.q: Which is an advantage of a text editor for writing HTML?
o: Found in all operating systems and produces concise code
mc.e: Text editors exist in every OS and give concise code.
mc.ez: 所有系统都有、代码精简。

mc.q: Which file name will a browser open as a web page?
mc.e: .html or .htm.

mc.q: Which is the root element of an HTML document?
mc.e: <html> is the root.

mc.q: Where is the <title> element placed?
mc.e: <title> belongs in <head>.

mc.q: The text inside <title> is shown

sec: 5.2 Effective Measures to Improve Network Security

k: Malware refers to programs that can damage computer functions, steal user data, gain unauthorised access, or attack networks. Always name the type AND describe its behaviour.

items.t: Hackers: black hat and white hat
k: White hat hackers legally attack computer systems to look for security bugs, helping organisations improve network security.
A virus attaches itself to executable files or documents. Once the user executes the program, the virus attacks the files and other data in the computer and replicates itself.
A worm is self-replicating malware that does not need to be attached to any file and can spread to other computers on the network by itself.
A Trojan program disguises itself as a useful application to lure users into installing it. It may create a backdoor that allows hackers to gain remote control of the computer.
Spyware's main purpose is to steal the user's personal information, such as account passwords and keyboard input, while hiding to avoid being noticed. Adware profits from displaying advertisements.
Ransomware encrypts the files in a computer, and the hacker then demands a ransom for decryption.
name the channel, then the matching prevention.
match each malware to its threat: ransomware → ransom; worm → resources exhausted; Trojan → remote control; spyware → data stolen.
A MITM attack is a hacker attack between the normal sender and receiver, intercepting or tampering with the communication between the two parties.

A DoS attack refers to the attempts of hackers to make the target server unable to provide services to users. In a DDoS attack, hackers use numerous hacked computers as zombie computers, remotely controlled to send requests to the target.

Antivirus software scans the information in a computer and isolates infected files. It compares files with the virus signatures in the virus database. Users should enable automatic update to keep the database up to date.

items.t: Detecting new malware and choosing security software
items.tz: 侦测新恶意软件与选择保安软件
k: Antivirus software must be updated regularly so its virus signatures can identify the latest malware; a newly released virus may not be detected even by the latest software until its signature is added.

A firewall filters incoming and outgoing data packets, blocks malicious packets, prevents unauthorised access, and stops the computer from sending malicious packets. It checks the IP address, type and port of each packet against defined rules.

items.tz: 软件防火墙与硬件防火墙
k: Software firewall: can only protect a single device, easier to install and lower cost. Hardware firewall: protects all devices in the network, more efficient and stable, but the cost is high.

Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user. Authorisation is the process of granting users the access to data. Accounting is monitoring the user's access records in the system to ensure the correct use of data.

A VPN establishes a tunnel between the user's device and the VPN server. The VPN application encrypts network data packets, which protects data transmitted on the Internet and prevents unauthorised access.
WPA uses the Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP), which encrypts transmission data with a constantly changing key. WPA2 is an advanced version of WPA which conforms to higher security standards.

items.t: Hide SSID and MAC address filtering
items.tz: 隐藏 SSID 与 MAC 地址过滤
k: Turning off the SSID broadcast hides the network name so it cannot be automatically searched by other devices. With MAC address filtering, the access point only allows devices with MAC addresses on the whitelist to use the Wi-Fi network.
As anyone can connect to public networks, hackers may intrude into them and monitor the incoming and outgoing information.
Disable the 'Pop-ups and redirects' feature. Enable the automatic update function of the web browser to ensure software vulnerabilities are duly removed.

Eavesdropping refers to the unauthorised interception and monitoring of the content of other people's private communications without consent. It is difficult to detect whether the data has been intercepted. Use encryption so that intercepted data cannot be read.

Hacking refers to hackers' behaviour of using different methods to attack and destroy network security. Data and files stored in the computer may be stolen or destroyed; the content of a website may be changed; the computer may become a zombie computer and launch a denial-of-service attack.

Social engineering refers to a scammer's behaviour of manipulating the trust between people or the victim's greed to trick the victims into disclosing confidential personal information. It is also a common method of spreading malware.

Baiting: scammers exploit the victim's curiosity, e.g. leaving USB drives containing malware in public places. Quid pro quo: scammers claim to provide services or goods and ask the victim to disclose personal information in exchange.
Catfishing: scammers use others' photos and personal information to create fake social media accounts and ask for money. Pretexting: scammers pretend to be someone else to gain the victim's trust.
Phishing refers to scammers' behaviour of forging official websites and sending messages to deceive victims into visiting fake websites and entering personal information.
Spamming of electronic messages refers to the behaviour of sending a large number of redundant messages through SMS or emails without the recipient's consent.
Disclosure of too much personal information on the Internet, such as phone numbers and addresses, may lead to identity theft.

Many online system registrations require users to provide personal information that has nothing to do with the nature of the service. Personal information may be accessed or transferred to a third party for commercial purposes, or even leaked.
Clear browsing history and cookies; turn off the autofill function; use private browsing; use a proxy server to hide the IP address.

When a user browses a website, the website generates a cookie to store information on the device to record the user's operations, such as user preferences, browsing behaviour and login authentication results. Third-party cookies track user activity across websites.
Private browsing does not leave browsing history, cookies and input data on the device, but it does not hide the IP address. Turn off autofill on public computers.

A proxy server establishes an intermediate connection point between the user and the website, hiding the user's IP address. The website can only record the IP address of the proxy server. Unlike a VPN, the connection is not encrypted. A proxy can also filter web pages and use a buffer to load pages faster.
Use at least 8 characters with a mixed combination of numbers, uppercase letters, lowercase letters and special characters; do not use personal information, simple passwords or common words.
Change passwords regularly (at least once every three months); do not use the same password on different systems; do not record, send or share passwords.
Do not open attachments or hyperlinks in suspicious emails. Scan attachments, especially those with extensions such as .exe, .vbs and .bat, with antivirus software before opening.
Read the privacy policy to check the purpose of collection, whether the data is necessary and whether it will be transferred to third parties; provide only the minimum personal information needed.

items.t: HK laws: Telecommunications Ordinance & Crimes Ordinance
items.tz: 香港法例：电讯条例与刑事罪行条例
k: Telecommunications Ordinance Section 27A: unauthorised access to computer by telecommunications. Crimes Ordinance Section 60: destroying or damaging property (including data). Section 161: access to computers with criminal or dishonest intent, maximum imprisonment 5 years.

items.tz: 香港法例：私隐条例与非应邀电子讯息条例
k: The PDPO lists six data protection principles; personal data must not be used for purposes other than the original purpose without consent. The UEMO allows recipients to refuse commercial electronic messages.

mc.q: When a virus is spread through a Bluetooth connection, which of the following applications installed on a notebook computer can prevent the infection?
mc.e: A firewall can block unauthorised incoming connections; email clients and browsers don't.

mc.q:
When Peter tries to change the password of his computer account, the following screen is shown.
Change password
Current password: ____
New password: ____
Re-enter new password: ____
[Save] [Cancel]
What is/are the use(s) of ‘Current password’?
st: (3) It prevents other people from changing the password.
mc.e: Asking for the current password proves it's the owner; re-entering the new one is what catches typos.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the best practice when using online banking systems?
st: (2) Use a combination of letters and numbers for the passwords and change them regularly.
(3) Avoid using wired network when wireless network is available.
mc.e: Hard-to-guess login names and strong, changed passwords help; wireless is less secure than wired.

mc.q: John does not download patches to upgrade the operating system of his computer. Which of the following statements best describes the possible consequences?
o: The license of the operating system will soon expire and he will have to re-install it.
The operating system may be more vulnerable to attacks by hackers.
The computer cannot connect to the Internet.
The IP address of the computer may need to be changed.
mc.e: Patches fix security holes; without them the OS is easier to attack.

mc.q: In an office network, a technician installs a firewall instead of antivirus software. What is the major reason for this?
o: The computers in the office can be protected from adware.
The network can be protected from online security threats.
File transfer through the network can be faster.
The network can withstand virus attacks.
mc.e: A firewall guards the network against outside intrusions, not viruses in files.

mc.q: Mary receives an anonymous email, saying that the attached file photos.exe includes some photos of Mary. She tries to execute the file but no photos are displayed. What is/are the possible reason(s)?
st: (1) Photo editing software has not been installed in Mary's computer.
(2) The file contains malicious code that harms Mary's computer.
(3) The email server cannot execute the file.
mc.e: An anonymous .exe pretending to be photos is likely malware (a Trojan).

mc.q: Which of the following statements about phishing email is/are correct?
st: (1) Phishing email is a type of advertisement that a company sends out to target recipients.
(2) Phishing email is typically carried out by sending target recipients an email with a fake web site to acquire their personal information.
(3) Target recipients will not be able to use their computers for a few days after a phishing attack.
mc.e: Phishing tricks users into giving personal data through fake sites.

mc.q:
Cathy receives an anonymous email about changing the password of her online banking account, as shown below. She clicks the hyperlink in the email and a malicious web site is displayed.

Kowloon Bank
Your password has expired. Please click the following link to update your password.
https://KLNbanks.ru

Which of the following security issues is/are mainly involved in the instance?
mc.e: A fake bank email leading to a fake site is phishing; the malicious site may also intrude into her computer.

mc.q: Which of the following actions can help Cathy ensure that she is browsing a trusted web site?
o: Ensure that the domain name does not contain '.ru'.
Verify the digital certificates of the web site.
Follow hyperlinks in emails sent by friends instead of anonymously.
Enable a firewall before browsing the Internet.
mc.e: A valid digital certificate confirms the site's identity.

mc.q: Ransomware is malware that encrypts victims' computer files and demands a ransom payment to restore them. How can we minimise the impact of ransomware?
st: (1) Creates backups of computer files regularly.
(2) Do not open anonymous or phishing email.
(3) Do not download pirated copies of computer software through p2p software.
mc.e: Backups let you restore files; avoiding phishing mail and pirated software avoids infection.

mc.q:
ABC Coffee Shop offers free WiFi for customers. The details are:
ABC Coffee Shop
- A 30-minute session of free WiFi service
- SSID: abc; Password: YW$1818abc
- Unencrypted connection
- 128 Kbps maximum bandwidth
Customers should not use the WiFi connection for online banking because
o: the free session is too short.
the SSID is too short and easily guessed.
the data passing through the connection is not encrypted.
the maximum bandwidth is still too low.
mc.e: Unencrypted traffic can be sniffed by others on the network.

mc.q: Ms Li finds that the file server in her company is infected by ransomware. Some important document files have been encrypted and cannot be opened. What should she do?
st: (1) Try to put the encrypted files in another file server and open them.
(2) Report the incident to the police.
(3) Pay the ransom to acquire the password.
mc.e: Report it; moving files does not decrypt them and paying is not advised.

mc.q: In a computer network, which of the following can protect a user's privacy from a hacker attack?
mc.e: OS updates patch holes and a firewall blocks intrusions; backups do not stop data being stolen.

mc.q: Peter just finds that he cannot open some important files in a computer in his office due to a ransomware attack. What should he do immediately?
mc.e: Disconnect first so the ransomware cannot spread to other computers on the network.

mc.q: How can updating an operating system frequently protect computers from virus attacks?
o: More support from the developer of the operating system can be provided.
The computer performance can be enhanced.
A virus check can be conducted.
mc.e: Updates patch security holes that viruses use.

mc.q: Which malware attaches itself to executable files and activates when the file is run?
mc.e: A virus needs a host file and is activated when the host is executed.
mc.ez: Virus 依附宿主文件，执行时启动。

mc.q: Which malware can spread through a network by itself without a host file?
mc.e: Worms self-replicate and spread over networks automatically.

mc.q: Which statement about Trojan programs is correct?
mc.e: Trojans lure users by looking useful; they do not self-replicate.

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a Trojan program?
o: It can self-replicate to all contacts
mc.e: Self-replication to contacts describes a worm.
mc.ez: 自我复制是 worm 特征。

mc.q: The main purpose of spyware is to
mc.e: Spyware collects data such as keystrokes and passwords while hiding.

mc.q: A keylogger that records every keystroke is a type of
mc.e: Recording keyboard input to steal data is spyware.

mc.q: Which malware profits mainly from displaying advertisements?
mc.e: Adware shows pop-ups/banners for profit.

mc.q: Files on a PC are encrypted and a message demands Bitcoin for the key. This is
mc.e: Ransomware encrypts files and demands ransom.

mc.q: Which is the BEST action after a ransomware infection?
o: Disconnect from the network, report to police and restore from backup
Copy the encrypted files to another PC and open them
mc.e: Do not pay; isolate, report and restore from backup.

mc.q: Which measure best reduces the damage of ransomware?
mc.e: Backups let you restore without paying.

mc.q: Which is NOT a common way for malware to spread according to the textbook?
o: Client-side scripts in dynamic web pages
mc.e: The four channels are scripts, email/IM, freeware/shareware and storage devices.
mc.ez: 调高解像度不是传播途径。

mc.q: Why did worms spread fast through emails from friends?
o: Emails from known contacts lower the recipients' alertness
mc.e: Victims trust messages from contacts.

mc.q: A hacker secretly relays and alters messages between a user and a bank website. This is
mc.e: MITM intercepts/tampers between two parties.

mc.q: An attacker sets up a free Wi-Fi called 'Airport_Free' to monitor victims' traffic. This is an example of
mc.e: Evil twin = fake hotspot used for MITM/eavesdropping.

mc.q: The aim of a DoS attack is to
o: make the target server unable to provide services
mc.e: DoS exhausts resources so users cannot get service.

mc.q: In a DDoS attack, the computers used to send requests are called
mc.e: Hacked computers remotely controlled = zombies.

mc.q: Why is a DDoS attack harder to block than a DoS attack from one computer?
o: Traffic comes from many different IP addresses
mc.e: Blocking one IP is not enough.

mc.q: How does antivirus software identify known malware?
o: By comparing files with virus signatures
mc.e: Signatures act like fingerprints.

mc.q: Why should antivirus automatic update be enabled?
o: To recognise the latest malware signatures
mc.e: New malware requires new signatures.

mc.q: Which information does a firewall check in data packets?
mc.e: Rules are based on IP, port, type etc.

k: Encryption is a process of transforming data into an unreadable form with a key, to ensure data privacy in case the data is hacked or accessed illegally. It does not prevent interception, but prevents the readable content from being interpreted. Decryption is the reverse process using the corresponding key.
The sender uses an encryption key to convert the plaintext into ciphertext; the recipient uses a decryption key to convert the ciphertext back into plaintext.
A longer key has more possible key combinations, so a hacker needs more time to try every combination (brute force); but a longer key needs more computation time to encrypt and decrypt.

Private key encryption uses the same key for encryption and decryption. The key must be exchanged securely beforehand. Problems: difficult to transfer the key securely, and difficult to manage keys when there are many users.

items.tz: 公开密码匙（不对称）加密
k: Public key encryption uses a pair of keys: a public key available to everyone and a private key kept confidential by the owner. A message encrypted with either key can only be decrypted by the other key of the pair.

In encryption mode, the sender encrypts with the recipient's public key so only the recipient can decrypt with his private key. In authentication mode, the sender encrypts with his own private key; since only the sender has it, successful decryption with the sender's public key verifies the sender's identity. This is the basis of digital signatures.

items.t: Which key does the sender use? (Activity 6.2 drill)
items.tz: 发送者用哪把钥匙？（活动 6.2 练习）
k: The sender encrypts the message with the recipient's public key, so only the recipient can decrypt it with his own private key, which prevents eavesdropping and interception.

items.t: Public Key Infrastructure and Certification Authority
items.tz: 公开密码匙基础建设与核证机关
k: A CA acts as a publicly trusted third party to issue and manage digital certificates. A digital certificate verifies that an individual or organisation owns a particular public key.

The sender encrypts the message using the recipient's public key and signs it using his own private key; the recipient verifies using the sender's public key and decrypts using his own private key. This achieves privacy, authentication, integrity and non-repudiation.
Authentication is a security measure used to verify the user's identity. Username and password is convenient and cheap, but the strength of the password affects the degree of security.
A token generates a one-time password which can only be used once and becomes invalid after a short time, protecting users from password guessing attacks.
A smart card is a hard token whose chip stores encrypted information or the private key of the card holder.
Biometrics identifies a person relying on the unique physical attributes of human beings, e.g. fingerprint, iris, retina, face and voice.

items.t: Digital certificates for authentication and iAM Smart
items.tz: 数码证书认证与智方便
k: A digital certificate issued by a recognised CA binds a public key to a verified identity, so the online service can trust that the user is genuine.

Two-factor authentication is the combined use of two different authentication factors to verify user identity. Although hackers may steal a user's password via the Internet, it is very difficult for them to steal something you hold via the Internet.

items.t: SSL / TLS encryption in online transactions
items.tz: 网上交易的 SSL/TLS 加密
k: SSL/TLS establishes an authenticated and encrypted communication link between clients and servers using public key encryption, so data such as credit card numbers can be transmitted safely via HTTPS.

items.t: Digital certificate and digital signature in transactions
items.tz: 交易中的数码证书与数码签署
k: A digital signature is created using the sender's private key and verified with the sender's public key; it ensures authentication, integrity and non-repudiation. An electronic signature is any signature in electronic form and is not necessarily a digital signature.

items.t: 2FA in online transactions: token, SMS OTP, QR code
k: The bank sends a one-time password to the user's registered mobile phone; it can be used only once and expires after a short time. The uniqueness of the SIM card enables the phone to act as a security token.
Multi-factor authentication verifies a user with two or more different factors (something you know, hold and are); the more factors verified, the higher the degree of authentication.
AI systems analyse the user's login pattern (location, time, IP address); if irregularities are found, a stronger authentication mechanism than usual is applied.
Bitcoin uses a decentralised peer-to-peer network; each user keeps a distributed ledger of all transactions, which are verified by miners and cannot be tampered with.

mc.q: Which of the following can enhance the security of online banking?
mc.e: Security tokens add a second authentication factor.

mc.q: Which of the following functions is provided by a typical Internet browser?
o: Block unauthorised access to the computer.
Support the Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) in online transactions.
mc.e: Browsers support SSL/HTTPS; blocking access and virus protection are firewall/antivirus jobs.

mc.q: A bank has a secure room which only a few staff members can enter. Which of the following security measures is the most secure one for controlling access?
mc.e: A fingerprint (biometric) can't be lent, lost or guessed.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are security measure(s) an online bank can use to authenticate customers' identities?
mc.e: A security token proves the customer's identity; the others don't authenticate users.

mc.q: Which of the following may have security risks?
st: (1) Using a public computer in a coffee shop to log on to an online bank
(2) Using the Wi-Fi network provided by a shopping centre to check email
(3) Using a public computer to check the digital certificate of a web site
mc.e: Logging in on a public computer or public Wi-Fi exposes credentials; just checking a certificate sends no secrets.

mc.q: Why do we need Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) on the Internet?
o: An IP address includes at least four values.
The socket for power supply can be protected.
mc.e: SSL encrypts data in transit.

mc.q: What is/are the major benefit(s) of using data encryption for transferring confidential information over the Internet?
st: (1) Hackers cannot collect the encrypted data easily.
(2) Hackers cannot read the confidential information easily.
(3) Hackers cannot delete the confidential information easily.
mc.e: Encryption stops data being read, not intercepted or deleted.

mc.q: When Eva logs on to a web site, she will receive an SMS message on her phone with a password. What is the SMS message about?
mc.e: A one-time password by SMS is two-factor authentication.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the common measures for online systems to authenticate user identities?
mc.e: Security tokens prove who the user is. DNS resolves names and firewalls filter traffic; neither authenticates users.

mc.q: Which of the following programs can enhance the security of using a computer?
mc.e: Firewalls and encryption protect the computer. Adware shows ads and can be a risk.

mc.q: What is/are the advantage(s) of using Secure Socket Layer (SSL) on web sites?
st: The data transfer rate is higher.
The IP addresses of the web sites can be hidden.
mc.e: SSL encrypts data. It does not speed things up or hide IP addresses.

mc.q: A web site adopts an encryption key 2048 bits long instead of 1024 bits long. Why does this increase the security level?
o: Hackers take more time to crack the system.
The time for data transmission increases.
It is more difficult to memorise the key.
The size of an encrypted data packet increases.
mc.e: A longer key means far more possible keys, so brute force takes much longer.

mc.q: What is the main purpose of encryption?
o: Ensure data privacy if data is accessed illegally
mc.e: Encryption keeps content private; it does not stop interception.
mc.ez: 加密保障私隐，不阻止截取。

mc.q: Which is TRUE after a message is encrypted?
mc.e: Only reading is prevented.

mc.q: The original readable message is called
mc.e: Plaintext = 明文.

mc.q: Decryption converts
mc.e: Reverse of encryption.

mc.q: Caesar cipher shift 3: encrypt 'CAT'.
mc.e: C→F, A→D, T→W.

mc.q: Caesar cipher shift 3: decrypt 'LFW'.
mc.e: Shift back 3.

mc.q: How many combinations does a 24-bit key have?
mc.e: n-bit → 2^n.

mc.q: A computer tries 1024 keys per second. Maximum time to crack a 20-bit key?
Why is a longer key more secure?
o: Hackers need more time to try all keys
Data takes more time to transmit
mc.e: More combinations → longer brute force.

mc.q: A drawback of a longer encryption key is
o: it cannot be used in HTTPS
mc.e: Trade-off is computation time.

mc.q: Symmetric key encryption uses
o: one key for encryption and the same key for decryption
a public and a private key
mc.e: Same key both ways.

mc.q: A major problem of private key encryption is
o: the key must be transferred securely
mc.e: Key distribution problem.

mc.q: 20 users each need a unique symmetric key with every other user. Number of keys?
In public key encryption, the private key should be
mc.e: Private key is confidential.

mc.q: A message encrypted with Bob's public key can be decrypted by
mc.e: The other key of the pair.

mc.q: Amy wants only Bob to read her message. She encrypts with
mc.e: Encryption mode uses recipient's public key.

mc.q: To prove a notice really came from the school, the school encrypts it with
mc.e: Authentication mode / signature.

mc.q: Which mode is the basis of digital signatures?
mc.e: Signing with private key.

mc.q: A student sends credit card details to a merchant. Which key should encrypt them?
mc.e: Confidentiality → merchant's public key.

mc.q: A parent digitally signs a reply slip to the school using
mc.e: Signature uses sender's private key.

mc.q:
Dry run the following algorithm on the array AR.
cnt ← 1
ind ← 1
while cnt < 100
   cnt ← cnt + 2
   AR[ind] ← cnt
   ind ← ind + 1
What is the value of AR[5]?

Dry run the following algorithm.
X ← 1
Y ← 20
while X < Y
   output 'A'
   X ← X + 2
   Y ← Y - 2
How many character 'A's are displayed?

The following two pseudo code segments are used for searching.
S1S2
J ← 1
while J <= 10000
   if st = N[J]
      Found ← J
   J ← J + 1
Flag ← 0
J ← 1
while J <= 10000 and Flag = 0
   if st = N[J]
      Found ← J
      Flag ← 1
   J ← J + 1
When comparing the execution times of the two segments, which of the following statements is correct?
o: They are more or less the same.
mc.e: S2 stops as soon as the item is found; S1 always checks all 10000.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?
X ← 5
Y ← 9
If (X+Y < 15) or (X-Y < X+Y)
   then Y ← Y-X
   else X ← Y-X
Output X, Y
mc.e: 14 < 15 is true, so Y = 9 − 5 = 4; X stays 5.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?
S ← 5
C ← 0
While S ≤ 10
   C ← C + 1
   S ← S + C
Output C
mc.e: S: 5→6→8→11; C ends at 3.

mc.q:
An array DAT stores English names as shown below.
AmyBobCarolDave
DAT[1]DAT[2]DAT[3]DAT[4]
After executing the following algorithm, which element in DAT stores 'Carol'? P ← 4 While P > 2 DAT[P] ← DAT[P-1] P ← P - 1
mc.e: P=4: DAT[4]←Carol; P=3: DAT[3]←Bob. Carol is in DAT[4].

mc.q:
Consider the algorithm below.

A ← 1
While A < 10
    A ← A + A
    Output A

Which of the following values is/are included in the output?
mc.e: A doubles: outputs 2, 4, 8, 16 (16 is output before the test fails).

mc.q: Which of the following pseudocodes produce the same result?
st:
(1) IF P < 3 AND Q > 25 THEN
    R ← R + 1

(2) IF Q > 25 THEN
    IF P < 3 THEN
        R ← R + 1

(3) IF P < 3 THEN
    IF Q > 25 THEN
        R ← R + 1
mc.e: Nested IFs in either order equal one IF with AND.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following algorithm?

S ← 0
For J from 1 to 5
    Output J
    S ← S + J
Output S
mc.e: Outputs 1 2 3 4 5, then S = 15.

mc.q:
NUM is an integer array. What is the output of the following algorithm?

K ← 0
While K <= 100 do
    NUM[K] ← K × K
    K ← K + 1
Output (NUM[3] + NUM[4])

Study the following statement:

If NOT ( X > 30 OR ( Y AND Z ) )
    Then output '***'

For which of the following combinations of the values X, Y and Z will '***' be displayed?
mc.e: Need X ≤ 30 and (Y AND Z) false: only X = 30, FALSE, FALSE.

mc.q:
A is an array with A[1], A[2], ..., A[N] storing N non-zero values. What is the purpose of the following algorithm?

Input P
K ← P
While K <= N-1 do

     THEN  A ← B
     ELSE  B ← A

mc.q:
The following algorithm shows how a vending machine works:
Step 1: Wait to receive a coin.
Step 2: If the coin is not $1, $2, $5 or $10, eject it.
Step 3: If $6 or more is deposited, do steps 4 and 5.
Step 4:     Release a can of lemon tea.
Step 5:     Reduce the deposit by $6.
Step 6: Eject the deposit.
Step 7: Do step 1.
Which of the following statements about the algorithm is true?
o: A can of lemon tea will cost less than $6.
The vending machine will release lemon tea.
A can of lemon tea will cost more than $6.
The vending machine will release lemon tea only if a $10 coin is received.
mc.e: Step 6 ejects the deposit after EVERY coin, so the deposit never builds up. Only a single $10 coin reaches $6.

mc.q: The sales department of an insurance company wants to improve service to its clients. It asks the IT project manager to establish some web pages for the clients. What should the IT project manager do first?
o: Define the scope of the service.
Set up a project team and recruit programmers.
mc.e: The first stage is defining the problem/scope.

mc.q:
What is the output of the following Python program?
list = [10, 23, 55]
print(list[2])
mc.e: Indices start at 0, so list[2] is the third item, 55.
mc.ez: 索引由 0 开始，list[2] 是第三项 55。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q1 (p.154)

mc.q:
Study the program:
list = [0] * 2
list[0] = "0"
list[1] = "integer"
What are the data types of list[0] and list[1] respectively?
mc.e: Both values are in quotation marks, so both are strings.
mc.ez: 两个值都有引号，都是字符串。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q2 (p.154)

mc.q:
A program records weights until -1 is entered:
list = []
weight = float(input())
__________
    list = list + [weight]
    weight = float(input())
print(list)
Which option fills the blank?
mc.e: A loop is needed that continues while the input is not the sentinel -1.
mc.ez: 需要循环，在输入不是 -1 时继续。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q3 (p.154)

mc.q:
A program calculates the average height:
list2 = []
i = 0
total = 0
height = float(input())
while height != -1:
    list2 = list2 + [height]
    __________
    height = float(input())
print("The mean is", total/i)
Which option fills the blank?
mc.e: Both the total and the counter i (number of heights) must be updated, because the mean is total/i.
mc.ez: 平均 = total/i，所以总和和计数 i 都要更新。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q4 (p.155)

mc.q: A program searches for target in num = [2, 4, 6, 7, 10] and sets found. Which code fills the blank?
o:
for i in range(0, 5):
  if num[i] == target: found = True

for i in range(0, 4):
  if num[i] == target: found = True
mc.e: Each item must be compared; num has 5 items (indices 0 to 4), so range(0, 5). range(0, 4) misses 10.
mc.ez: 列表有 5 项，要用 range(0, 5)，否则漏掉最后一项。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q5 (p.155)

mc.q: In a while-loop search of a 100000-item list, while i < 100000 and flag == False:, what is the purpose of flag?
o: To check if there is input or not
To stop the Python program immediately
To stop the iteration once the target is found
mc.e: When flag becomes True the loop condition fails, so searching stops early.
mc.ez: 找到后 flag 变 True，循环立即停止，节省时间。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q6 (p.155)

mc.q:
Which fills the blank to find the lowest score?
score = [9, 5, 3, 7, 8]
lowest = score[0]
for i in range(1, 5):
    ________
print("The lowest is", lowest)
mc.e: Replace lowest only when a smaller item is found.
mc.ez: 遇到更小的值才更新 lowest。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q7 (p.155)

mc.q:
An algorithm deletes a record by index:
X = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
index = int(input())
for i in range(index, len(X)-1):
    X[i] = X[i + 1]
X[5] = 0
What should the user input to delete the record "4"?
mc.e: The value 4 is stored at index 3.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q8 (p.156)

mc.q:
If the input is 4, what is the output?
X = [1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7]
i = 0
num = int(input())
while num > X[i]:
    i = i + 1
X = X + [0]
for j in range(len(X)-1, i, -1):
    X[j] = X[j - 1]
X[i] = num
print(X)
mc.e: The while loop finds i = 3 (first item greater than or equal to 4); items shift backward and 4 is inserted at index 3.
mc.ez: 找到插入位置 3，后移并插入 4。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q9 (p.156)

mc.q: d = "Hello_world", y = "", loop for i in range(0, 5): [blank], print(y). The output is Hello. Which fills the blank?
mc.e: Characters d[0] to d[4] are joined: H, e, l, l, o.
mc.ez: 把 d[0] 到 d[4] 逐个接上。
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch5 Chapter Exercise MC Q10 (p.156)

mc.q:
What is the output?
a = [0]*4
a[1] = 7
a[3] = a[1] + 2
print(a)
mc.e: a[1]=7 and a[3]=7+2=9; others stay 0.

mc.q: Which statement creates a list of 6 empty strings?
mc.e: [value]*n repeats the item n times inside a list.
mc.ez: [值]*n 在列表中重复 n 次。

mc.q: A list has 25 items. What is the index of its last item?
mc.e: Last index = N - 1 = 24.

mc.q: Which code causes an IndexError?
mc.e: [0]*5 has indices 0 to 4 only; a[5] is out of range.

mc.q: Why must a list be initialised before for i in range(0, 5): marks[i] = 0?
o: Python needs the data type declared
Items that do not exist cannot be accessed by index
mc.e: Assignment by index only works on existing items; an empty or undefined list has no index i.
mc.ez: 只能对已存在的项目用索引赋值。

mc.q:
What is the output?
list2 = [34, 23, 90, 56, 100]
list2[1] = list2[2] - 5
print(list2[1] + list2[0])
What sequence does range(2, -1, -1) produce?
mc.e: Start 2, step -1, stop before -1.
mc.ez: 由 2 开始，到 -1 之前停止。

mc.e: Prints indices 0, 1, 2 in order on one line.

o: When i = 6, num[i+1] (num[7]) is out of range
mc.e: The list has indices 0 to 6; num[7] does not exist.
mc.ez: i=6 时 num[7] 超出范围。

mc.q:
What is the output?
num = [10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40]
for i in range(0, 6):
    num[i] = num[i] + 5
print(num[5], num[6])
mc.e: Indices 0 to 5 increase by 5 (num[5] 35→40); num[6] stays 40.

mc.q: In memory, an array arr has base address 3046. What is the address of arr[4]?
mc.e: Address = base + index = 3046 + 4 = 3050.
mc.ez: 地址 = 起始地址 + 索引。

mc.q: Why do array indices start from 0?
o: The index is the distance from the first item's address, which is 0 for the first item
mc.e: Address of item = base address + index, so the first item has offset 0.
mc.ez: 索引表示与第一项的距离。

mc.q:
What is the output?
a = [3, 6, 9]
b = [0]*3
for i in range(0, 3):
    b[i] = a[2-i]
print(b)
mc.e: b copies a in reverse order.
item[0] is the first character of each name.
mc.ez: 每个名字的第一个字符。

mc.q:
What is the output?
x = []
x = x + [5]
x = x + [8]
x.append(1)
print(len(x), x[2])
mc.e: x becomes [5, 8, 1]; length 3, x[2] = 1.

mc.q:
What is the output?
time = [15.1, 14.9, 15.6, 16.1]
total = 0
for i in range(0, len(time)):
    total = total + time[i]
print(round(total/len(time), 3))
Why is N = len(time) better than writing 8 in range(0, 8)?
o: The same program works for lists of any length
mc.e: The loop bound adapts to the list, so it need not be rewritten for other distances.
mc.ez: 程序适用于任何长度的列表。

mc.e: 9 is in the list.

mc.q:
What is the output?
the_list = [4, 9, 2, 9, 7]
index = -1
i = 0
while i < len(the_list) and index == -1:
    if the_list[i] == 9:
        index = i
    i = i + 1
print(index, i)
mc.e: Found at index 1, i incremented to 2, then loop stops.
mc.ez: 在索引 1 找到，i 变 2 后停止。

mc.e: A for loop without stopping keeps overwriting, so the LAST match (index 3) is kept.
mc.ez: for 循环会记下最后一个匹配。
