mc.q: In an IT project, Tom has written the source code. He tests it with valid input data items. What should he do next?
o: Check the modularity of the program design.
Continue to test the program with invalid data items.
mc.e: Testing should cover invalid (and boundary) data too, before documentation.

mc.q:
In the following algorithm, what input value of B will generate a run-time error?
input B
A ← 2
C ← 2
D ← square root of (B × B - 4 × A × C)
output D
mc.e: B = 2: 4 − 16 = −12, square root of a negative number → run-time error.

mc.q: What is the major advantage of using an array in algorithm design?
o: The modular approach can be used in the design.
It is useful in iteration design.
The size of an array is flexible.
mc.e: Indexed elements can be processed with a loop variable.

mc.q:
The following pseudocode represents part of an algorithm.

IF (AGE > 6) AND (AGE < 12) THEN
    OUTPUT AGE

Which of the following sets of test data is the most approriate?
mc.e: A covers a value below, both boundaries (6, 12), a valid value inside, and a value far above.

mc.q: When solving a problem in a project, Mary needs to define the scope of the problem precisely. What is/are the major reason(s) for doing this?
st: (1) She can break down the problem into sub-problems effectively.
(2) She can use a truth table to illustrate the solution.
(3) She can ignore the boundary cases when testing the algorithm.
mc.e: A clear scope makes decomposition easier; boundary cases must still be tested.

mc.q:
The problem-solving procedures for developing a computer system are listed below. What is the correct order of the procedures?

(1) Tests the system.
(2) Defines the problem.
(3) Designs the algorithm.
(4) Writes the program codes.
mc.e: Define → design → code → test.

mc.q:
Study the following algorithm:
INPUT n
IF n < -6 THEN
   y ← y + 2
ELSE  IF   n > 9  THEN
           y ← y - 2
      ELSE y ← y x 2
Which of the following sets of input data is most suitable for testing the algorithm?
mc.e: It covers all three branches plus both boundary values -6 and 9.

mc.q: What are the characteristics of using modularity for designing computer solutions?
st: (1) Usually modularity is used to solve simple problems.
mc.e: Modules can be reused and developed independently; modularity suits complex problems and lowers cost.

mc.q:
What are the boundary cases for testing in the following segment of an algorithm?
Input A
If A > 5
   Then B ← 10
   Else B ← 20
Output A, B
mc.e: The condition A > 5 changes between 5 and 6.

mc.q:
A bank updates its automatic teller machine system with new restrictions on cash withdrawals, as follows:
• Available cash notes $100, $500 and $1 000
• Minimum withdrawal amount = $200
• Maximum withdrawal amount = $10 000
Which of the following sets of withdrawal amounts should be used as test data for this system update?
mc.e: It tests both boundaries (100/200, 10 000/11 000) and a non-multiple of 100 (950).

mc.q: After writing the source code of a program, which of the following should be done according to the problem-solving procedures?
st: Outline the input and output requirements of the problem.
Test the program with boundary cases.
Define the scope of the problem.
mc.e: (1) and (3) belong to problem definition/analysis, BEFORE coding. Testing comes after.

mc.q: What is the importance of a problem definition in problem-solving?
o: The design and the scope of work can be set.
There is no need to define sub-problems.
An error-free algorithm will be developed.
mc.e: Defining the problem sets the scope of the work. It never removes later steps or guarantees no errors.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the advantage(s) of modularity in programming?
st: It is easier to trace a program.
It facilitates programming through team work.
mc.e: Modules are easier to trace and can be shared among a team. Users never see the modules, so the manual is not affected.

mc.q: Why should appropriate test data be prepared?
st: To test whether exceptional input data can be handled
To verify expected results from given input data
mc.e: Test data finds errors, checks exceptional cases and compares output with expected results: all three.

mc.q:
Consider the following pseudocode for checking a normal school exam result:
IF (MARKS >= 50) THEN
     OUTPUT 'PASS'
ELSE
     OUTPUT 'FAIL'
Which of the following sets of test values is appropriate?
mc.e: Good test data covers both outcomes and the boundary: 99 (pass), 0 (fail) and 50 (boundary).

mc.q: Which of the following are advantages of using the modular approach when designing algorithms?
st: A module can be reused in other scenarios.
The execution time of an algorithm is shorter.
The modules are easier to design and test.
mc.e: Modules are reusable and easier to design and test. They do not make the program run faster.

mc.q: What kind of information is stated in the user manual of a software package?
mc.e: User manuals tell users system requirements, installation and usage; the others are technical documentation.

mc.q: Which of the following sequences of tasks in problem solving procedures is correct?
st: Outline the input and output requirements of the problem.
Define the scope of the problem.
Evaluate the output of the solution to the problem.
mc.e: Define the problem, then I/O, then test/debug, then evaluate.

mc.q: Anson has finished designing an algorithm and tested it with some valid data items. What should he do next?
o: Draw the flowchart for the algorithm.
Improve the algorithm with modularized design.
Continue to test the algorithm with invalid data items.
mc.e: Testing must also include erroneous (invalid) data.

mc.q:
Refer to the algorithm:
Input second
if second < 0 or second > 59 then
    Output "Error"
Which set of test data is the most appropriate?
mc.e: It has erroneous values on both sides (-2, 60), both boundaries (0, 59) and a normal value.
mc.ez: 两边错误值、两个边界和正常值都有。

mc.q: A digital wallet allows transfers from $1 to $3000. Which set of amounts should be used as test data?
mc.e: Includes invalid 0 and 4000, boundaries 1 and 3000, and normal values.
mc.ez: 包含无效值、边界值 1 和 3000 及正常值。

mc.q: Algorithm: if X > 50 then Y ← 100 else Y ← 0. Which are the boundary cases? (1) 0 (2) 50 (3) 51 (4) 100
mc.e: The dividing value is 50; 50 and 51 sit either side of it.
mc.ez: 分界值是 50，所以 50 和 51 是边界。

mc.q: Algorithm: if op > 5 'Should be smaller'; else if op < -5 'Should be larger'; else 'OK'. Most appropriate test data?
mc.e: Covers all three branches and both boundaries.
mc.ez: 覆盖三个分支和两个边界。

mc.q: Slope algorithm: Y2←4, Y1←2, X1←1, Output (Y2-Y1)/(X2-X1). Which input X2 gives a run-time error?
mc.e: X2 = 1 makes X2 - X1 = 0: division by zero.

mc.q: A flowchart finds the smallest of three inputs with min ← 0 initially and min ← N whenever N < min. Which set cannot output the correct result?
mc.e: No positive number is below 0, so 0 is output instead of 2.
mc.ez: 都不小于 0，输出 0 而不是 2。

mc.q: Following the previous question, which logic error prevents the correct result?
o: The initial value of min is 0.
The initial value of c is 1.
mc.e: min should start as the first input (or a very large value).
mc.ez: min 应以第一个输入为初值。

mc.q: Algorithm 1 checks all 100 pairs with a for loop; Algorithm 2 uses while i <= 100 AND sorted_list = True. Which is correct about execution times?
mc.e: Algorithm 2 stops at the first unsorted pair.
mc.ez: 算法2 一发现未排序就停止。

mc.q: BMI Algorithm 1 uses single conditions (bmi < 18.5, < 23, < 25); Algorithm 2 uses compound ones (0 < bmi AND bmi < 18.5, 18.5 <= bmi AND bmi < 23 ...). Steps of operation?
mc.e: Algorithm 2 makes two comparisons per condition; the lower checks are redundant in an else-if chain.
mc.ez: 算法2 每个条件比较两次，多余。

mc.q: Algorithm 1: if A == 0 and B == 0. Algorithm 2: nested if A == 0: if B == 0. Steps of operation?
mc.e: Short-circuit 'and' evaluates B only when A == 0, just like the nested version.
mc.ez: and 短路求值，与嵌套一样。

mc.q: A programmer has written a program to calculate the profit of a shop. What should he do next?
o: Draw a flowchart to explain the program.
Use different sets of data to test for any possible errors.
Submit the program directly to the shop.
mc.e: After writing comes testing.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q1 (p.196)

mc.q: Boundary cases for: if Y < 3 'less'; if Y >= 3 and Y <= 6 'between'; if Y > 6 'more'.
mc.e: The dividing values are 3 and 6.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q2 (p.196)

mc.q: Algorithm: if X > 5 Output A; if X < 5 Output B; else Output C. Suitable test set?
mc.e: 1 gives B, 5 gives C, 6 gives A: every output is tested.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q3 (p.196)

Which line contains a syntax error?
1 name = input("name:")
2 age = "17"
3 print(name, is, age)

Which line contains a logic error?

2 if score >= 50 or score < 50:
3     print("Pass")
4 else:
5     print("Fail")
mc.e: The condition is always True, so everyone passes.

mc.q: A = 5, then a missing statement, then Output B. Which statement contains a run-time error?
mc.e: Division by zero.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q6 (p.197)

mc.q:
What error(s) does this contain?
import math
A = int("10")
B = 2
C = math.sqrt(-A + B)
mc.e: sqrt(-8) raises ValueError at run time.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q7 (p.197)

mc.q: word = input(input word:) contains a syntax error. Replace it with:
mc.e: The prompt must be a string literal.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q8 (p.197)

mc.q:
Average of five inputs:
total = 0
N = 4
for i in range(1, 6):
    num = int(input("Num: "))
    total = total + num
print(total / N)
Replace the last line with:
mc.e: Five numbers are read, so divide by 5.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q9 (p.198)

mc.q: Sum of five inputs: lines 3-6 read num[0..4]; line 7 for j in range(1, 5):; line 8 total = total + num[j]. Which line has an error?
mc.e: range(1,5) skips num[0]; use range(0,5).
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q10 (p.198)

mc.q: Program 1 finds largest and smallest in one loop from index 1; Program 2 uses two separate loops from index 0. Execution times?
mc.e: Program 1 traverses the list once with N-1 iterations; Program 2 does 2N.
mc.src: Textbook D2 Ch6 Chapter Exercise MC Q11 (p.198)

mc.q: Which type of test data is used to check if a program can process invalid inputs?
mc.e: Erroneous data are invalid inputs.
mc.ez: 错误数据用来测试无效输入。

mc.q: A program accepts integer ages 0 to 120. Which value is both erroneous and boundary data?
mc.e: 121 is just outside the valid range.

mc.q: A program accepts integer ages 0 to 120. Which value is both normal and boundary data?
mc.e: 0 is valid and on the edge.

mc.q: What should be done when the test result differs from the expected result?
o: Conclude there is an error and debug the program
mc.e: A difference indicates an error.

mc.q: Normal test data should be enough to:
o: test all branches of the selection structures
mc.e: Normal data must reach every branch.
mc.ez: 正常数据要覆盖所有分支。

mc.q: Algorithm: input coupon (1,2,3 valid) and isStudent (True/False). Using coupon values 0,1,2,3, how many test combinations?
For if mark >= 40 with integer marks, which three values best test the boundary?
mc.e: Test v-1, v, v+1.

mc.q: A hotel offers rooms 1-10-2022 to 1-12-2022. Which check-in/check-out pair is erroneous because the range is illogical?
mc.e: Check-out is earlier than check-in.

mc.q: Which date is erroneous because it does not exist?
mc.e: September has 30 days; 2024 is a leap year.

mc.q: BMI algorithm: <=0 Error, <18.5 Underweight, <23 Normal, <25 Overweight, else Obese. Output for 18.5?
mc.e: 18.5 is not < 18.5 but is < 23.

mc.q: Which error is detected by the IDE before the program runs?
mc.e: Syntax errors break language rules.
mc.ez: 语法错误由 IDE 检测。

mc.q: Which error type gives no error message but wrong output?
mc.e: Logic errors run but produce wrong results.
mc.ez: 逻辑错误没有错误信息。

mc.q: Which is a run-time error?
o: Accessing an item outside the array index range
mc.e: IndexError happens during execution.
mc.ez: 索引越界在运行时发生。

mc.q:
What does this output?
A = 10
B = 20
A = B
B = A
print(A, B)

mc.q: Which Python error message appears for int("A")?
o: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'A'

mc.q: import math; print(math.sqrt(2 - 6)) raises:
mc.e: Square root of a negative number.

mc.q: What is wrong with if num = 0: in Python?
mc.e: Use == for comparison.

mc.q: Which statement about C = A x B in Python is correct?
o: It is a syntax error; use *
mc.e: x is not an operator.

mc.q:
What does this print?
price1 = "10"
price2 = "15"
print(price1 + price2)
mc.e: + concatenates strings.

mc.q: A loop while i <= 10: print(i) without updating i causes:
mc.e: i never changes.

items.t: Recommendation systems: why the Internet 'knows' you
items.tz: 推荐系统：为什么网络比你更懂你
k: Recommendation systems track users' activities with big data and predict their actions with AI algorithms.
Benefit: personalised, relevant content; increases website traffic and sales.
Concern: privacy, since data are collected without users noticing; filter bubble.
Volume – large amount of data; challenge: storage of the growing data
Variety – wide range of data types; challenge: integration of different data sources
Velocity – high speed of data generation and analysis; challenge: effective and timely evaluation
Veracity – uncertainty of data; challenge: data accuracy and quality
Match the scenario to the V, then state its challenge in the textbook phrase.
AI is the intelligence of machines that often involves heuristic programs to allow machines to learn from experience and make decisions like humans.
A heuristic discovers effective decisions through previous experience.
Machine learning is the process of a machine training itself by reading sample data, without programming every detail manually.
Steps: provide data → find patterns → generate model → obtain predictions.
More samples give more accurate output.

items.tz: 监督式与非监督式学习
k: Supervised learning trains the computer with labelled datasets.
Unsupervised learning identifies patterns in unlabelled datasets without human guidance.

items.t: Deep learning and artificial neural networks
items.tz: 深度学习与人工神经网络
k: An artificial neural network is a set of algorithms inspired by the human brain, designed to recognise patterns.
Input layer → hidden layer(s) → output layer.
Pattern recognition is the process of finding similarities, relationships or patterns to analyse and solve complex problems more efficiently.
AI first identifies and categorises the data, then generates the most possible output.
Images are formed by pixels; the AI scans the pixels of different images, groups pixels to identify features, and recognises the object when the same pattern is detected again.
Facial recognition captures specific features on a face and detects and matches the human face against a database of faces to verify identity.
A digital video is a collection of frames; video recognition needs a more comprehensive analysis of multiple continuous frames.
Self-driving vehicles analyse multiple frames and combine the analyses to react to unexpected events and recognise road signs.
Voices differ in pitch (frequency) and volume (amplitude); these features are captured through digitalisation (sampling).
Speech recognition allows computers to convert human speech into written format.
There is no exact definition of spam, so the AI customises the filter by recording users' preferences (training through manual classification).
CAPTCHA distinguishes humans from computers to block spammers.
OCR converts images of printed or handwritten text into editable, machine-readable text.
Instant camera translation uses OCR and AR.

items.t: Applications of AI and data science (overview)
items.tz: AI 与数据科学的应用（总览）
k: An application involves AI if the system learns from data to recognise, predict or make decisions; a fixed calculation is not AI.
Data science extracts useful information from data.
Data mining is the process of sorting structured data to recognise patterns and establish relationships.

items.t: Relationship between IoT, big data, AI and data science
items.tz: IoT、大数据、AI 与数据科学的关系
k: IoT collects data → big data is used to train AI models (through data science) → AI automates tasks using intelligence (through IoT devices).

items.t: Ethics of AI and data science
items.tz: AI 与数据科学的伦理
k: Threats to privacy
Discriminatory outcomes
Liability for unintended consequences on public safety
Using AI as a weapon

items.t: 3D printing: what it is and how it works
k: 3D printers eject materials such as plastic, metal or food; multiple layers are stacked upon each other.
3D model drawn → sliced into layers → codes for nozzle movement generated → printed layer by layer.
3D printing is an additive manufacturing method.
A 3D model can be downloaded from a 3D model sharing platform, scanned with a 3D scanner, or built with 3D design software.
3D printing is suitable for customised, small-quantity production and for printing items on site instead of shipping them.
Time-saving: faster prototyping
Lower cost: one-step production, reduces labour costs
Tailor-made: customised products without moulding
Sustainability: reduces waste, local production reduces carbon footprint
IP challenges: easier and cheaper to create fakes; current IP law needs to be updated.
Community safety: undetectable 3D-printed plastic firearms.
Decentralisation of local production; fierce competition.
3D visualisation gives a greater sense of depth than 2D images.
VR replaces the real world; AR overlays digital images onto the real world; holograms can be seen with bare eyes.
VR is a computer-simulated environment which gives users a feeling of being in the virtual environment.
Imagination: 3D models by CAD software; Replication: captured by 360-degree cameras.
VR headsets create an immersive experience by totally taking over one's vision.
VR provides virtual hands-on training with a lower risk of failure in real life.
AR overlays digital images and information onto the real world.
AR aims to enhance the real-world experience by adding virtual objects.
AR shows extra digital information on top of the real view, e.g. heads-up displays, AR navigation, virtual try-on.
Virtual images produced by holograms can be seen with bare eyes.
A holographic pyramid creates the image by a transparent pyramid reflecting the video shown on the screen.
Benefits: virtual hands-on training with lower risk of failure; more flexible, anytime and anywhere; lower cost.
Limitations: digital divide; privacy and security concerns about data collection by AR; less aware of surroundings; technical expertise required.

items.t: Lab and activity summary: hands-on tools
items.tz: 实验与活动总结：动手工具
k: Recognise the application of 3D printing, AR and VR through practical experience.

mc.q: What is/are the advantage(s) of using tablet computers in e-learning?
st: (1) Students can easily carry tablet computers and access a Wi-Fi network.
(2) Tablet computers can store a large amount of learning materials so that online resources will not be necessary.
(3) Tablet computers have a high processing power.
mc.e: Portability + Wi-Fi is the real advantage; storage and processing power are limited.

mc.q: Which of the following are the potential benefits of e-learning?
st: It can track individual learning progress.
mc.e: E-learning tracks progress and lets people learn any time. It needs more hardware, not less.

mc.q: Computer Assisted Diagnosis (CADx) helps doctors interpret medical images of the human body. It combines the elements of artificial intelligence and digital image processing. Which of the following domains of knowledge is the most important to CADx?
mc.e: AI and image processing are built on algorithm design.

mc.q:
Which of the following are examples of big data and AI?
(1) Automated news writing
(2) Crowdedness predictions in Google Map
(3) Google Translate
mc.e: All three learn from large data sets to generate or predict output.
mc.ez: 三者都从大量数据学习来生成或预测。

mc.q: Computer-assisted Translation (CAT) uses AI and translation memories. Which knowledge is the most important to CAT?
mc.e: Translation logic is built from algorithms (machine learning).

mc.q:
Which of the following are examples of big data collected by Google Maps to predict arrival time?
(1) Historical traffic patterns
(2) Live traffic conditions provided by drivers
(3) Users' location history collected by Google
(4) Users' identity
mc.e: Traffic and location data help ETA prediction; identity is not needed.
mc.ez: 交通和位置数据有助预测，身份无关。

mc.q:
Which statements about 3D printing are correct?
(1) It is easier to produce complex designs.
(2) It is cheaper for small production.
(3) It is more flexible to modify the design.
(4) It can only create 3D objects with plastic.
mc.e: 3D printers can also use metal or food, so (4) is wrong.
mc.ez: 也可用金属、食物，(4) 错。

mc.q: Which of the following will most likely be considered copyright infringement in Hong Kong?
o: Sharing copyrighted 3D printable files with friends without permission
Searching for 3D printable files using peer-to-peer file sharing software
Designing 3D models and printing it out as a gift
Downloading free 3D printable files and printing it for personal use
mc.e: Distributing copyrighted files without permission infringes copyright.
mc.ez: 未经许可分享受版权保护的档案属侵权。

mc.q:
Schools use AR and VR to teach Geography and Biology. What are the benefits?
(1) Alternatives to real field trips and experiments
(2) Widening the digital divide
(3) Enhancing students' engagement
(4) Deepening students' understanding
mc.e: Widening the digital divide is a drawback.

mc.q: Fashion brands close physical stores and add AR try-on to their apps. What is the drawback of this decision?
mc.e: Customers without devices/skills are excluded.
mc.ez: 没有装置或技能的人被排斥。

mc.q: AI can help people block spam automatically. Which knowledge area is the most important for this function?
mc.e: Spam filtering is a classification algorithm.
mc.ez: 过滤垃圾邮件是分类算法。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q1 (p.38)

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of big data?
o: The amount of data grows rapidly.
The Internet produces more accurate and reliable data.
There is a wide range of data types.
A large amount of data is generated.
mc.e: Veracity means big data are uncertain, not more accurate.
mc.ez: Veracity 指数据不确定，并非更准确。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q2 (p.38)

mc.q: A student points his phone camera at a dinosaur fossil and an animated 3D dinosaur pops up on screen to explain it. Which technology is applied?
mc.e: Digital content overlaid on the real-world camera view is AR.
mc.ez: 在真实画面上叠加数码内容是 AR。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q3 (p.38)

mc.q: Velocity means generating and analysing data at high speed. Which method can help overcome the challenges brought by big data?
o: Analysing data with the help of AI.
Funding poor families to buy mobile devices.
Promoting IoT to generate more data.
mc.e: AI enables effective and timely evaluation of fast data.
mc.ez: AI 能及时有效地分析数据。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q4 (p.38)

mc.q:
Which are applications of AI and big data?
(1) Calculation of a student's average score in an examination
(2) Facial recognition feature of photo sharing sites
(3) Speech recognition behind a digital assistant
(4) Friend recommendation feature of social media sites
mc.e: Averaging is a simple fixed calculation, not AI.
mc.ez: 计平均分只是简单计算。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q5 (p.38)

mc.q:
Which of the following can apply virtual reality technology?
(1) Surgical training
(2) Lift maintenance training
(3) Watching movies
(4) Theme park rides
mc.e: All are VR applications (training, media, theme park).
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q6 (p.39)

mc.q:
Which of the following involve AI?
(1) Image search
(2) Music recognition
(3) Spam detection
(4) Handwriting recognition
mc.e: All use pattern recognition.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q7 (p.39)

mc.q:
AlphaGo defeated the human Go champion. Which can AI also do?
(1) Word autocorrect
(2) Songwriting
(3) Voice and text translation
(4) Car driving
mc.e: AI can do all of these, including generating music.
mc.ez: AI 全部做得到，包括作曲。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q8 (p.39)

mc.q:
Which are possible negative impacts of 3D printing?
(1) Creating fakes becomes easier.
(2) Factory workers may lose jobs because products can be printed at home.
(3) Printable firearms may pose danger to society.
(4) Artificial body parts become less affordable.
mc.e: 3D printing makes prosthetics MORE affordable.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q9 (p.39)

mc.q:
Which is/are application(s) of AI?
(1) Doctors making professional judgments about patients based on medical records.
(2) Shopping sites suggesting products based on user preferences in the past.
(3) Streetlights adjusting the brightness according to the surrounding area.
mc.e: (1) is done by humans; (3) is a simple sensor rule. Only (2) learns from data to predict.
mc.ez: (1) 是人做的；(3) 只是感应器规则；只有 (2) 从数据学习预测。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q10 (p.39)

mc.q: Which of the following is the benefit of 3D printing?
o: It reduces carbon footprint with global shipping.
It's easier and cheaper for individuals to create their own products.
The subtractive manufacturing method produces less waste.
mc.e: Customisation without moulds; it is additive and reduces shipping via local production.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch1 Chapter Exercise MC Q11 (p.39)

mc.q: Which V of big data refers to the uncertainty of data?
mc.e: Veracity = uncertainty; challenge is accuracy and quality.

mc.q: The main challenge of the 'Volume' characteristic of big data is
mc.e: Volume → storage.
mc.ez: 数据量大 → 储存问题。

mc.q: A system must combine text posts, photos, videos and GPS locations. Which challenge is it mainly facing?
mc.e: Many data types = variety → integration.
mc.ez: 多种类型 = variety → 整合。

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the extra V's mentioned for big data?
mc.e: The extras are value, variability and visualisation.
mc.ez: 额外的 V 是 value、variability、visualisation。

mc.q: A heuristic is best described as
o: a program that always finds the optimal answer
a problem-solving strategy that discovers effective decisions through previous experience
mc.e: Textbook definition.

mc.q: What is the correct order of machine learning steps?
o: Provide data → Generate model → Find patterns → Obtain predictions
Generate model → Provide data → Find patterns → Obtain predictions
Provide data → Find patterns → Generate model → Obtain predictions
Find patterns → Provide data → Generate model → Obtain predictions
mc.e: Data → patterns → model → predictions.
mc.ez: 数据 → 规律 → 模型 → 预测。

mc.q: In Teachable Machine, what should be done after clicking 'Train Model'?
o: Upload a new image not used as a sample to test the model
Export the samples to a spreadsheet
mc.e: Test with unseen data.

mc.q: Which statement about supervised learning is correct?
o: Humans train the computer with labelled datasets.
It relies on no human guidance.
It usually needs longer training time than unsupervised learning.
mc.e: Supervised = labelled data from humans.
mc.ez: 监督式 = 人类提供有标签数据。

mc.q: Compared with supervised learning, unsupervised learning usually
o: needs more training data and longer training time
mc.e: Table 1.1.

mc.q: An email service learns from emails users have marked 'spam' or 'not spam'. This is an example of
mc.e: User-provided labels → supervised.
mc.ez: 用户给标签 → 监督式。

mc.q: An artificial neural network is inspired by
o: the human brain and nervous system
mc.e: Interlinked neurons.

mc.q: Which layer of an artificial neural network produces the final result?
mc.e: Output layer gives the output.

mc.q: In Fig. 1.6, what happens in Stage II (Prediction)?
o: Pixels are printed layer by layer
A set of labelled cat and dog photos is used for learning
A new image is input and the classifier outputs a label
The data are stored in the cloud
mc.e: Prediction uses the learnt classifier on new input.
mc.ez: 预测阶段用训练好的分类器处理新输入。

mc.q: To recognise an image, an AI model mainly analyses
o: groups of pixels to identify features
mc.e: Pixels are grouped to find patterns/edges.

mc.q: A shopper uploads a photo of a lamp to find where to buy it. This feature is
mc.e: Search by image.

mc.q: Why does a video recognition system need more comprehensive analysis than image recognition?
mc.e: Many frames must be analysed and combined.

mc.q: Self-driving cars mainly use which technology to identify distances to road signs?
mc.e: Computer vision on camera frames.

mc.q: Speech recognition can distinguish voices because each voice has different
mc.e: Unique waveforms.

mc.q: The process that captures sound wave features by sampling at fixed time intervals is called
mc.e: Digitalisation (Core A ch.3).

mc.q: Digital assistants translate human speech into language machines understand using
mc.e: NLP.

items.t: Health risks of prolonged ICT use
items.tz: 长时间使用 ICT 的健康风险
k: health risk + cause + solution , e.g. " RSI in the wrist, caused by repetitive mouse clicking; use a mouse pad with wrist rest to keep the wrist straight. "

items.t: Correct sitting posture and workstation set-up
items.tz: 正确坐姿与工作台设置
k: " adjust the monitor so that the viewing angle is slightly downward ", " keep the forearm horizontal ", " keep the wrist straight ", " keep the feet flat on the floor / footrest ".

items.tz: 手机与平板的正确姿势
k: " Raise the screen to eye level so the user need not bend the neck ."

items.tz: 人体工学的定义与目的
k: " to suit the people who use them " and " minimise the risk of injury ".

items.tz: 电脑用的人体工学产品
k: name the product, then " keeps the wrist straight / raises the screen to eye level , reducing RSI / neck pain ".

items.t: Taking breaks: the 20-20-20 rule and stretching
items.tz: 休息习惯：20-20-20 法则与伸展
k: " take regular breaks and exercise "; " every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds ".
" user-friendly ", " reduces the user's effort / errors ".

items.tz: 界面设计准则：一致、效率、记忆
k: use the guideline name + its phrase, e.g. " Memory: minimise users' memory load by using universal signages. "

items.tz: 误解：人体工学只关于家具
网络成瘾的征兆和症状
k: quote the three signs word for word.
give one physical and one mental impact, plus poor social relationships .
" makes the ignored people feel excluded or less important ".

items.tz: 资讯自由的优点与缺点
网络欺凌的定义与形式
网络欺凌对心理健康的风险

items.tz: 网络欺凌：旁观者应如何做

k: " Everyone has the responsibility to think critically before spreading any information. "

items.tz: 法律后果：《诽谤条例》与《盗窃罪条例》

items.tz: 在社交媒体保护个人资料

items.tz: 数码平等与香港互联网普及率
数码隔阂的意思与范畴

items.tz: 误解：数码隔阂只是没有网络

k: " toxic substances such as lead and mercury leak into soil and rivers, harming the ecosystem and health ".

items.tz: 能源标签（强制性能源效益标签计划）

Positive impact: pollution monitoring, carbon footprint, going paperless

k: " On an OLED screen, black pixels do not emit light, so dark mode reduces power consumption. "

mc.q: Why do many readers like using mobile devices to read books?
st: (1) The ergonomic design of mobile devices helps relieve eye strain.
(2) Mobile devices provide various functions which make reading convenient.
(3) It is convenient for carrying a lot of books.
mc.e: Search, bookmarks, many books in one device are real benefits; screens do not relieve eye strain.

mc.q:
Henry lives in Hong Kong. He likes bags made in Europe so he buys a bag through the online shopping web site of a shop in France.
What are the possible reasons for Henry's choice to buy the bag online?
st: (1) He can select and buy the bag during office hours in France.
(2) There are many different kinds of bags for Henry to choose from.
(3) The bag is not for sale in Hong Kong.
(4) He has a credit card to pay for it.
mc.e: Online shops are open 24 h, so office hours don't matter; having a card is a means, not a reason.

mc.q:
Andrew creates the following group message through a social networking site.

Dear best friends,
The ABC shop has raised its prices and they are so high. I am so angry!
Let's burn down the shop at midnight. Join us!
Andrew

Betty receives and forwards this message to invite her friends, but she does not join the event. Carol receives and reads this message from Betty. Carol does not take any action.
Who has/have misused the social networking site and caused damage to the society?
mc.e: Andrew wrote it and Betty spread it; Carol only read it.

mc.q: At home, John unintentionally detects his neighbour's WiFi network without any security measures. He can fully control the wireless router. What should he do?
o: Connect to the network for web browsing only.
Connect to the network for transferring large files only.
Configure the wireless router with an authentication key.
mc.e: Using or changing someone else's network without permission is wrong; just ignore it.

mc.q: Some teenagers in Hong Kong are addicted to playing online games. Which of the following behaviours are common in this group of teenagers?
st: (1) They prefer playing online games to joining face-to-face social activities.
(2) They play online games as a way of escaping from daily life problems.
(3) They feel irritable when being stopped from using computers.
mc.e: All three are typical signs of Internet/game addiction.

mc.q: The Hong Kong Government launched the Internet Support Learning Programme in 2011. The Programme helps needy students to acquire computer equipment and Internet access services. What issue is the Government addressing?
mc.e: Helping poor students get computers/Internet narrows the digital divide.

mc.q: Which of the following can reduce the threats from using social networking web sites?
st: (1) Block or ignore people that you do not know or trust.
(2) Use default privacy settings to restrict access.
(3) Only disclose the name and address in the account.
mc.e: Default settings are often public, and disclosing your address is risky.

mc.q: For the sake of their health, users should take a rest after every hour of computer use. A software company wants to improve its word processing software to include this ergonomic feature. When a user uses the software for an hour, the software should
st: (1) display an alert message on the screen.
(2) send an alert email to the user.
mc.e: An on-screen alert is immediate; email may be unread, and shutting down loses work.

mc.q: In 2012, the US Government launched a project to explore how ‘big data’ could be used. ‘Big data’ refers to the huge amount of data collected which is difficult to process using database management systems. Which of the following are examples of ‘big data’?
st: (2) User behaviour in a social networking web site
(3) The total number of government officials in the US
mc.e: DNA and social-network behaviour are huge data sets; a headcount is one number.

mc.q: Which of the following public policies can improve the digital divide in Hong Kong?
st: (1) Subsidise low-income families so that they can get Internet access at home.
(2) Provide computer equipment to students in need.
(3) Give free training courses to citizens who lack basic IT skills.
mc.e: Access, equipment and skills are all parts of the digital divide.

mc.q: Mary is a teenager and makes a new friend, Ada, through a random search function in a social networking web site. Ada wants to meet Mary the following Monday night at 10 p.m. in a restaurant. Mary's eldest brother advises her not to meet Ada. What is the major reason?
o: Mary can use another function in the social networking web site to make new friends.
Mary's eldest brother cannot join the meeting.
Mary can meet another friend earlier.
mc.e: Online identities can be fake; meeting a stranger is risky.

mc.q: Which of the following actions for desktop computers is/are environmentally-friendly?
st: (3) Use LED monitors instead of CRT monitors.
mc.e: Power management and LED monitors save energy; resolution barely matters.

mc.q:
David answers the following question in his school assignment: 'What is the history of the HKEAA?' He uses a search engine and finds the following paragraph:

The HKEAA was established in 2077...

Which of the following actions is/are appropriate?
st: (1) Put the entire paragraph in a search engine and search for similar results.
(2) Browse other web sites to validate the information.
(3) Copy the paragraph to the assignment.
mc.e: The year 2077 is clearly wrong, so check other sources; don't copy it.

mc.q: Mr Chan wants to buy a tablet computer for his 8-year-old daughter, Susan. Which of the following actions is/are appropriate?
st: (1) Mr Chan should buy a tablet computer with a longer battery life.
(2) Susan should use the tablet computer with a mouse.
(3) Susan should take a 5-minute break after using the tablet computer for 30 minutes.
mc.e: Longer battery life means less charging hassle, and regular breaks protect her eyes; a tablet is made for touch, not a mouse.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are ergonomic design(s)?
st: (1) A password can be set on a wireless router to prevent access by unauthorised users.
(2) The angle of the elevation/depression of a monitor display is adjustable.
(3) The text shown in word processing software can be enlarged.
mc.e: Ergonomics is about fitting equipment to the user's body: an adjustable monitor angle.

mc.q: Recently some countries have attracted more females to study ICT courses and to work in the ICT industry. What is the benefit of this policy?
mc.e: More diverse talent brings more ideas and innovation.

mc.q: Which of the following are characteristics of the Information Age?
st: (1) Information is widely distributed via the Internet.
(2) Information can be quickly accessed by the public.
(3) All company information on the Internet is correct.
mc.e: Information spreads widely and fast, but not all of it is correct.

mc.q:
What is the aim of the following policy?

"The Government helps families in need acquire computers and Internet access, and delivers personal support and training to them so children and parents can tap the online world's potential."
o: Promoting the freedom of information on the Internet
Promoting the change in the nature of work
mc.e: Giving needy families computers and training narrows the digital divide.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the government e-services provided by GovHK?
st: (1) Enrolling for community recreation and sports programmes
(2) Applying for admission to universities in Hong Kong
mc.e: Leisure programme enrolment and library renewals are government e-services; university admission is through JUPAS/universities.

mc.q: What changes have been brought about by the emergence of the Information Age?
st: (2) New ICT-related jobs appear and change the job market.
(3) There are more opportunities to acquire information and to learn new things.
mc.e: New ICT jobs and more learning chances; remote work means less office space, not more.

mc.q: What are the major reasons for applying ergonomic design principles to computers in the work environment?
st: (2) Saves on costs of setting up computers.
(3) Provides a customised, adjustable setup for meeting different people's needs.
mc.e: Ergonomics protects health and fits different users; it usually costs more, not less.

mc.q: The World Health Organization (WHO) states that 15% of the world's population have disabilities. What can we do for these people to improve the access to ICT significantly?
o: Gives persons with disabilities notebook computers.
Sets up free computer centres for persons with disabilities to access the Internet.
Develops appropriate tools for persons with disabilities to access ICT.
Provides free ICT training for persons with disabilities.
mc.e: Assistive tools (screen readers, special input devices) let them actually use ICT.

mc.q: What are the good ergonomic practices in software design?
mc.e: Clear messages and a consistent interface help users; a fixed font size does not.

mc.q: Which of the following will help overcome the digital divide in a city?
st: (1) Implementing a Bring-Your-Own-Device (BYOD) policy in schools to replace desktop computers
(3) Providing more than one free email account for each citizen
mc.e: Free WiFi widens Internet access; BYOD can hurt students without devices.

mc.q: What of the following is/are the benefit(s) of e-government?
st: (1) Government information can be more easily accessed by the public in digital format.
(2) The data security of the government information is enhanced.
(3) The digital divide in society can be closed.
mc.e: E-government improves access; it does not by itself raise security or close the digital divide.

mc.q: Which of the following is not appropriate for enhancing students' information literacy?
o: Watching documentaries about the ocean online
Searching for the installation password of a software package through an online discussion forum
Reading school newsletters through the school intranet
Finding the history of computers through the Internet
mc.e: Hunting for software passwords online is unethical and likely illegal.

mc.q: A student is addicted to online gaming and plays more than 8 hours every day. Which of the following health problems might he encounter?
mc.e: Long gaming hours can harm sleep, eyesight and mood.

mc.q: An online shop collects its members' personal information. Which of the following actions is/are not appropriate without members' consent?
st: (1) The shop encrypts and uploads all personal information to cloud storage.
(2) The shop sends all personal information to other online shops which provide other services to members.
(3) When a member unregisters his/her membership, the shop keeps the personal information permanently to help with his/her re-registration in the future.
mc.e: Passing data to others and keeping it longer than needed break data privacy principles.

mc.q: What should be considered when using information from the Internet to write a report?
st: Some information on the Internet is unreliable.
Most information on the Internet is free.
Many hackers steal personal information through social media.
mc.e: Reliability of the source matters for a report. Price and hacking are not about using the information.

mc.q: Which of the following can narrow the digital divide in the society?
st: Providing computers to students for learning
Providing self-service kiosks for ordering food in restaurants
Using electronic payment to replace cash payment in shops
mc.e: Giving people access to computers narrows the gap. Kiosks and e-payment push people without IT skills further out.

mc.q: Why is information literacy important in a knowledge-based society?
st: People should be able to identify fake information and hoaxes on the Internet.
People should be able to write artificial intelligence (AI) programs.
People should understand that some information from the Internet lacks credibility.
mc.e: Information literacy is judging information. Writing AI programs is not part of it.

mc.q: A shopping mall plans to develop a mobile application for customers to register their shopping records and gain bonus points for gifts. Which of the following considerations should be the least important?
mc.e: Security, privacy and which OS to support all matter. App file size matters least.

mc.q: Which of the following are appropriate when using a social media application?
st: Understand the terms of use of the application.
Forward information sent from others to friends as soon as possible.
mc.e: Read the terms and share as little personal data as possible. Forwarding without checking spreads rumours.

mc.q: Which of the following are proper measures when using social media platforms?
st: Manage the privacy settings to control who can see your posts.
Use a strong login password and change it regularly.
Be aware of what personal information you have provided.
mc.e: All three protect your account and privacy.

mc.q: Which of the following can help bridge the digital divide?
st: Providing free access to computers in public libraries.
Providing Internet access for students in need.
Providing online English lessons for students in need.
mc.e: Free computers and Internet access close the gap in IT access. Online English lessons need access already and teach English, not IT.

mc.q: A research company estimates that in 2012 China has over 500 million Internet users. China’s Internet population becomes the largest in the world. Which of the following statements about China is/are correct?
st: The growth in e-commerce will be greatly accelerated.
The number of computers per person is the largest in the world.
The broadband quality is the best in the world.
mc.e: Many users drive e-commerce; a large total does not mean most computers per person or best broadband.

mc.q: Which of the following examples can effectively reduce theft of digital intellectual property?
mc.e: Watermarks mark ownership of digital works. Firewalls and virus definitions protect systems, not IP.

mc.q: Which of the following equipment can help to minimise repetitive strain injury to fingers and wrists during typing?
mc.e: An armrest (wrist support) reduces strain on wrists and fingers.

mc.q: Which practice helps prevent repetitive strain injury in fingers and wrists caused by clicking the mouse?
o: Use a wrist rest to keep the wrist natural.
Maintain good lighting in the room.
mc.e: A wrist rest keeps the wrist straight; the others target leg, neck and eye problems.
mc.ez: 护腕令手腕平直，其余对应腿、颈、眼。

mc.q: Peter uses dual monitors. Which set-up is ergonomic? (1) swivel chair to avoid neck twisting (2) both monitors at arm's length (3) one monitor above the other
mc.e: Stacking monitors makes him tilt his head up.

mc.q: Susan installs a rest reminder app to prevent prolonged smart device use. Which feature should it include? (1) close the app she is using (2) turn off the device (3) push a rest notification
mc.e: A reminder should notify, not force-close apps or the device.

mc.q: Which interface features relate to user-friendly ergonomic design? (1) zoom for poor eyesight (2) consistent terms (3) stations grouped by rail line (4) sufficient colour contrast
mc.e: All reduce user effort or suit user abilities.

mc.q: Peter's feet do not reach the floor. Which ergonomic product prevents leg fatigue?
mc.e: A footrest keeps the feet flat.

mc.q: Without a footrest, what should Peter adjust to prevent leg fatigue? (1) chair height (2) monitor viewing angle (3) monitor height (4) table height
mc.e: Lower the chair so the feet rest flat (1). Then lower the table so the forearms stay horizontal (4), and lower the monitor so the top is at eye level (3). The viewing angle does not need to change.
mc.ez: 把椅子调低让双脚平放 (1)；再把桌子调低保持前臂水平 (4)；把显示器调低到视线水平 (3)。屏幕视角不必改。

mc.q: Which action can avoid neck pain from prolonged computer use?
o: Adjust the viewing angle of the monitor.
mc.e: Monitor angle slightly downward avoids bending the neck.
mc.ez: 调整显示器角度避免弯颈。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC1 (p.77)

mc.q: Why does Charles type documents on a desktop computer and keyboard instead of his tablet?
o: Mechanical keyboards allow better hand-eye coordination.
Desktop computers are easier to operate.
Desktop computers show texts more clearly on a larger screen.
mc.e: Adjustable monitor, keyboard and chair form an ergonomic workstation.
mc.ez: 桌面电脑配合人体工学设计。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC2 (p.77)

mc.q: George reads social media 6 hours daily. Which health issue will NOT arise from his Internet addiction?
mc.e: Diabetes is not a listed impact.

mc.q: Which are signs and symptoms of Internet addiction? (1) watching a movie on a streaming site every night (2) upset when cannot connect (3) thinking about the Internet during lessons (4) prioritising Internet over important tasks
mc.e: (1) alone is a normal leisure habit.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC7 (p.77)

mc.q: Patrick reposted fake news about an idol and left offensive comments. What should he have done?
o: Fact-check the information with other sources
mc.e: Fact-checking.

mc.q: George claims a coupon bug and asks for DMs. Amy does not repost because: (1) it may be a scam as George's identity is unknown (2) it may cause a huge loss to the shop (3) it is illegal to steal coupons without authority
mc.e: All three reasons apply.

mc.q: George posts Amy's phone number and photos and fake statements that she shoplifted. Which laws may he violate? (1) Copyright (2) Personal Data (Privacy) (3) Defamation
mc.e: Doxxing + harming reputation.

mc.q: Eva's public selfies were reposted with teasing comments. How can she prevent personal data leakage?
o: Set her account to private and only allow close friends to see it
Comment on the forum asking people to stop
mc.e: Private account.

mc.q: Peter is hired to spread rumours harming a company's reputation. Which is correct?
o: Peter has the right to spread false information
The company may take legal actions against Peter
Peter should invite friends to earn money too
mc.e: Defamation.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC5 (p.77)

mc.q: Amy, an online friend, asks Andy to lend tuition money. Andy's classmate disagrees. Why?
o: Andy does not know how to transfer money
Amy can borrow from richer friends
Andy can buy a game with the money
Amy may tell lies and it may be a fraud
mc.e: Possible fraud.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC6 (p.77)

mc.q: What is the problem of digital divide?
o: Those who cannot access online information will become isolated from society
mc.e: Isolation from society.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC4 (p.77)

mc.q: Which feature helps visually impaired people use ICT?
mc.e: Others help hearing/language groups.
mc.ez: 其余帮听障或语言群体。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC3 (p.77)

mc.q: Which measures can the government use to overcome the digital divide in HK? (1) more free Wi-Fi (2) fund the disabled to buy smartphones with assistive technology (3) high-contrast official websites (4) abandon cash and only accept digital payment
mc.e: (4) widens the divide.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC8 (p.77)

mc.q: Which are examples of digital divide? (1) the elderly cannot type on phones (2) poor students cannot afford high-speed Internet (3) employers favour male programmers believing females are bad at programming
mc.e: Age, income and gender gaps.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC9 (p.78)

mc.q: Susan buys a tablet for her 70-year-old father. Which should she do? (1) buy a wireless mouse (2) make the font bigger (3) enable screen reader (4) install a simple and clean launcher
mc.e: Bigger font and simple launcher.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC10 (p.78)

mc.q: Advantages of a live transcription app: (1) easier communication for hearing impaired (2) auto notes in meetings (3) widen the digital divide (4) reduce RSI by less keyboard use
mc.e: It narrows, not widens, the divide.

mc.q: The Community Chest funded WeTV.hk to provide accessible media and job opportunities for disabled talents. Its aim is to
mc.e: Helps the disabled participate digitally.

mc.q: Which policies bridge the digital divide among the elderly? (1) Elderly IT Learning Portal (2) ICT Outreach Programme teaching basic IT skills (3) ICT Training Programme with advanced courses
mc.e: Advanced courses do not target elders' basic gap.

mc.q: Which action can save electricity and protect the environment?
o: Turn on battery optimisation when using a smartphone.
Reduce the screen resolution when using a laptop computer.
Open tens of browser tabs simultaneously when using a desktop computer.
Turn off the automatic screen lock when using a tablet computer.
mc.e: The textbook answer is battery optimisation; many tabs and no screen lock waste power.

mc.q: Purposes of Free-Flow Tolling: (1) reduce manpower expenditure (2) eliminate the digital gap (3) improve traffic at the tunnel (4) reduce carbon emission
mc.e: Not related to digital gap.

mc.q: The 20-20-20 rule says every 20 minutes you should look at something about how far away for 20 seconds?
mc.e: 20 feet ≈ 6 m.

mc.q: According to the book, how often should you take a 5-minute break to stretch?
mc.e: 5-minute stretch every hour.

mc.q: Deep vein thrombosis is dangerous mainly because
o: blood clots may travel to the lungs
mc.e: A clot reaching the lungs can be fatal.

mc.q: Which item reduces eyestrain caused by sunlight reflecting on the screen?
mc.e: Blinds block strong sunlight and reflections.

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT an ergonomic design?
o: Vertical mouse that avoids twisting the wrist
Adjustable font size in an app
mc.e: A password is a security feature.

mc.q: Splitting a long online registration into several short steps follows which interface guideline?
mc.e: Break complex tasks into simpler tasks (efficiency).

mc.q: Using universal icons such as a magnifying glass for 'search' mainly
mc.e: Universal signage = memory guideline.
mc.ez: 通用标志减少记忆负担。

mc.q: Using the same word 'Delete' (not 'Remove' in some screens and 'Erase' in others) throughout an app follows
mc.e: Consistent terminologies.

mc.q: 'Tech neck' is mainly caused by
o: looking down at a phone for long periods
mc.e: Bending the neck forward.

mc.q: Which is a sign of Internet addiction rather than a habit?
o: Being late for school because you could not stop gaming
Surfing for an hour after finishing homework
mc.e: Missing important tasks because you cannot stop.
mc.ez: 无法停止以致错过要事。

mc.q: Which is a MENTAL health impact of Internet addiction listed in the book?
mc.e: Mental: poor memory, anxiety/depression, concentration difficulty.
mc.ez: 心理：记忆差、焦虑抑郁、难集中。

mc.q: 'Phubbing' means
o: ignoring the person you are with to look at your phone
mc.e: Phone snubbing.

mc.q: Which game feature best helps prevent teenagers' game addiction?
o: Automatic logout after a daily playtime limit
mc.e: Playtime limits enforce breaks.

mc.q: Which is NOT a benefit (pro) of freedom of information in Table 2.2?
mc.e: Lack of quality control is a con.

mc.q: SOHO in the book refers to
mc.e: Small office/Home office: video conferencing, remote work, cloud collaboration.

mc.q: Ride-hailing and mobile payment are examples of which Internet change in Fig. 2.11?
mc.e: E-commerce.

mc.q: Why can freedom of information lead to fines and imprisonment?
o: Abusing it to harm others (fake news, cyberbullying, scams) breaks laws
Using social media requires a licence
mc.e: Freedom does not justify harming others.
mc.ez: 滥用自由伤害他人会违法。

mc.q: Which con of freedom of information is shown when an old web page still lists last year's bus fares?
mc.e: Old pages are not updated.

mc.q: Which statement about cyberbullying is correct?
o: It is harassment over the Internet on any platform where people interact
Joking and bullying have the same effect
It is legal if the bully is anonymous
It only happens on social media
mc.e: Messaging apps, social media, games, forums, etc.

mc.q: Nearly what proportion of Hong Kong students have experienced cyberbullying according to the survey in the book?
mc.e: Nearly half.

k: IP is the creation of intellect, a set of separate intangible asset rights granted to a person, a party or a company. Protecting IP ensures a safe and fair environment for artists and inventors to continue their innovations .

items.t: Four types of IP: overview and registration
k: Except for copyright, the other types of IP all require registration. In Hong Kong, registration is done with the Intellectual Property Department .

items.t: Copyright symbol and patents for software
k: Computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem. A patent protects an invention which can be a product, process or substance.

items.tz: 商标（™ 与 ®）及注册外观设计
k: Trademark: a unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others' . Registered design: protection of the new and distinctive appearance of products .

items.t: Who owns copyright? Monkey selfie and AI works
items.tz: 谁拥有版权？猴子自拍与 AI 作品
k: Only works created by a human are protected by copyright ; a work with no human author is in the public domain .
The copyright of a work is automatically given to the creator after the work is completed; there is no need to register. It generally lasts until 50 years after the death of the creator.

items.t: Works protected by the Copyright Ordinance
k: The Copyright Ordinance protects original literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works ; sound recordings, broadcasts, films or cable programmes ; and the typographical arrangement of published editions .

items.tz: 误解：意念 vs 表达
k: Copyright does not protect ideas. It protects the expression of ideas when it is presented in a tangible form.
The copyright owner has exclusive rights to copy, publish, broadcast, adapt and translate the work, grant the right to use it in return for royalties , sell it and pass it to others in a will .
Creative Commons licences are established to protect both creators and users. Elements: Attribution, Share-alike, Non-commercial, No Derivative Works .
Unauthorised use and redistribution of copyrighted works in digital form are considered Internet piracy.
Pirated software may contain malware, cannot receive security updates or technical support, and using it is copyright infringement.
Name the stakeholder + the effect: "Creators lose income, so they lose motivation to create new high-quality works."
Write it as a chain with 'so': "Piracy reduces sales, so companies earn less and investors withdraw; companies close, raising unemployment, and tax revenue falls."
Distributing and using pirated media and software for commercial purposes are criminal offences; maximum penalty: $50,000 per pirated copy and 4 years' imprisonment.

items.t: Civil lawsuit and the BT case
items.tz: 民事诉讼与 BT 案
k: Copyright owners have the right to ask buyers or users for monetary compensation through a civil lawsuit.

items.t: IP authorities: IPD vs Customs and Excise
items.tz: 知识产权署 vs 香港海关
k: Only the Customs and Excise Department takes criminal sanctions against copyright and trademark infringements.
Fair dealing allows limited use of a copyrighted work without the permission of the copyright owner for purposes such as education, research and private study, criticism, review and news reporting.

items.t: Fair dealing or infringement? School cases
items.tz: 公平处理还是侵权？学校个案
k: Not all acts for educational purposes can be exempted ; only limited, non-profit use relevant to teaching is fair dealing.

items.t: When the dealing is unfair: news cases
items.tz: 不公平处理的新闻个案
k: It is not fair dealing because it is for commercial purposes and reproduces the whole work , so it replaces the market for the original .
Users should obtain permission from the copyright holders and read the terms and conditions before using the copyrighted material : identify, obtain, use according to terms, acknowledge .

items.tz: 注明出处与 CC 署名
k: "[Title]" by [Creator] is licensed under [Licence].
In-text citation cites the author and year of publication in the body; the reference list is attached at the end of the article.

items.tz: 误解：抄袭 vs 侵犯版权
k: Copyright infringement may occur, but not always, in plagiarism, and vice versa. Plagiarism is unethical while copyright infringement is illegal.

items.tz: 版权持有人保护版权的方法
k: Copyright holders have a responsibility to set terms and conditions to limit the use of granted copyright , e.g. publishing with a CC licence.
Licences are granted to users by developers to define how the software can be used or the restriction of certain usages.

items.t: Four types of software licence compared
k: Only open source software gives access to the source code. Shareware is a free trial that is time-limited or feature-limited.

items.t: Choosing a licence type as a user
items.tz: 用户角度：选择软件类型
k: For shareware: advanced features may be available only when you purchase and it is only free for the trial period .

items.t: Choosing a licence type as a developer
items.tz: 开发者角度：选择授权模式
k: Shareware lets a developer make money for authorising use , not give up copyright , and attract more people to try it .

items.t: Misconception: freeware and open source are not uncopyrighted
items.tz: 误解：免费及开源软件也有版权
k: Only public domain software is uncopyrighted. Freeware, shareware, open source and commercial software only grant users rights to use the software under different licence agreements.

items.t: User licence: single-user, multi-user and site licence
items.tz: 用户授权：单用户、多用户、场地授权
k: A single-user licence allows the software to be installed on only one device or used by only one user at a time.
SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing ; users pay for the licence monthly or annually .

items.tz: 永久授权 vs 订阅
k: Perpetual: indefinite use with one-off payment, Internet connection not required . Subscription: access on multiple devices by account login, free frequent updates .
A licence key is a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid for the software; it is entered during installation to register or activate the software.

items.tz: 锁定装置 vs 锁定用户授权
k: Device-locked: the licence key is locked to the unique machine ID of your device . User-locked: the licence key is locked to a specific account; users can use it on any device but must remain signed in .
Invisible watermarks are harder to remove, do not affect the carrying object, and can still be extracted even after cropping, resizing and compression.
Data given to different recipients is watermarked differently. This is useful to trace the person who leaks the confidential information.
Digital signature is used for verifying the sender's identity and detecting unauthorised modification and forgery such as pirated software.

items.tz: 必须上网的应用：以加密防盗版
k: When the game connects to the Internet, it is processing data encryption and decryption, which aims to prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about open source software is correct?
o: It is free of program bugs.
It can be modified and distributed freely.
It runs faster in a networked operating system.
mc.e: Open source licences let anyone modify and redistribute the code.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about open source software is correct?
o: Open source software is written by open source programming languages.
Open source software is executed in open source operating systems.
The source code can be copied, modified and redistributed freely.
Private companies cannot use open source software to make a profit.
mc.e: Open source = source code available to copy, modify and share.

mc.q: In a company, all URLs browsed through the office computers are recorded by a proxy server. Which of the following statements is correct?
o: The URLs should be recorded during office hours only.
The records should be checked by authorised staff only.
The records are the digital property of the staff.
The company has committed a computer crime.
mc.e: Logs contain personal data, so only authorised staff should access them.

mc.q: Peter uses peer-to-peer file sharing software to download a commercial application program. His friends advise him not to install it. Why?
st: (1) His action will create a digital divide.
(2) The application program may be spyware.
mc.e: Pirated software from P2P may carry malware and breaks copyright law.

mc.q: Which of the following can help visually impaired persons to browse the web?
mc.e: Braille displays and magnifiers are assistive tools; filtering isn't.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about copyright protection in Hong Kong is correct?
o: Ideas are not protected unless they are in the form of expressions or products.
The Customs and Excise Department cannot take legal action against copyright piracy unless the copyright owners file a complaint.
A book cannot be protected unless it is published in Hong Kong.
Computer programs are not protected unless the copyright owners inform the Office of the Government Chief Information Officer (OGCIO).
mc.e: Copyright protects expressions, not bare ideas; protection is automatic.

mc.q: Cindy meets her friends and shares her photos. She does not upload the photos to her social networking account. Why not?
st: (1) Cindy wants to own the copyright of the photos.
(2) Cindy wants to protect her personal privacy.
(3) Cindy wants to prevent her account from being hacked.
mc.e: Not uploading keeps the photos private; she owns the copyright either way.

mc.q: Peter is a student and does the following actions. Which of them are illegal?
st: (1) Uses a BT program to share his homework.
(2) Uses a BT program to download copyrighted songs for his own use.
(3) Buys copyrighted software and makes copies for his best friends only.
mc.e: Downloading copyrighted songs and copying software break copyright; sharing his own homework does not.

mc.q: Mary downloads three types of programs, P, Q and R from the Internet. She can use P for a trial period, changes the source code of Q and only uses some functions in R. Which type(s) of program is/are shareware?
mc.e: Shareware is either time-limited (P) or feature-limited (R); Q is open source.

mc.q: Which of the following behaviours may infringe intellectual property rights?
st: (1) Sending an email with a virus to a friend
(2) Hacking into an online bank account
(3) Posting a scanned newspaper on a personal web site
(4) Uploading a video of a TV programme to the Internet
mc.e: Copying newspaper and TV content breaks copyright; viruses and hacking are other crimes.

mc.q: Free online encyclopedias such as Wikipedia contain a huge number of articles. Which of the following statements about the online encyclopedias are correct?
st: (1) People can search the relevant articles for a topic quickly.
mc.e: Online encyclopedias are searchable and frequently updated, but the articles are still copyrighted.

mc.q: Ms Lee is a photographer. Mr Cheung downloads a lot of copyright photos from her web site and uses them in his tutorial school without her approval. What legal consequences are there of doing this?
st: (1) Mr Cheung needs to compensate Ms Lee.
(2) Mr Cheung commits a criminal offence.
(3) Mr Cheung needs to close down his tutorial school.
mc.e: Commercial use of copyright works without permission can lead to civil compensation and criminal liability, not forced closure.

mc.q: What is/are the appropriate measure(s) to take to protect the intellectual property rights of photos posted on the Internet?
mc.e: A digital watermark marks ownership of the image.

mc.q: A photographer posts his photos to a social media web site for the public to look at. Which of the following can be applied to the photo to protect his intellectual property?
mc.e: A digital watermark marks the photo's ownership.

mc.q: Why do people develop open source software?
st: (1) They want to earn more money from selling their software.
(2) They want more people to use their software.
(3) They want to own the copyright of the software.
mc.e: Open source is about wide use and sharing, not sales.

mc.q: Which of the following actions will most likely infringe copyright in Hong Kong?
o: Using peer-to-peer file sharing software to share personal videos
Broadcasting a street view live through a social media web site
Uploading TV programmes to a personal web site and sharing them with friends
Using peer-to-peer file sharing software to search for an audio file
mc.e: TV programmes are copyright works; uploading them without permission infringes.

mc.q: What is/are the major characteristic(s) of open source software?
st: (1) Developers can set the selling price.
(2) Users can change the source code.
(3) All functions of the software can be used during the trial period.
mc.e: Open source lets users read and modify the source code.

mc.q: What can Alice do when using open source software?
st: Seek approval from the software developer before using the software.
Amend the source code for her own use.
Amend the source code drastically and own the copyright of the entire software.
mc.e: Open source lets anyone use and modify the code without asking, but she cannot claim copyright of the whole software.

mc.q: Which of the following Internet activities are probably infringements of copyright?
st: Extracting a video from an old movie DVD and uploading it to the Internet
Drawing a picture and sharing it with friends using peer-to-peer (p2p) software
Downloading newspaper articles from the Internet and publishing a book containing them
mc.e: (1) and (3) reuse other people's work without permission. Sharing your own drawing is fine, even over p2p.

mc.q: John plays Internet games and uses social media all the time. Which of the following are likely the consequences of such indulgence in Internet activities?
st: A higher chance of having anxiety and attention problems
Infringement of copyright in Internet activities
mc.e: Too much screen time harms mental health and fitness. Heavy use does not by itself mean copyright infringement.

mc.q: Peter installs a software package on his computer. He also installs it on another computer. He does not infringe copyright because ________.
st: the license of the software package allows such installation
the two computers are located in different countries
the operating systems of the two computers are different
mc.e: Only the licence decides whether a second installation is allowed.

mc.q: Which of the following about the use of robots are correct?
st: Robots can follow working procedures accurately.
Robots can replace the work of all the employees.
Robots can take up dirty, dangerous jobs.
mc.e: Robots are accurate and can do dirty or dangerous work, but they cannot replace every employee.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the advantage(s) of using open source software over freeware?
st: It is easier to set up and use.
Users can improve the source code and share it in the community.
mc.e: Only open source lets users change and share the code. It is not always easier or cross-platform.

mc.q: Why do many companies prefer commercial software to open source software?
st: Open source software contains more software bugs.
Commercial software developers can provide better support.
Open source software cannot be modified by companies.
mc.e: Companies value vendor support. Open source is not necessarily buggier, and it can be modified.

mc.q: Mrs Lee does not allow her son to use Bit Torrent freeware on her home computer because
st: her son may download illegal software.
it is illegal to use the software.
his school does not install this software.
mc.e: BitTorrent itself is legal; the risk is downloading pirated material.

mc.q: Which of the following is not open source software?
mc.e: Internet Explorer is proprietary freeware, not open source.

mc.q: Which of the following statements about copyright is correct?
o: It is effective only if the author has a statement about copyright on his/her work.
It applies to computer software only.
The author must register his/her work to obtain copyright.
It applies automatically to the owner of the original work.
mc.e: In Hong Kong copyright arises automatically; no registration or notice needed.

mc.q: Which of the following actions may be seen as copyright infringement?
o: Broadcasting a school event with permission.
Downloading articles from an academic database.
Sending selfies to friends using peer-to-peer (P2P) software.
Uploading films to the cloud storage and sharing them with friends.
mc.e: Sharing copyrighted films without permission is unauthorised distribution (Internet piracy).
mc.ez: 未经许可分享电影属互联网盗版。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC1 (p.108)

mc.q: Janice takes the following actions on her work computer. Which of them is considered legal?
o: Buying a CD and using the music in an event promotional video.
Using peer-to-peer (P2P) software to download a movie for personal use.
Sending freeware to colleagues via a BT program.
Sharing a commercial software with friends via the cloud.
mc.e: Freeware may be copied and redistributed freely.
mc.ez: 免费软件可自由复制及分发。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC2 (p.108)

mc.q: Which may be considered copyright infringement? (1) Screenshot of a free online newspaper posted on social media (2) Using photos from an official website to sell a used product online (3) Photocopying one page of a 36-page recipe book for a school assignment (4) Removing the watermark from a copyrighted photo and uploading it to a personal website
mc.e: (3) is limited use for education (fair dealing); the others use works without permission.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC3 (p.108)

mc.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes copyright in Hong Kong?
o: Copyright owners cannot transfer their copyrights to others.
Copyright only protects high quality works.
Copyright owners are required to put a copyright symbol '©' on their work for a higher level of copyright protection.
mc.e: Copyright is given automatically when a work is completed; no registration or notice is needed.
mc.ez: 版权自动产生，毋须注册或声明。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC4 (p.108)

mc.q: Which of the following statements about freeware is correct?
o: Distribution of the software is not allowed.
The software is free to make copies.
The software is allowed to be installed on a single device only.
The source code is free to modify.
mc.e: Freeware: unlimited users, copying and redistribution allowed, no source code access.
mc.ez: 免费软件可复制，但不能改源码。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC5 (p.108)

mc.q: Ms Lee downloads an open source image editor. What can she do? (1) Edit posters for commercial purposes (2) Add her own code to the program (3) Send the modified version to her friends
mc.e: Open source is free for commercial use and may be modified and redistributed.
mc.ez: 开源可商用、修改及分发。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC6 (p.108)

mc.q: Which is/are the major characteristic(s) of freeware? (1) Free to use for non-commercial purposes (2) The developer can modify the source code (3) Users can access the source code (4) Users need permission from the copyright owner before using it
mc.e: Freeware is free to use (at least non-commercially); users cannot access the source code and need no extra permission.
mc.ez: 免费软件可免费使用，用户看不到源码。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC7 (p.108)

mc.q: Which can help prevent unauthorised distribution of digital images? (1) Digital watermark (2) Digital signature (3) Secure Socket Layer (SSL)
mc.e: Watermarks embed ownership/trace sources; signatures verify senders; SSL only encrypts transmission.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC8 (p.109)

mc.q: Peter writes a program on his own. Which are his rights as copyright owner? (1) Translate and publish it in another language (2) Charge a licence fee for the right to use it (3) Sell the copyright to another company (4) Transfer ownership of the software to others
mc.e: All are exclusive rights: adapt/translate, grant use for royalties, sell, transfer.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC9 (p.109)

mc.q: Reasons for developers to publish software as shareware? (1) Make money for authorising others to use it (2) Do not want to give up copyright (3) Want more people to improve the source code together (4) Want to attract more people to try it
mc.e: Improving source code together is a reason for open source, not shareware.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC10 (p.109)

mc.q: Which is/are the exception(s) to copyright infringement? (1) Scanning workbooks and distributing copies to students (2) Printing and distributing sheet music written in 1866 (3) Activating software on all school computers with a single-device licence key (4) Showing TV broadcasts in restaurants with permission from the copyright owner
mc.e: 1866 music's copyright has expired; (4) has permission. (1) and (3) are unauthorised copying.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC11 (p.109)

mc.q: Which use of copyrighted work is considered legal in Hong Kong?
o: Selling pirated products in the Lunar New Year Fair.
Buying an activation key with a cheaper price from a software pirate.
Sharing copies of lecture notes made by your school teacher with friends in other schools.
Photocopying one page from a reference book that cannot be borrowed for a school project.
mc.e: Copying one page for a school project is limited, fair educational use.
mc.ez: 影印一页作功课属公平处理。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC12 (p.109)

mc.q: What is the legal consequence of selling copies of your own HKDSE past papers on social media?
o: The Innovation and Technology Commission (ITC) will take legal action.
HKEAA can report the case to the Customs and Excise Department for further investigation.
Your action is considered a civil offence.
No legal consequence because copyright does not protect digital files on the Internet.
mc.e: HKEAA owns copyright of submitted work; selling pirated copies is a criminal matter handled by C&ED.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC13 (p.109)

mc.q: Cindy uploads photos without the watermark '© All rights reserved'. Which statement is correct?
o: Cindy owns the copyright without declaration.
The social media company will own the copyright.
Cindy has to register for copyright protection.
mc.e: Copyright is automatic; ideas are not protected, only their tangible expression.
mc.ez: 版权自动拥有，毋须声明。

mc.q: What is the legal consequence of sharing a commercial Chinese input software with friends via a cloud drive?
o: You may be liable to imprisonment.
Your action may be considered a criminal offence.
You may be sued for copyright infringement through a civil lawsuit.
You will need to pay fines to the Customs and Excise Department.
mc.e: The copyright owner can seek monetary compensation through a civil lawsuit.
mc.ez: 版权持有人可提出民事诉讼。

mc.q: Patrick bought cracked software at half the legal price. What is NOT a possible consequence?
o: His computer may be attacked because bug-fix updates cannot be installed.
The copyright owner will offer a customised free trial for Patrick.
The act violates intellectual property rights.
mc.e: Pirates get no support or offers from the owner.
mc.ez: 版权持有人不会给盗版用户试用。

mc.q: Peter posts photos of old housing estates online. Which actions are illegal? (1) A publisher uses the photos in a textbook (2) A teacher shows one photo in a lesson (3) A friend reposts them on social media (4) A friend prints a photo with his permission
mc.e: Only fair non-profit educational use is exempt; (4) has permission.
mc.ez: 只有非牟利教学豁免，(4)有许可。

mc.q: Which use is most likely to be fair dealing?
o: Distribute copies of HKDSE past papers to students without paying any fee.
Copy an entire article from a website into a school assignment.
Play a few minutes of a documentary to illustrate a historical event.
Show an entire film during an English lesson.
mc.e: Limited part used for instruction.

mc.q: Which is NOT considered copyright infringement in Hong Kong?
o: Uploading a travel vlog taken by you on a video sharing website.
Sharing your single-user streaming subscription account with friends.
Using copyrighted music for an advertisement competition without paying any fee.
Broadcasting gameplay on a live streaming platform.
mc.e: You own the copyright of your own vlog.
mc.ez: 自己拍的 vlog 版权属自己。

mc.q: HKEAA owns the copyright of all work submitted by candidates. Which is least likely to be infringement?
o: You share your SBA video submitted to HKEAA on social media.
You sell copies of your submitted answer scripts.
You write examination strategies according to your submitted answers.
You photocopy your submitted answer scripts and give them to friends.
