mc.e: Writing your own strategies uses ideas, not copies of the work.
mc.ez: 写自己的策略不涉复制作品。

mc.q: A tutor photocopies a whole book and distributes copies to students. What can the copyright holders do?
o: Complain to the Intellectual Property Department about the pirated copies.
Nothing, because it is for educational purposes.
Complain to the Customs and Excise Department about the pirated copies.
mc.e: C&ED takes criminal sanctions; copying a whole book is not fair dealing.

mc.q: George wants to use shareware X to edit vlogs. Disadvantage(s)? (1) Source code will be modified by others (2) Advanced features may be available only when you purchase (3) It is only free for the trial period (4) Technical support may not be provided
mc.e: Shareware has trial/feature limits; it usually does provide support.
mc.ez: 共享软件限时限功能，但有支援。

mc.q: Patrick installed video editing software free for educational use and now has a freelance job. What should he do first?
o: Read the licence agreement to check if it can be used for commercial purposes.
mc.e: Educational licences may forbid commercial use.
mc.ez: 先看授权是否容许商用。

mc.q: Which can protect IP from unauthorised use of videos posted on online streaming sites? (1) Digital signature (2) Avoid opening links from unknown users (3) Digital watermarks
mc.e: Watermarks prove ownership/trace copies; signatures verify the sender only.

mc.q: What is the legal consequence of selling cracked apps on online shopping platforms?
o: You will not be arrested unless the copyright holder complains.
The OGCIO processes copyright infringement complaints.
The Intellectual Property Department will take criminal sanctions.
Your action may be considered a criminal offence.
mc.e: Only C&ED takes criminal sanctions, even without a complaint.
mc.ez: 可构成刑事罪行，海关可主动执法。

mc.q: Intellectual property is best described as
o: any information found on the Internet
the hardware and software owned by a person
a set of separate intangible asset rights over creations of the intellect
physical goods produced by a company
mc.e: IP = creation of intellect; intangible asset rights.
mc.ez: 知识产权是一组无形财产权。

mc.q: Which type of intellectual property does NOT require registration in Hong Kong?
mc.e: Except for copyright, other IP types all require registration.

mc.q: The unique shape and curved edges of a new smartphone body are best protected by
mc.e: Registered design protects new and distinctive appearance.

mc.q: A mobile app's icon and name are best protected by
mc.e: Trademark: unique sign distinguishing products; examples include app name and icon.

mc.q: Which statement about patents is correct?
o: Computer programs can never be patented.
A computer program can be patented if it solves a technical problem.
Patents protect the appearance of a product.
mc.e: Book: computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem.
mc.ez: 解决技术问题的程序可获专利。

mc.q: What does the symbol ® indicate?
o: The work is in the public domain
mc.e: ® = registered trademark; ™ = trademark.

mc.q: A court held that selfies taken by a monkey are in the public domain because
o: only works created by humans are protected by copyright
the camera owner did not register them
mc.e: Only human-created works are protected.

mc.q: In general, copyright in Hong Kong lasts until
o: 50 years after the death of the creator
mc.e: 50 years after the creator's death.

mc.q: Which is protected as a 'typographical arrangement of a published edition'?
o: The interface layout of a published website
mc.e: Table 3.1 example.

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT protected by copyright?
o: The idea of making a photo-sharing app
mc.e: Ideas are not protected; only their tangible expression.

mc.q: Which is NOT an exclusive right of a copyright owner?
o: Stopping others from criticising the work in a review
Passing the copyright to others in a will
mc.e: Criticism and review is fair dealing.

mc.q: Payment received by a copyright owner for granting others the right to use the work is called
mc.e: Royalties (版權費).

mc.q: A picture is licensed under CC BY-NC. Which use is NOT allowed?
o: Showing it in class with credit
Using it in a school project with credit
Printing it on T-shirts for sale
Sharing it with credit on a personal blog
mc.e: NC forbids commercial use.

mc.q: Under a CC licence with 'SA', a user who adapts the work must
o: share the new work under the same licence
mc.e: Share-alike.

mc.q: Which is an example of Internet piracy?
o: Downloading Firefox from its official site
Streaming a song on a licensed music app
Buying a cracked membership of software on an online shopping site
mc.e: Buying cracked versions/memberships is piracy.

mc.q: Which is a security risk of using pirated software?
mc.e: Pirated software may carry malware and cause data breaches.

mc.q: Which is an ECONOMIC impact of copyright infringement?
mc.e: Fig 3.3 chain ends with lower tax revenue.

mc.q: The maximum penalty for selling a pirated copy under the Copyright Ordinance is
mc.e: Book figure.

mc.q: A shop sells 4 pirated DVDs. What is the maximum total fine?
Which government department takes criminal sanctions against copyright and trademark infringement?
mc.e: Only C&ED.

EAC1.tz: 使用 SQL 管理数据

k: A database is a collection of structured data in a computer system that facilitates the storage and retrieval of data. Database management includes: retrieval of information ; modification, deletion and insertion of data ; modification of the database structure .

items.t: Paper database vs digital database (library example)
items.tz: 纸本数据库 vs 数码数据库（图书馆例子）
k: Data can be searched by the system in a relatively short time instead of manually; data is stored in the online system , so it is easy to update and back up and can be accessed by multiple users at the same time .

items.tz: 数据库结构：栏位、记录、数据表
k: Field: a single piece of information. Record: a complete set of fields. Table: a collection of records.

items.tz: 设计数据库（DVD 租赁活动）
k: A poor database design may lead to problems such as causing data to become unreliable or inaccurate; the performance of the database may be degraded, and its flexibility may also be lost.
We often use a database management system (DBMS) to help us manage databases. e.g. Microsoft Access (with GUI), MySQL (without GUI).
We use queries to filter, sort, summarise, update or delete data in a DBMS. These queries are written in Structured Query Language (SQL). WHERE filters records; HAVING filters groups.

items.t: SHOW DATABASES and the data hierarchy
k: SHOW DATABASES gets a list of the databases in MySQL. In a DBMS, there can be multiple databases.
Whenever we start MySQL, we must specify which database to use before manipulating any data from tables. USE database
To store data, we should create a table inside the database first. CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), NAME CHAR(16), CLASS CHAR(2), CNO INT)
SHOW TABLES gets a list of the tables in the current database.
Semicolon indicates the termination of statements. MySQL is case insensitive most of the time … it is a good practice that we write our SQL in a consistent way.

items.tz: 命名规则与反引号（增润）
k: We may enclose names containing symbols, digits and whitespaces with a backquote (`) to prevent errors. Quotation marks (') are used to enclose strings and dates.
State the error precisely, e.g. 'The data type of each field is not specified.' / 'The closing bracket is missing.'
When creating a table, we have to define the data type of each field. Dates in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD' . Real numbers are usually stored as floating point numbers.
When character strings, date and time are input into tables, they should be enclosed in single or double quotation marks.
CHAR() occupies a fixed size of storage space. VARCHAR() occupies a varied size of storage space , but spends extra storage space for the length information and has a slightly worse performance .
If numbers with leading zeros are stored as numeric values, i.e. INT or FLOAT, the leading zeros will be removed. We should store such numbers as character strings, i.e. CHAR() or VARCHAR().

items.t: Choosing data types to minimise storage (Example 1.1)
items.tz: 选择数据类型以节省空间（Example 1.1）
k: Justify each choice: 'EID has no letters or leading zeros, so INT uses less storage than a string.' 'FEE has a decimal part, so FLOAT.'
If you arrange the values in the same order as the fields in the table, you do not have to specify the fields. If you specify the fields, you can arrange the values in any order.
We may leave a field empty during insertion. In such a case, this field will have a NULL value, i.e. a lack of value. Not all fields are allowed to have a NULL value.
When the field value is 0, it is not NULL. It has a data type, number. NULL has no data type.
We may insert more than one record at a time. Use comma to separate the records.
The SQL result is not the table. Using SELECT FROM to retrieve data never changes the data in the actual table.
When retrieving data, we may set criteria to filter records.

items.tz: ORDER BY 排序：ASC 与 DESC
k: Data can be sorted in either ascending order (ASC) or descending order (DESC). The default sorting order is ascending. Character strings are sorted in alphabetical order.
We may filter duplicated results by using DISTINCT.

items.t: Learning SQL step by step (The Secret of Learning SQL)
items.tz: 逐步学 SQL（The Secret of Learning SQL）
k: For 'state the purpose', describe the result in plain words, e.g. 'To list the names of students in class 1B in ascending order of class number.'

items.t: The secret of learning SQL: three steps
items.tz: 学好 SQL 的秘诀：三个步骤
k: purpose questions want what the result means, e.g. "List the name of each shop and the highest price of its products." , not a word-by-word reading of the code.
UPDATE changes data in existing records. To update multiple fields, separate the assignments with commas.

items.t: Use a unique field as the criterion
k: SID is an identity number, which is supposed to be unique for each student. Different students may share the same name. We risk updating the wrong student if we use NAME in the criterion.

items.t: Danger: UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE
items.tz: 危险：UPDATE / DELETE 没有 WHERE
k: UPDATE usually comes with a WHERE clause, otherwise it will update the whole table. Using DELETE without a WHERE clause simply deletes all records from the table.
DELETE FROM removes records that match the criterion.
Since one careless mistake is capable of wiping out or drastically changing a table, it is important to make a backup from time to time so that we may roll back the database to its previous state.
DROP TABLE deletes the whole table from the database. Once a table is deleted, all its records, if any, will be deleted as well.
Once a database is deleted, all its tables, if any, will be deleted as well.
Give reasons: 'PID contains letters, so character type.' 'STOCK cannot have a decimal part, so integer.' 'PRICE usually has a decimal part, so real number.'

To maintain data integrity and validate data input, we should set constraints for a table. Primary key is a field or a combination of fields that store unique data for every record. The value stored in the primary key field cannot be empty, i.e. NULL.
HKID is chosen as the primary key because it is unique for each citizen, available for every citizen, and does not change.
Constraint PRIMARY KEY prevents a field from storing duplicated values or NULL by any means, including insertion and updating.
We may set a combination of fields as the primary key of the table. Such a primary key is called a composite key. Every combination of the fields must be unique.

items.t: Foreign key: host table and parent table
items.tz: 外键：host table 与 parent table
k: Foreign keys are used to show the relationship between records in two tables. A foreign key in a table X is always the primary key of another table Y. Table X is the host table, while table Y is the parent table.
FOREIGN KEY (CLASS) REFERENCES CLASSLIST(CLASSNAME)

items.tz: FOREIGN KEY 的效果（参照完整性）
k: Constraint FOREIGN KEY prevents a field from storing a value that does not exist in the corresponding field of the parent table by any means, including insertion, update and deletion.
Constraints are useful for data validation and shorten our time for data management.

items.t: PRIMARY KEY vs UNIQUE vs NOT NULL; combining constraints
items.tz: PRIMARY KEY、UNIQUE、NOT NULL 比较与组合
k: PRIMARY KEY ≈ UNIQUE + NOT NULL , and it is the field used to identify records. We may apply more than one keyword to a field, as well as apply a keyword to more than one field.
AUTO_INCREMENT is a feature that can be applied to a primary key field. The value will be automatically assigned, starting from 1.
A redundant field stores data that can be derived from other fields or found in another table. e.g. 'GID is redundant because it can be derived from PCODE and GCODE.'
After creating a table, its structure can still be altered. Some of the alterations may result in data loss so we should proceed with caution.
Beware that the newly added field contains no data if it does not have a default value.
ALTER TABLE STUDENT RENAME COLUMN LAME TO NAME

When changing the data type of a field, the DBMS will also try to convert the data type of all values stored in that field. Such a conversion may result in data loss. If there is any value that cannot be converted properly, the change of data type will fail.
Once a field is deleted, all its values will be deleted as well. Adding back a field with the same name does not help.

items.t: Adding and dropping a primary key
k: When adding constraints, all existing data must not violate the constraints to be added, otherwise such an operation will fail. Since a table must not have more than one primary key, the name of the primary key field is not specified when dropping it.

items.t: Misconception: adding a new PRIMARY KEY field to a filled table
items.tz: 误解：在已有数据的表加新主键栏位
k: The PRIMARY KEY constraint forbids the value of a primary key to be NULL or duplicated ; all existing records would get the same value (NULL/0), so the statement cannot be executed.

items.t: Adding and dropping foreign keys; SHOW CREATE TABLE
items.tz: 新增与删除外键；SHOW CREATE TABLE
k: Since there can be more than one foreign key in a table, when dropping a foreign key, we need to specify which one to drop.
Adding fails if existing data violates the constraint ; e.g. ADD CHECK (CNO > 0) fails if some CNO is 0 or negative.
Character strings are sorted in alphabetical order , so Regular, Bronze, Silver, Gold are not sorted by level; storing the type as an integer ID referring to MTYPELIST solves this.

items.t: Numbers stored as strings sort wrongly
items.tz: 数字存成字符串会排错
k: SCORE1 is a character string, so it is sorted in alphabetical (character) order, not numeric order.
A score of 0 is a valid score. If the default were 0, an absent player could not be distinguished from a present player who scored 0.

items.t: Managing data using SQL cheat sheet

mc.q: Which statement can be executed without error?
mc.e: Database names should not contain spaces.

mc.q: Which statement can be executed without error?
o: create table shop (id int, name char(30))
create table shop id int, name char(30)
mc.e: Every field needs a data type and the list must be in brackets after the table name.

mc.q: A field EID ranges from 0 to 999,999 with no leading zeros. To minimise storage it should be
mc.e: An integer (4 bytes) is smaller than a 6-character string.

mc.q: Which statement shows all fields of finished events in EVENT (FINISHED is Boolean)?
o: SELECT * FROM EVENT ORDER BY FINISHED
mc.e: Filter with WHERE FINISHED = 1 (or TRUE).

mc.q: Which statement sets product BA1100 as out of stock?
o: UPDATE PRODUCT SET STOCK = 0 WHERE PID = 'BA1100'
mc.e: Out of stock means STOCK = 0 for that PID.

mc.q: In HKCITIZEN, why is EMAIL not suitable as the primary key?
o: Not everyone has an email address, so it may be NULL, and it may change
Emails cannot be stored as VARCHAR
mc.e: A primary key must be available for everyone and should not change.

mc.q: In GAME, GID is made of PCODE + GCODE. Which field is redundant?
mc.e: GID repeats PCODE and GCODE; PCODE is needed as a foreign key, so drop GID.

mc.q: BOOKCLUB has over 500 records. Why does ALTER TABLE BOOKCLUB ADD MEMID INT PRIMARY KEY fail?
o: INT cannot be a primary key
ADD cannot be used with constraints
A table cannot have more than 500 records
MEMID would be NULL/0 for all records, but a primary key cannot be NULL or duplicated
mc.e: Existing records would all share the same empty/default value.

mc.q: USER.MTYPE values Regular, Bronze, Silver, Gold sorted by ORDER BY MTYPE give
mc.e: Strings are sorted alphabetically.

mc.q: PLAYER has SCORE1 CHAR(2) with values '7','11','1','-4'. ORDER BY SCORE1 DESC puts first
mc.e: As strings, '7' > '11' because '7' > '1'.
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch1 Chapter Exercise Q3(b) (p.56)

mc.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three database management tasks listed in the textbook?
o: Retrieval of information from a database
Modification, deletion and insertion of data
mc.e: The three tasks are retrieval; modification, deletion and insertion of data; and modification of the database structure.
mc.ez: 数据库管理三项工作不包括网络加密。

mc.q: In a database, a single piece of information such as a student's class is a
mc.e: A field is a single piece of information.

mc.q: A complete set of fields describing one student is a
mc.e: A record is a complete set of fields.

mc.q: Which is correct about the data hierarchy?
o: A table is a collection of records
A database is a collection of fields only
mc.e: Database > table > record > field.

mc.q: Which is an advantage of an online library management system over checkout cards and log books?
o: Librarians must copy data into log books
Data can be searched by the system in a relatively short time
mc.e: The system searches data quickly instead of manually.
mc.ez: 系统可在短时间内搜寻。

mc.q: Which DBMS described in the textbook has a graphical user interface?
mc.e: Microsoft Access is a DBMS with a GUI; MySQL is used without a GUI (unless via a tool such as MySQL Workbench).

mc.q: Which keyword is used for summarisation?
mc.e: Table 1.1: summarisation uses GROUP BY.

mc.q: Which may be a result of a poor database design?
mc.e: A poor design may make data unreliable or inaccurate, degrade performance and lose flexibility.
mc.ez: 设计差令数据不可靠、不准确。

mc.q: Which statement lists the databases in MySQL?
mc.e: The command is SHOW DATABASES (plural).

mc.q: What is wrong with: CREATE TABLE HOTEL (HID INT, HNAME CHAR(40), HADDRESS CHAR(40)
o: Field names must be lower case
mc.e: The bracket opened before HID is never closed.

mc.q: A user types SHOW DATABASES and presses Enter, but MySQL gives no response. Why?
o: The statement has not been terminated with a semicolon
mc.e: MySQL will not respond until it sees a semicolon.

mc.q: Before manipulating data in tables after starting MySQL, we must
mc.e: We must specify which database to use with USE.

mc.q: Which pair of symbols is correct?
o: Backquotes enclose strings; quotation marks enclose names
Backquotes enclose names with spaces; quotation marks enclose strings and dates
mc.e: `name with space` vs 'string value'.
mc.ez: 反引号包名称，单引号包字符串和日期。

mc.q: In CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID CHAR(5), ...), CHAR(5) means
o: a string of 5 characters at most
mc.e: CHAR(5) means a string of 5 characters at most.
mc.ez: 最多 5 个字符的字符串。

mc.q: A field stores 4-digit book codes that may begin with zeros, e.g. 0472. The best data type is
mc.e: Numbers with leading zeros must be stored as strings, otherwise the zeros are removed.

mc.q: Value '000123' is stored in an INT field. What is stored?
mc.e: Leading zeros are removed when stored as a number.

mc.q: Which data type is most suitable for whether an event has finished (1 or 0)?
mc.e: Only 0 or 1, so Boolean.

mc.q: Which is the correct date value format for a DBMS?
mc.e: Dates are written in quotes as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

mc.q: Without quotes, the value 2036-04-15 inserted into a numeric context evaluates to
mc.e: It is read as the subtraction 2036 - 4 - 15 = 2017.

mc.q: Which statement about CHAR and VARCHAR is correct?
o: VARCHAR(100) storing 5 characters uses the same space as 100 characters
CHAR(100) storing 5 characters uses the same space as 100 characters
CHAR needs extra space for length information
VARCHAR has better performance than CHAR
mc.e: CHAR occupies a fixed size; VARCHAR uses extra space for the length and is slightly slower.

k: SQL operators are used in an expression to help us modify or filter data in a database.

items.t: Evaluating criteria with a truth table
k: draw a table with one row per record and one column per condition. Say: "the record is selected only if the whole criterion is TRUE" .
"* and / are performed before + and -; brackets ( ) change the order."
"The SELECT statement only displays the calculated values; the data stored in the table is not changed."

items.t: Using operators in UPDATE, WHERE and DELETE
items.tz: 在 UPDATE / WHERE / DELETE 中用运算符
k: "Use UPDATE ... SET to change the stored data; SELECT only displays the result."
state the rearranged formula, then write the statement; use brackets for the whole denominator .

items.tz: 延伸：用 CONCAT() 连接字符串
k: answer with the textbook's MySQL syntax: CONCAT(...) .
"Use date functions (e.g. TIMESTAMPDIFF) instead of + / - for calculations between dates."
read the boundary words carefully: "at least 20" includes 20, so use >= .
"Strings are compared character by character in dictionary order." Compare data of the same type .
"When a string is compared with a number, the string is converted to a number."
"AND returns TRUE only if all criteria are TRUE; OR returns TRUE if at least one criterion is TRUE; NOT reverses the result."

items.t: Order of logical operators: NOT > AND > OR
k: "Logical operators are evaluated in the order NOT, AND, OR. Use parentheses to make the order clear."

items.tz: OR 漏括号的典型错误
k: "Add parentheses around the OR conditions because AND has a higher priority than OR."
"IN is used to select more than one value."
"BETWEEN ... AND selects values within a specific range inclusively."
"LIKE is used to select character strings that follow a specific pattern."
count underscores carefully: each _ represents exactly one character .
"Include the space after the surname so that other surnames such as Ngai are not selected."

items.t: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL
items.tz: IS NULL 与 IS NOT NULL
k: "IS NULL / IS NOT NULL are used to separate records with and without NULL values."
"0 is not NULL. NULL means no value; it does not even have a data type."

items.t: DISTINCT with criteria and the Example 2.2 method
items.tz: DISTINCT 配合条件；例题 2.2 方法
k: when the question says "without duplicates" or "list the different ..." , use DISTINCT .

items.t: Rewriting criteria in a shorter way
k: when NOT moves inside brackets, AND becomes OR and OR becomes AND .

items.tz: SQL 在商业分析中的应用
k: "Business analysts use SQL to filter and summarise data to discover buying patterns and support business decisions."
"SQL functions are used in an expression to help us analyse data."
"MID(str, start_num, num_char) returns num_char characters starting from the start_num-th character."

items.tz: 取最后 n 个字符
k: show the start position: LENGTH(UID) − 4 + 1 = LENGTH(UID) − 3 .

items.t: Cleaning data with TRIM, UPPER and LOWER in UPDATE
items.tz: 用 UPDATE 配合 TRIM / UPPER / LOWER 清理数据
k: "Use UPDATE ... SET field = TRIM(field) to remove leading and trailing spaces from the stored data."

items.t: Validating and comparing data with text functions
items.tz: 用文字函数检查和比较数据
k: state which part of the string you take and why, e.g. "the first character of CLASS represents the grade" .

items.t: Nesting functions: removing an unwanted ending
items.tz: 嵌套函数：删去结尾多余字符串
k: "Functions can be nested; the inner function is evaluated first."
"MONTH(DOB) * 100 + DAY(DOB) converts the date into an integer MMDD so that a range can be compared regardless of the year."
"Aggregation functions help us summarise data."
"COUNT(*) counts all records, while COUNT(field) does not count NULL values."
"GROUP BY categorises the records before the aggregation functions summarise each category."

items.t: Non-grouped fields should not be selected directly
items.tz: 非分组字段不应直接 SELECT
k: "Only columns with aggregation functions (or grouping fields) are summarised data."
"HAVING is followed by criteria and is used to filter the categories after grouping."

items.tz: WHERE 与 HAVING 的分别
k: "WHERE is used to filter the records before categorisation, while HAVING is used to filter the categories after categorisation."

items.t: Aggregation functions cannot be used in WHERE
items.tz: 聚合函数不能放在 WHERE
k: "Aggregation functions cannot be used in the WHERE clause; use HAVING instead."
e.g. "average credit of members of each gender in each member type" → GROUP BY TYPEID, SEX .

items.t: COUNT and grouping by a function
k: "COUNT(*) counts the number of records in each group."
"MAX/MIN return the largest/smallest value; for dates, the latest/earliest date."

items.t: SELECT NAME, MAX(SCORE) does not find the top student
k: "Only the columns with aggregation functions are summarised data; NAME is not related to MAX(SCORE)."

items.t: Enrichment: finding the top record with LIMIT or a subquery
items.tz: 延伸：用 LIMIT 或子查询找最高分学生
k: "The subquery method lists all records with the highest value, while LIMIT 1 shows only one even if there is a tie."
"SUM returns the total and AVG returns the average of the non-NULL values."

items.tz: 计算平均前先排除记录
k: "Use WHERE to exclude the record before categorisation so that it does not affect the average."

items.t: Putting it together: WHERE + GROUP BY + HAVING
k: write clauses in order WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → ORDER BY .

items.t: Review: primary key, foreign key and ALTER TABLE
items.tz: 复习：主键、外键与 ALTER TABLE
k: "TYPEID is a foreign key in MEMBER which refers to the primary key ID of MTYPE."

items.t: Activity: making your own sample data
k: in "explain" questions, give a concrete record that would be wrongly included or excluded.
use these exact terms when asked to "state the type of" an operator or function.

items.t: SQL operators and functions cheat sheet
items.tz: SQL 运算符与函数速查表

mc.q: Which statement correctly converts every WEIGHT in TEMP from kg to pounds (×2.2) and stores it?
o: ALTER TABLE TEMP SET WEIGHT = WEIGHT * 2.2
mc.e: Stored data is changed with UPDATE ... SET.

mc.q: Given s = ½at², which SET clause correctly stores the acceleration a?
mc.e: a = 2s / t². '/ TTIME * TTIME' cancels out.

mc.q: Which statement deletes records whose WEIGHT was wrongly stored as the negative of SID?
o: DELETE FROM TEMP WHERE SID - WEIGHT
DELETE FROM TEMP WHERE SID = WEIGHT
mc.e: The minus sign can be used as a negative sign.

mc.q: 'Employees who have worked for at least 20 years' should be written as...
mc.e: 'At least' includes 20.

mc.q: Which criterion lists team A, C or E members with more than 10 leaves?
o: TEAM = 'A' OR TEAM = 'C' OR TEAM = 'E' AND LEAVE > 10
mc.e: Without brackets, AND binds only to TEAM = 'E'.
mc.ez: 不加括号时 AND 只作用于 TEAM='E'，用 IN 最安全。

mc.q: Which is equivalent to CLASS <> '1B' AND CLASS <> '2C'?
mc.e: NOT can be placed before IN.
mc.ez: NOT 可放在 IN 前。

mc.q: Which is equivalent to NOT SCORE1 BETWEEN 60 AND 80?
mc.e: Outside the inclusive range.

mc.q: Which pattern finds book names (BN) containing at least two 't'?
mc.e: '%tt%' needs them next to each other.
mc.ez: '%tt%' 要求两个 t 相连。

mc.q: Which pattern finds names whose second-to-last character is 't' (e.g. 'Memento')?
mc.e: t followed by exactly one character.

mc.q: Names start with the surname followed by a space. Why is ENAME LIKE 'Ng%' wrong for 'surname Ng'?
o: It also matches surnames such as Ngai
mc.e: Use 'Ng %' with a space.

mc.q: Which criterion finds employees not assigned to a team?
mc.e: Use IS NULL; = NULL returns nothing.

mc.q: Which is a shorter way to write NOT DOB < '2013-05-05'?
mc.e: NOT < becomes >=.

mc.q: Which is equivalent to SCORE2 >= SCORE1 AND SCORE2 <= SCORE3?
mc.e: BETWEEN accepts fields as the two ends.
mc.ez: BETWEEN 的两端可以是字段。

mc.q: Using MOVIE data, which directors are output by SELECT DNAME FROM MOVIE WHERE MNAME LIKE 'The Man_%'? Names: The Manhunter (Ada Kwong), The Manic (Bill Smith), The Man on Fire (Cheve Lee), The Man (Ada Kwong).
o: Ada Kwong, Bill Smith, Cheve Lee, Ada Kwong
Ada Kwong, Bill Smith, Cheve Lee
mc.e: 'The Man_%' needs at least one character after 'The Man', so 'The Man' itself is excluded. 'The Man on Fire' matches (_ = space).
mc.ez: 'The Man' 后至少要多一个字符；空格也算字符。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch2 Exercise Q3(b) (p.101), adapted

mc.q: UID values have different lengths. Which expression gives the last four characters?
mc.e: Start = LENGTH − 4 + 1.

mc.q: For FCODE = '123456', what is MID(FCODE, LENGTH(FCODE) - 2, 2)?
mc.e: Start at 4, take 2.
mc.ez: 由第 4 个字符起取 2 个。

mc.q: An administrator wants to permanently remove leading and trailing spaces from USERNAME. Which is correct?
mc.e: SELECT does not change data.

mc.q: Which statement finds the number of unwanted spaces at the start and end of FNAME?
mc.e: Original length minus trimmed length.
mc.ez: 原长减去 TRIM 后的长度。

mc.q: Users with an 8-digit PHONE that has missing digits are found by...
o: WHERE LENGTH(PHONE) <> 8 OR PHONE IS NOT NULL
mc.e: Check the length.

mc.q: Which criterion finds dates of birth between 08-23 and 09-22 of any year?
mc.e: Combine month and day into one integer.
mc.ez: 把月日合成整数再比较。

mc.q: Which criterion selects dates containing at least one digit 8 in the month or day?
mc.e: Month August, or day 8, 18 or 28.

mc.q: Contestants born between 2010 and 2015 inclusive belong to age group 1. Which UPDATE is correct?
o: SELECT AGID = 1 FROM CONTESTANT WHERE YEAR(DOB) IN (2010, 2015)
UPDATE CONTESTANT SET AGID = 1 WHERE YEAR(DOB) > 2010 AND YEAR(DOB) < 2015
UPDATE CONTESTANT SET AGID = 1 WHERE YEAR(DOB) BETWEEN 2010 AND 2015
UPDATE CONTESTANT SET AGID = 1 WHERE DOB BETWEEN 2010 AND 2015
mc.e: Use YEAR() and inclusive BETWEEN.
mc.ez: 用 YEAR() 和包含两端的 BETWEEN。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch2 Exercise Q1(a) (p.99), adapted

mc.q: Which finds the latest registration date for each member type?
o: SELECT TYPEID, COUNT(REGDATE) FROM MEMBER GROUP BY TYPEID
SELECT TYPEID, MAX(REGDATE) FROM MEMBER GROUP BY TYPEID
SELECT TYPEID, MIN(REGDATE) FROM MEMBER GROUP BY TYPEID
mc.e: Latest date = MAX.

mc.q: Which finds the character length of the longest product name?
mc.e: MAX(PNAME) is the alphabetically last name, not the longest.
mc.ez: MAX(PNAME) 是字典序最大，不是最长。

mc.q: Warehouse A has (PRICE 13.9, STOCK 216) and (PRICE 62.9, STOCK 193). What is SUM(PRICE * STOCK) for A?
To count discontinued phones in PHONE (DISC is Boolean), use...
o: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM PHONE WHERE DISC = TRUE
mc.e: Filter with WHERE then COUNT(*). COUNT(DISC) counts all non-NULL values, TRUE or FALSE.
mc.ez: 先 WHERE 再 COUNT(*)；COUNT(DISC) 会把 FALSE 也数进去。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch2 Exercise Q2(c) (p.100), adapted

mc.q: Which is a correct primary key for PRODUCT(CAT, SN, PNAME, PRICE, WAREHOUSE, STOCK) given data (FD03,261,...) and (DI05,261,...)?
mc.e: SN repeats across categories; together they are unique.
mc.ez: SN 会重复，CAT+SN 合起来唯一。

mc.q: In MEMBER(NAME, TYPEID, MEMID, ...) with MTYPE(ID, NAME), TYPEID is...
o: a foreign key referring to MTYPE.ID
mc.e: TYPEID links to MTYPE.ID.

mc.q: TEAM totals: X 8, Y 5, Z 6. Output of ... GROUP BY TEAM HAVING TOTAL > 5 where TOTAL = SUM(EGG)?
mc.e: Only totals larger than 5.
mc.ez: 只保留总数大于 5 的组。
mc.src: Textbook EA Ch2 Chapter Summary (p.99), adapted

mc.q: SQL operators are mainly used in an expression to help us...
o: modify or filter data in a database
mc.e: Definition from the textbook.
mc.ez: 运算符用来修改或筛选数据。

items.t: Key roles in the database industry
items.tz: 数据库行业的主要职位
k: match the key duty word to the role: security / performance → DBA ; design / queries / applications → developer ; supervise / projects → manager ; trends / insights → analyst .

items.t: Why store data in multiple tables?
items.tz: 为什么把数据分成多个表储存
k: Storing data in multiple tables linked with foreign keys makes it easier to maintain data consistency and saves data storage.

items.tz: 多对多关系：中间表 SC
k: A student may join as many clubs as they want without adding duplicated data to STUDENT.
The result of INNER JOIN includes only the records with matching values in both tables.
The result of LEFT JOIN includes all records from the left table and the matched records from the right table; unmatched fields are NULL.
The result of RIGHT JOIN includes all records from the right table and the matched records from the left table.
The result of FULL JOIN includes all records from both tables; fields without a match are NULL.

items.t: Comparing INNER, LEFT, RIGHT and FULL JOIN
k: Outer joins (LEFT/RIGHT/FULL) keep unmatched records and fill missing fields with NULL; INNER JOIN discards unmatched records.

items.t: Selecting, filtering and sorting joined records
items.tz: 对连接结果选取、过滤和排序
k: After joining, records can be filtered with WHERE and sorted with ORDER BY using fields from any of the joined tables.
Table aliases shorten statements and distinguish fields with the same name; column aliases give meaningful headings to result columns.

items.t: Summarising joined data: GROUP BY and HAVING
k: GROUP BY groups the joined records; HAVING sets conditions on groups (aggregate values), while WHERE sets conditions on individual records.
Use an outer join on the side whose records must all be listed; choose the foreign key that matches the meaning of the question.

items.t: Derived fields and COUNT(field) vs COUNT(*)
items.tz: 衍生字段与 COUNT(字段) vs COUNT(*)
k: Values that can be calculated should not be stored, to avoid data inconsistency. After an outer join, count a field from the other table (NULL for unmatched rows), not COUNT(*).

items.tz: 连接后 WHERE 与 HAVING 的分别
k: WHERE filters records before grouping; HAVING filters groups after grouping and may contain aggregate functions.
An equi-join lists tables in FROM and matches them with an equality condition in WHERE; its result is the same as INNER JOIN.
NATURAL JOIN joins tables on all fields with the same name, and shows each common field once.
A self join joins a table to itself; two different aliases must be used so that the table is treated as two tables.

items.t: Self join for pairing: removing self-pairs and duplicates
items.tz: 用自连接配对：去掉自己配自己和重复
k: Add s1.ID < s2.ID to avoid pairing a record with itself and to avoid duplicated pairs.
To join n tables, n − 1 join conditions are needed; the linking table connects the other two tables.
GROUP_CONCAT() combines the values of a field in each group into one string.

items.t: Example 3.2: three tables and two copies of one table
items.tz: 例 3.2：三个表及同一表的两份
k: When the same table plays two roles (member and leader), include it twice with different aliases.
CROSS JOIN combines every record of one table with every record of another table; the number of records is the product of the two numbers of records.

items.t: CROSS JOIN in practice: buyers and sellers
items.tz: CROSS JOIN 应用：买家与卖家
k: CROSS JOIN is used when there is no relationship between the tables but every combination needs to be evaluated.

items.t: Subquery: a query inside another query
k: A subquery is a query nested inside another SQL statement; its result is used by the main query, e.g. as a condition.
An aggregate function returns one value for the whole group, so it cannot be selected together with a non-grouped field; use a subquery to find the record with the maximum value.

items.t: IN and NOT IN with a subquery
items.tz: IN 和 NOT IN 子查询
k: IN returns TRUE if the value matches any value in the result of the subquery; NOT IN returns TRUE if it matches none of them.

items.t: Subqueries in INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE
items.tz: 在 INSERT、UPDATE、DELETE 中使用子查询
k: A subquery can be used in the WHERE clause of UPDATE and DELETE statements, and INSERT INTO … SELECT inserts the result of a query into a table.
EXISTS returns TRUE if the subquery returns at least one record. A correlated subquery refers to a field of the main query and is evaluated once for each record of the main query.

items.t: NOT EXISTS and the NOT IN NULL trap
items.tz: NOT EXISTS 与 NOT IN 的 NULL 陷阱
k: NOT EXISTS returns TRUE if the subquery returns no records. If the result of a NOT IN subquery contains NULL, no record will be returned.
ANY returns TRUE if the comparison is TRUE for at least one value returned by the subquery.
ALL returns TRUE if the comparison is TRUE for all values returned by the subquery.
A join returns one record per matching combination, so DISTINCT may be needed; a subquery only tests each record of the main query once.

items.t: The main query cannot retrieve data from a subquery
items.tz: 主查询不能取用子查询的字段
k: The main query cannot retrieve data from the subquery; tables must be joined in the main query if their fields are to be displayed.

items.t: Correlated subqueries: comparing with the outer row
items.tz: 相关子查询：与外层的行比较
k: A correlated subquery uses a field of the main query, so it is evaluated for each record of the main query.

items.t: 'Does not have': use NOT IN, not <>
k: To find records that do not have a value, use NOT IN / NOT EXISTS with a subquery that finds the records that have it.
COUNT(DISTINCT field) counts the number of different non-NULL values; the statement counts the number of different cat breeds within each hotel.

items.t: Join vs subquery: rewriting between them
items.tz: 连接 vs 子查询：互相改写
k: A join is needed when fields from more than one table are displayed; a subquery is suitable when the condition depends on the result of another query.
UNION combines the results of two queries and removes duplicated records; the queries must have the same number of fields with compatible data types.

items.t: WHERE and ORDER BY in combined results
items.tz: 合并结果中的 WHERE 和 ORDER BY
k: A WHERE clause only applies to its own SELECT statement; ORDER BY is placed at the end and sorts the combined result.

items.tz: 连接表 vs 合并结果
k: Joining tables combines fields of related records; set operators combine the records of query results with the same structure.
UNION ALL combines the results of two queries without removing duplicated records.
INTERSECT returns the records that exist in the results of both queries.
EXCEPT returns the records in the result of the first query that do not exist in the result of the second query.

items.t: Summary of the four set operators
k: All set operators require the queries to have the same number of fields with compatible data types.

items.t: Enrichment: selecting data from results; several set operators
items.tz: 增润：从结果中再查询；多个集合运算
k: A combined result can be treated as a table by giving it an alias, so that data can be selected from it.
Choose the set operator by the meaning: either → UNION, both → INTERSECT, only the first → EXCEPT, every occurrence → UNION ALL.
A view is a virtual table based on the result of a SELECT statement. It does not store data, and it simplifies SQL statements for frequently retrieved data.
CREATE VIEW view_name AS SELECT … creates a view; calculated fields should be given aliases.

items.tz: 增润：对聚合结果再聚合
k: An aggregate function cannot summarise the result of another aggregate function directly; treat the aggregated result as a table (or a view) first.

items.t: A view does not store data: no manual updates
items.tz: 视图不储存数据：不用手动更新
k: A view refers to data from other tables or views, thus does not need manual updates.

items.t: Views can miss records: COUNTCLUB and Dio
items.tz: 视图可能漏记录：COUNTCLUB 与 Dio
k: A view built only from the linking table misses records with no match; use an outer join from the main table and count a field that is NULL for unmatched records.

items.t: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW and views built on views
items.tz: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW 及以视图建视图
k: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW modifies the structure of an existing view; a view can refer to other views.
If the tables or views referred to by a view are deleted, the view no longer works.
A view simplifies SQL statements and needs no manual updates because it refers to data in other tables.
An index allows the DBMS to perform binary search on the indexed field to speed up the data retrieval process.
It takes time for the DBMS to update the index and storage space to store it, so only frequently searched fields should be indexed.
CREATE INDEX index_name ON table_name (field_name) creates an index on a field; DROP INDEX removes it.
An index speeds up data retrieval but takes time to update and storage space to store.
Use LEFT JOIN in the view so that rooms without patients (or patients without rooms) are not missed.

items.t: Checkpoint 3.5 pattern: views of views for payments
items.tz: Checkpoint 3.5 模式：用视图的视图计算付款
k: A view can refer to another view, so complex calculations can be built up step by step.

mc.q: A manager wants each team's average salary, excluding teams whose average salary is below 20000. Which clause should contain the condition?
mc.e: The condition is on a group summary, so it must be in HAVING after GROUP BY. WHERE would exclude individual employees before grouping.
mc.ez: 条件针对组的汇总值，要用 HAVING。

mc.q: TEAM stores MEMNUM, the number of employees in each team. Why is this field undesirable?
o: It cannot be a primary key
It takes the place of a foreign key
It must be updated whenever employees are added, or data becomes inconsistent; it can be computed with COUNT()
mc.e: MEMNUM is derivable data. Storing it risks data inconsistency; compute it with COUNT() instead.
mc.ez: 可计算的数据，储存会造成不一致。

mc.q: Every employee belongs to a department. To list each employee with their department name, excluding departments with no employees, which joins are suitable when EMPLOYEE is the left table?
mc.e: No employee lacks a department, so LEFT and INNER give the same result. RIGHT JOIN would add departments with no employees.
mc.ez: LEFT 和 INNER 结果相同；RIGHT 会多出空部门。

mc.q: In Example 3.2, to list each employee with the name of their team leader using EMPLOYEE and TEAM, what is needed?
o: Two copies of EMPLOYEE with different aliases
mc.e: The leader is also an employee, so EMPLOYEE is used twice (e for members, l for leaders).
mc.ez: 组长也是员工，EMPLOYEE 要用两个别名。

mc.q:
Why is the following statement wrong?
SELECT NAME, h.NAME FROM BREED WHERE ID IN
  (SELECT BID FROM CAT, HOTEL h WHERE HID = h.ID AND h.NAME = 'Alpha')
o: IN cannot be used with a join in the subquery
The main query cannot retrieve data (h.NAME) from the subquery
Aliases are not allowed in subqueries
mc.e: h exists only inside the subquery; to output hotel names you must join in the main query.
mc.ez: 主查询不能取子查询的栏位。

mc.q: A query should list hotels that have no Ragdoll cats. Which is correct?
o: ID IN (SELECT HID FROM CAT, BREED b WHERE BID = b.ID AND b.NAME <> 'Ragdoll')
ID NOT IN (SELECT HID FROM CAT, BREED b WHERE BID = b.ID AND b.NAME = 'Ragdoll')
mc.e: Find hotels that do have Ragdolls, then take the others. The <> version lists hotels with any non-Ragdoll cat and misses hotels with no cats.
mc.ez: 先找有 Ragdoll 的酒店，再 NOT IN。

mc.q: What is the purpose of SELECT h.NAME, COUNT(DISTINCT c.BID) FROM HOTEL h LEFT JOIN CAT c ON h.ID = c.HID GROUP BY h.ID?
o: Count the number of different breeds in each hotel, including hotels with none
List hotels with more cats than capacity
Count the cats in each hotel
mc.e: LEFT JOIN keeps every hotel; COUNT(DISTINCT c.BID) counts different breeds; empty hotels get 0.
mc.ez: 计算每间酒店的品种数目。

mc.q: Which statement correctly lists participants in team 'A' in at least one of FOOTBALL and RELAYRACE?
o: SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL WHERE TEAM = 'A' UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE WHERE TEAM = 'A'
(SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE) WHERE TEAM = 'A'
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION ALL SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL WHERE TEAM = 'A' INTERSECT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE WHERE TEAM = 'A'
mc.e: 'At least one' → UNION; each SELECT needs its own WHERE.
mc.ez: 至少一项 → UNION，各自 WHERE。

mc.q: 'List each participant aged at least 22 who does not participate in both events at the same time.' Which subquery is used with NOT IN?
o: SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL INTERSECT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL EXCEPT SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
SELECT PID FROM FOOTBALL UNION ALL SELECT PID FROM RELAYRACE
mc.e: Exclude those in both events: NOT IN (… INTERSECT …). UNION would exclude anyone in either event.
mc.ez: 排除同时参加两项的人：INTERSECT。

mc.q: In Example 3.5, view RPNUM must list every room with its number of patients. Why is r.ID selected and grouped instead of RID?
o: GROUP BY cannot use foreign keys
RID is NULL for rooms with no patients, so those rooms would lose their ID
mc.e: After ROOM LEFT JOIN PATIENT, RID (from PATIENT) is NULL for empty rooms.
mc.ez: 空房的 RID 为 NULL。

mc.q: Which of the following is a problem of storing club name, room and teacher inside every student record?
o: A new club with no members cannot be stored if SID is the primary key
mc.e: With club data inside STUDENT, a club without students has no SID, but SID is the primary key and cannot be NULL, so the club cannot be stored (insertion problem).
mc.ez: 主键 SID 不能是 NULL，没有学生的新学会无法储存。

mc.q: Science Club (3 members) moves to Room 301. How many records must be updated if club data is stored in STUDENT, and how many if it is stored in a separate CLUB table?
mc.e: Each member's record holds the room in the single-table design (3 updates); with a CLUB table, only one record changes.
mc.ez: 单表要改 3 条，分表只改 1 条。

mc.q: What is the main advantage of a linking table SC(SID, CID) when students may join many clubs?
o: A student may join many clubs without duplicating student data
It stores the number of clubs of each student
It removes the need for primary keys
mc.e: Each (student, club) pair becomes one row in SC, so student data in STUDENT is never repeated.
mc.ez: 学生可参加多个学会而不重复储存学生资料。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM STUDENT INNER JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
mc.e: Only matched records: Ben (NULL) and English Club (no student) are excluded, leaving 6.
mc.ez: 只有配对的记录，共 6 行。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
mc.e: All 7 students are kept; Ben gets NULL club fields; English Club is not included.

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does the following return?
SELECT * FROM CLUB LEFT JOIN STUDENT ON CLUB.CID = STUDENT.CID
mc.e: All clubs are kept: 6 matched rows plus English Club with NULL student = 7. This equals STUDENT RIGHT JOIN CLUB.
mc.ez: 6 行配对加 English Club 一行，共 7 行。

mc.q: Which statement about FULL JOIN is correct?
o: It is the same as CROSS JOIN
It includes unmatched records from both tables and is not available in MySQL
It requires the two tables to have the same number of fields
mc.e: FULL JOIN keeps records from both the left and right tables; MySQL does not support the keyword (use LEFT JOIN … UNION … RIGHT JOIN).
mc.ez: FULL JOIN 两边都保留；MySQL 不支援此关键字。

mc.q: In MySQL, which can produce the same result as STUDENT FULL JOIN CLUB?
o: The result of STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB combined by UNION with the result of STUDENT RIGHT JOIN CLUB
mc.e: LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched students, RIGHT JOIN keeps unmatched clubs, and UNION merges them removing duplicate matched rows.
mc.ez: LEFT JOIN 结果 UNION RIGHT JOIN 结果。

mc.q: Which statement about the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN is correct?
o: ON can only be used with INNER JOIN
ON CLUB.CID = STUDENT.CID gives a different result from ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
ON must always use fields with the same name
The order of the two fields in ON has no effect; the order of the tables does
mc.e: Which CID comes first in the ON clause has no effect; which table is written first (left table) does.
mc.ez: ON 中字段次序无影响，表的左右次序才有影响。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). Why does the following cause an error?
SELECT NAME, ROOM FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
o: ROOM is not a field of CLUB
NAME is ambiguous because both tables have a field called NAME
LEFT JOIN cannot select specific fields
CID must be written as STUDENT.CID in SELECT
mc.e: Both STUDENT and CLUB have NAME, so the table must be specified (STUDENT.NAME or CLUB.NAME).
mc.ez: 两表都有 NAME，须注明表名。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What is returned?
SELECT c.NAME FROM STUDENT s INNER JOIN CLUB c ON s.CID = c.CID
WHERE s.SCORE > 80 ORDER BY c.NAME
o: Art Club, Chess Club, Science Club
mc.e: Scores above 80: Clem 89 (Chess), Eva 83 (Science), Ben 86 (no club, dropped by INNER JOIN). Sorted: Chess Club, Science Club.
mc.ez: Ben 没有学会被 INNER JOIN 排除。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What does the following return for English Club?
SELECT c.NAME, COUNT(*) FROM CLUB c
  LEFT JOIN STUDENT s ON s.CID = c.CID GROUP BY c.CID
mc.e: The LEFT JOIN creates one row (English Club, NULL student). COUNT(*) counts rows, so it gives 1. COUNT(s.SID) would give 0.
mc.ez: COUNT(*) 计算行数，得 1；应用 COUNT(s.SID) 得 0。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). What is the average score shown for Chess Club?
SELECT c.NAME, AVG(SCORE) FROM STUDENT s LEFT JOIN CLUB c ON s.CID = c.CID
WHERE s.SID <> '03506' GROUP BY c.CID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
mc.e: Chess Club members: Clem 89 and Finn 35, average 62. (Gabe, removed by WHERE, is in Science Club.)

mc.q: Which statement is equivalent to STUDENT INNER JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID?
o: SELECT * FROM STUDENT CROSS JOIN CLUB
SELECT * FROM STUDENT LEFT JOIN CLUB ON STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
SELECT * FROM STUDENT, CLUB WHERE STUDENT.CID = CLUB.CID
mc.e: Equi-join (tables in FROM with an equality condition in WHERE) is another way to perform INNER JOIN.
mc.ez: Equi-join 就是 INNER JOIN 的另一写法。

mc.q: Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows does SELECT * FROM STUDENT, CLUB return (no WHERE clause)?
mc.e: Without a join condition, this is a CROSS JOIN: 7 × 4 = 28 rows.

mc.q: Why can't the textbook's STUDENT and CLUB tables be joined properly with NATURAL JOIN?
o: NATURAL JOIN needs an ON clause
They share two field names, NAME and CID, and NAME is not a foreign key
mc.e: NATURAL JOIN joins on all same-named fields; joining on NAME (student name = club name) is meaningless.
mc.ez: 两表有 NAME、CID 两个同名栏位，NAME 不是外键。

mc.q: What is required to perform a self join?
o: The table must have a composite primary key
The same table must be given two different aliases
The table must contain NULL values
The table must be joined with CROSS JOIN
mc.e: Two aliases let the DBMS treat the table as two different tables temporarily.
mc.ez: 同一表要给两个不同别名。

mc.q: STUDENT has CMSID, the SID of each student's class monitor. Which lists each student with their monitor's name?
o: SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1 INNER JOIN STUDENT s2 ON s1.SID = s2.SID
SELECT NAME, NAME FROM STUDENT WHERE CMSID = SID
SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1 INNER JOIN STUDENT s2 ON s1.CMSID = s2.SID
mc.e: s1 is the student, s2 the monitor; the link is s1.CMSID = s2.SID.
mc.ez: s1 是学生，s2 是班长，条件 s1.CMSID = s2.SID。

mc.q: When pairing students from STUDENT s1, STUDENT s2, which extra condition removes both self-pairs and duplicated pairs?
mc.e: s1.SID < s2.SID excludes equal SIDs (self-pairs) and keeps only one ordering of each pair. <> alone still leaves duplicates.
mc.ez: < 同时去除自配和重复；<> 仍有重复。

mc.q:
Use the textbook tables STUDENT(SID, NAME, SEX, CLASS, SCORE, CID) and CLUB(CID, NAME, ROOM, TEACH) (Ada 3A 0 CID 2; Clem 3B 89 CID 1; Eva 3B 83 CID 4; Gabe 3C 47 CID 4; Finn 3B 35 CID 1; Dio 3C 67 CID 4; Ben 3A 86 CID NULL; clubs 1 Chess, 2 Art, 3 English, 4 Science). How many rows are returned?
SELECT s1.NAME, s2.NAME FROM STUDENT s1, STUDENT s2
WHERE ABS(s1.SCORE - s2.SCORE) < 16 AND s1.SID < s2.SID
mc.e: Pairs: Clem–Eva, Clem–Ben, Eva–Ben, Gabe–Finn = 4.

k: A relational database organises data in a tabular form. Each table consists of columns and rows, and each row is a record.
a relational database may look more complicated, but it is much easier to manage in a DBMS (any table can be queried, joined, sorted and updated with SQL).

items.t: Relational database elements vs DBMS elements
items.tz: 关系式数据库元素与 DBMS 元素对照
k: "Entity type of a table?" → say what each row is, in plural: "students" .
"How is a relationship implemented?" → "by a foreign key" .
"How is a domain enforced?" → "by the data type and constraints (e.g. CHECK)" .
An entity is a physical or conceptual object. Entities must be unique. It is represented by a record.
for "State the entity types of A and B", answer with plural nouns describing each row: "School events and students respectively." Do not answer with a field or only the table name.

items.t: Misconception: attribute mistaken for an entity type
items.tz: 易错：把属性当成实体类型
k: "X is an attribute of Y, not an entity type." e.g. Age is an attribute of patients.
An attribute is a property of an entity, represented by a field. Remember: entity type → table, entity → record, attribute → field .
"Store the date of birth instead of age, because age changes every year but the birthday does not, so the data need not be updated frequently. Age can be calculated from the date of birth."
write " B participates in A ", " B sells A / A is sold by B ": entity type + verb + entity type.

items.t: Active and passive voice in relationships
k: " A is sold by B " (passive when the receiver comes first).

items.t: Misconception: specific entities used as entity types
items.tz: 易错：把特定实体当成实体类型
k: "Physics is an entity of the entity type subjects, not an entity type."

items.t: Why split data into tables (Mary's single-table idea)
items.tz: 为何要分表（Mary 的单表方案）
k: "STUDENT stores only the identity code of the club, so when club data changes, STUDENT need not be updated; and club data is kept even if all its members are deleted."
"The domain of an attribute is the set of all available values." It is implemented by the data type and constraints.

items.t: Common data types in a DBMS
k: name the type in words: integer, real / float, characters, Boolean, date, time . (SQLite is flexible but accepts the same keywords.)

items.t: How to choose a data type
k: give the type and the reason : "Characters, since some SIDs start with zero."
"Not reasonable, because ... should be a real number / should be one of ..."

items.t: Example 4.1: entity types, data types, domain, relationship
k: always quote the evidence from the question in your reason.
CLASS ( CLASS , ROOM, TEACHID) Foreign key: TEACHID
"Key fields are used to distinguish between records in a table."
"X is a candidate key because no two [entities] can have the same X."
"NULL means no data is stored; it is different from 0, which is a value."
"CLASS+CNO is a composite key: no two students share the same class and class number, and removing either field results in duplicated values."

items.tz: 判断候选键的常见陷阱
k: "Not unique, because ..." or "Not minimal, because X alone is already unique."
"SID, because it is unique and does not change, while email/class number may change."
"CID in STUDENT is a foreign key referencing the primary key CID of CLUB."

items.t: Benefits of using a foreign key
k: "Only one record needs to be updated when ... changes" ; "An integer takes less storage than a string."

items.t: Example 4.2: splitting tables and writing schemas
Add a field instead of overwriting a value (DISCOUNT)
items.tz: 新增字段代替直接改值（DISCOUNT）
k: "The original price is kept, so it can be restored by setting DISCOUNT to 0 after the promotion."
"The index table is sorted, so binary search can be performed, which is faster than searching records one by one."
("Why not index all fields?" 2 marks): Each index takes extra storage space [1]; every insert/update requires the index tables to be updated, which slows down data modification [1].

items.t: Counting binary searches in an index
k: list the items compared in order, then give the count.
name the integrity and say why: "Referential integrity, because CID 5 does not exist in CLUB."
"Entity integrity: the primary key of each record must be unique and not NULL."
"Referential integrity is violated because CID 5 in STUDENT cannot be found in CLUB."

items.t: Four actions blocked by referential integrity
items.tz: 参照完整性禁止的四种操作
k: "The deletion is rejected because the record is referenced by ... in the host table."
"Domain integrity is violated because 20:90 is not a valid time."
name it + quote the bad value.

items.t: Maintaining referential integrity when a parent record is removed
items.tz: 删除 parent 记录时保持参照完整性
k: "Delete (or update) the related records in the host table first, then delete the record in the parent table."
"Roll back the database to its previous state using the backup, to restore data integrity."

items.t: Example: SQL statements run in the wrong order
k: "The order of SQL statements matters. Restore the database from the backup and run the statements in the correct order."

items.t: Lab 4.1: backup with mysqldump and restore with mysql
k: "Export the database to an SQL file regularly with mysqldump; restore it with mysql."

items.t: Rolling back an interrupted batch of updates
items.tz: 中途中断的更新要回滚
