k: : Data structures refer to the methods of storing and organising data in the computer memory. They determine the sequences and locations of data items in the computer memory.

items.tz: 数组 Array 与直接存取
k: : An array is a simple linear data structure that stores a set of data sequentially in a continuous computer memory. Items are accessed directly (random access) by index because the address can be calculated.
: A pointer is a variable for storing a computer memory address, which is usually the address of another variable.
: A list stores index–item pairs; a dictionary stores key–value pairs, so a value is obtained by its key.
: Each block contains the block's transactions and a hash pointing to the previous block , like a node with data and a pointer. Unlike a linked list, insertion or deletion of a block cannot be done .

items.tz: 堆叠 Stack 与后进先出
k: : A stack is a data structure manipulated by the last-in first-out (LIFO) approach. Push adds to the top; pop removes from the top.
: Undo: push(R, pop(U)). Redo: push(U, pop(R)). A new action is pushed onto U and R is cleared. If U is empty, undo takes no action to avoid underflow.

items.tz: 应用：调用堆叠 Call stack
k: : A call stack is a stack stored in RAM used to coordinate sub-programs. A call pushes a stack frame (return address, parameters, local variables); a return pops it. Too many nested calls → stack overflow .

items.tz: 用 Python list 操作 stack
k: : Push: stack.append(item). Pop: stack.pop(). Peek: stack[-1]. Empty: len(stack) == 0. Popping an empty list raises IndexError (underflow).

items.tz: Stack 的 underflow 与 overflow
k: : Underflow: popping from an empty stack. Overflow: pushing into a full stack. Check isEmpty before pop and isFull before push.
: push(S, x) adds x to the top; pop(S) removes and returns the top item; isEmpty(S) returns true if S has no items. Write stacks bottom → top .

items.tz: 方法：reverse(A, B) 倒序搬移
k: : reverse(A, B): while not isEmpty(A), push(B, pop(A)) . The top of A becomes the bottom of B; reversing twice restores the original order.

items.t: Method: remove the bottom N items
items.tz: 方法：删除 stack 底部 N 项
k: : reverse(S1, S2); pop(S2) N times; reverse(S2, S1) . The first reverse brings the bottom items to the top; the second restores the order. Accessing items far from the top is inefficient (about 2 × n moves).

items.t: Method: take k items from the middle, get(n, k)
items.tz: 方法：从第 n 层取 k 项 get(n, k)
k: : Move items n..t to S3 (loop runs t − n + 1 times), pop k items from S3 to S2, then reverse(S3, S1) . S2 bottom→top = item n, ..., n+k−1.

items.tz: 例：用 stack 累加并分箱
k: : Trace with a table popped | temp | S1 | S2 , one row per loop. Note the condition: > 25 (not ≥), and only one box per loop.
: Back: push(goForward, pop(goBack)). Forward: push(goBack, pop(goForward)). Visiting a new page clears goForward. It uses stacks because the page to go back to is the most recent one (LIFO).

items.tz: 队列 Queue 与先进先出
k: : A queue is a data structure manipulated by the first-in first-out (FIFO) approach. Enqueue adds to the end (tail) ; dequeue removes from the beginning (head) .
: Stack: LIFO, one end (top). Queue: FIFO, two ends (enqueue at tail, dequeue at head). Neither allows inserting in the middle.

items.tz: 用 Python list 操作 queue
k: : Enqueue: queue.append(item). Dequeue: queue.pop(0). Peek: queue[0]. Stack uses pop(), queue uses pop(0).

items.t: Queue in an array: shifting method
items.tz: 用 array 表示 queue（搬移法）
k: : With the shifting method every dequeue moves all remaining items forward, which greatly increases the steps/time of operation, reducing the efficiency of the algorithm . Fix: use head and tail pointers .

items.t: Queue with head and tail pointers
items.tz: 用 head / tail pointer 操作 queue
k: : Enqueue: tail ← tail + 1; Q[tail] ← x. Dequeue: x ← Q[head]; head ← head + 1. head > tail means empty. Problem: when tail reaches the end of the array, enqueue overflows even though front cells are free ( wasted space ).
: Use a circular queue: when the pointer reaches the end of the array, reset it to the first index of the array, so the empty positions can be reused. In code: (pointer + 1) % size .

items.t: Circular queue: empty vs full and counter N
items.tz: Circular queue 要额外计数 N
k: : Empty and full both give head = (tail + 1) % size , so we cannot tell empty or full from the pointers alone . Keep a counter N : N = 0 → empty (underflow on dequeue); N = size → full (overflow on enqueue).

items.tz: Circular queue 的 index 公式
k: : last = (first + N − 1) % size; next empty = (first + N) % size; k-th = (first + k − 1) % size. Start from next and wait: (next − wait) % size .

items.t: Circular queue pseudocode: addQ and delQ
k: : Marking points: (1) check empty/full with N ; (2) correct index with % size ; (3) update N ; (4) update first with wrap-around. In delQ, read T[first] before moving first.

items.t: Traversing and tracing a circular queue
k: : Traverse with i ← start; repeat N times: visit P[i]; i ← (i + 1) % size . Dequeued cells may still hold old values ; don't count them.

items.tz: 链表 Linked list 与 node
k: : A linked list is formed by many nodes. Each node stores its own data and a pointer, which stores the address of the next node. Nodes in the linked list are all connected by pointers. Head pointer → first node; last node has a null pointer .
: Delete B from A → B → C: A.next ← B.next. Only the previous node's pointer changes; B's own pointer need not change. Deleting the first node: head ← head.next .
: Point the pointer of the new node to the next node first, then point the pointer of the previous node to the new node. (E.next ← A.next; A.next ← E)
: Doubly: advantage: nodes can be accessed from both directions; disadvantage: more memory (storage space) is required. Circular: the last node points back to the first.

: Disk fragmentation : a file is stored as scattered fragments; a linked list connects them (each segment stores the location of the next segment , last = N/A). Data need not be continuous, but access is sequential (slower).

items.tz: Linked list 与 array 比较
k: : Array: direct/random access, fast access, slow insert/delete (shifting). Linked list: sequential access, slow access, fast insert/delete (change pointers), extra memory for pointers.

items.tz: 用 array 表示 linked list
k: : Table Index | Content | Pointer ; Pointer = index of next node; start = first node. Null pointer may be −1 , any negative number, or a number larger than the largest index .

items.t: Insert and delete in the array representation
items.tz: Array 表示下的 insert / delete
k: : insert(n, x) : write x in empty row r; Pointer[r] ← Pointer[node n]; Pointer[node n] ← r. delete(n) : Pointer[node n−1] ← Pointer[node n]. Re-walk the list after each operation.
: length() : count steps from start until null. delete(n) : if n = 1, start ← NP[start]; else walk prev and current together, then NP[prev] ← NP[current] .
: After the loop, prev = node n−1 and current = old node n. NP[i] ← current first, then NP[prev] ← i . If n = 1: NP[i] ← start; start ← i.

items.tz: 线性搜索 Linear search（for 循环）
k: Linear search compares the target with each item in turn, from the first item, until it is found or the end of the list is reached .

items.t: Linear search with a while loop and a flag
items.tz: Linear search：while 循环与旗标 Flag
k: A flag (Boolean variable) is used to terminate the loop once the target is found , reducing the number of comparisons.

items.tz: 输出所有位置的 linear search

The number of comparisons is proportional to N ; worst case N , average (N+1)/2 .

items.t: Linear search in pseudocode (comparison in the loop condition)
items.tz: Pseudocode：在 while 条件中比较
k: The bound check i <= n is placed first to avoid accessing an element outside the array .

items.t: Linear search on a sorted list
items.tz: 已排序 list 上的 linear search
k: In an ascending list, once an item greater than the target is reached, the search can stop , because all later items are also greater.

items.tz: 二分搜索 Binary search 概念
k: The list must be sorted. The target is compared with the middle item, and the search range is halved after each comparison.

items.t: Binary search: start, mid and end
items.tz: Binary search 的 start / mid / end
k: In a trace table, record start, end, mid and the item compared on each row; the search ends when the item is found or start > end .
Initialise start = 0, end = len - 1 ; repeat while start <= end ; compute mid = (start + end) // 2 .

items.t: Binary search on a descending list
items.tz: 降序 list 的 binary search
k: Since the list is in descending order , if the middle item is greater than the target, the search continues in the second half .

items.t: Binary search on a sorted list of strings

k: Binary search needs a sorted list; each comparison halves the search range.

items.tz: 用 leftMost / rightMost 统计重复值

items.t: Efficiency of binary search: log2 N
k: The maximum number of comparisons is about log 2 N , since the search range is halved after each comparison.

items.tz: Linear search 与 binary search 比较
k: Binary search is more efficient for a large list , but the list must be sorted , and inserting new items in order takes extra time.
A temporary variable is needed to store the original value of A , otherwise it is overwritten and lost.

items.tz: 交换数组中两项（子程序）
k: When parallel arrays are used, the corresponding elements in all arrays must be swapped together .

Sorting arranges data in ascending or descending order of a key field , so that binary search can be used and data are easier to process.

items.tz: 选择排序 Selection sort：概念与每轮
k: In each pass, the largest (smallest) item in the unsorted part is selected and swapped with the first item of the unsorted part .
The inner loop finds the index of the largest item ; the outer loop swaps it into position i .
Selection sort always needs N(N-1)/2 comparisons , even if the list is already sorted, but at most N - 1 swaps .

items.tz: 插入排序 Insertion sort：概念与每轮
k: The first item of the unsorted part (key) is inserted into the correct position of the sorted part , by shifting larger/smaller items one place backwards.
Items are shifted one place backwards until the correct position is found, then the key is inserted .
Insertion sort is efficient when the list is almost sorted : best case N - 1 comparisons; worst case N(N-1)/2 .

items.t: Insertion sort: swap version vs shift version
items.tz: Insertion sort：swap 版与 shift 版
k: The shift version is more efficient because it requires fewer data movements (assignments) .

items.tz: 冒泡排序 Bubble sort：概念与每轮
k: Adjacent items are compared and swapped if they are in the wrong order ; after each pass the smallest (largest) unsorted item moves to its final position.
The inner loop compares mark[j] and mark[j+1] and swaps them if they are in the wrong order; its range decreases by 1 each pass .

items.t: Efficiency and improvements of bubble sort
items.tz: Bubble sort 的效率与改良
k: Use a flag to record whether any swap occurs in a pass; if no swap occurs, the list is sorted and the algorithm terminates .
All three take about N 2 /2 comparisons in the worst case; selection sort makes fewest swaps , insertion sort is best for nearly sorted data .

items.tz: 合并两个已排序 list：概念
k: The first unmerged items of the two lists are compared, and the smaller (for ascending order) is copied to the merged list ; repeat until both lists are used up.
Use two pointers to the first unmerged items; after copying an item, increase the pointer of that list by 1 .
The condition checks whether a list is used up before comparing its item , to avoid reading beyond the end of the list.
Since both lists are in descending order, merging starts from the last items and the pointers are decreased by 1 .
Merge sort repeatedly divides the list into halves until each sub-list has one item, then merges the sorted sub-lists .
A pivot is chosen and the list is partitioned into items smaller than the pivot and items greater than or equal to the pivot ; the sub-lists are sorted in the same way.

items.t: Efficiency of merge sort and quick sort
items.tz: Merge sort 与 quick sort 的效率
k: Merge sort and quick sort need about N log 2 N comparisons , since there are log 2 N levels of division with about N comparisons per level .
For a large amount of data , merge sort / quick sort is more efficient because the number of comparisons grows as N log 2 N instead of N 2 .

items.tz: 为什么有这么多排序算法？
k: The choice of sorting algorithm depends on the amount of data, the initial order of the data, the data structure / memory available and the cost of data movement .

o: It is kept and the new content is added at the end
It is kept and the new content is added at the start
mc.e: "w" overwrites the content.

mc.q: What does os.path.exists("a.txt") return?
o: The number of lines in a.txt
mc.e: It returns True if the file/path exists, otherwise False.

mc.q: Which statement must come before os.path.exists() can be used?
mc.e: exists() is in the os library.

mc.q: What is the data type returned by f.readlines()?
mc.e: readlines() returns a list of line strings.

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
content = f.read()
f.close()
print(type(content))
mc.e: read() returns the whole content as one string.

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
lines = f.readlines()
f.close()
print(len(lines))
mc.e: readlines() returns one item per line; the file has 3 lines.

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
line = f.readline()
f.close()
print(repr(line))
mc.e: The first readline() returns line one including its \n.
mc.ez: 第一次 readline() 返回第一行（含 \n）。

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
for i in range(3):
    f.readline()
line = f.readline()
f.close()
print(repr(line))
mc.e: After 3 lines, the pointer is at EOF, so the 4th readline() returns an empty string.
mc.ez: 第 4 次读到 EOF，返回空字符串。

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
f.readline()
f.readline()
line = f.readline()
f.close()
print(repr(line))
mc.e: The last line has no \n before EOF.

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
f.readline()
rest = f.readlines()
f.close()
print(rest)
o: ['This is line two.\n', 'This is line three.']
mc.e: readline() moved the pointer past line one; readlines() reads the rest.
mc.ez: 指针已过第一行，readlines() 读剩下的。

mc.q:
t.txt has 3 lines: "This is line one." / "This is line two." / "This is line three." (no line feed after line three). What is printed?
f = open("t.txt", "r")
all_text = f.read()
rest = f.readlines()
f.close()
print(len(rest))
mc.e: read() moved the pointer to EOF, so readlines() returns an empty list.
mc.ez: read() 后已到 EOF，返回空列表。

mc.q: Which character is stored at the end of every line (except usually the last) in a text file?
mc.e: The Line Feed character \n marks the end of a line.

mc.q: Which statement about the hidden pointer is correct?
o: It points to the last character when the file is opened
It always returns to the first character after each read
It is only used by read()
Each read starts from where the pointer last stopped
mc.e: Reading continues from the pointer's last position.
mc.ez: 每次读取从指针上次停下处开始。

mc.q:
What is len("Hi\n")?
print(len("Hi\n"))
mc.e: \n is one character.

mc.q: In Example 7.1's loop, which condition correctly stops reading at the end of the file?
mc.e: readline() returns "" only at EOF.
mc.ez: 只有 EOF 时返回空字符串。

mc.q: A file f has 5 lines including one blank line in the middle. How many items does the readline() while loop (len(name) > 0) collect?
mc.e: A blank line is "\n" (length 1), so the loop continues; all 5 lines are collected.

mc.q:
What happens when this runs and ghost.txt does not exist?
f = open("ghost.txt", "r")
mc.e: "r" on a missing file raises a run-time error (FileNotFoundError).
mc.ez: "r" 打开不存在的文件会出错。

mc.q: Which is NOT true about f.close()?
o: It helps make sure written content is saved
f.close without brackets does not close the file
It should be called after file operations
mc.e: close() does not delete; os.remove() deletes.

mc.q: A file is opened with "r" and the program calls f.write("Hi"). What happens?
o: Hi is added at the start
Hi is added at the end
mc.e: A file opened in "r" mode is read-only.

mc.q:
What is printed?
s = "This is a book."
print(s.find("is"))
mc.e: "is" first occurs inside "This" at index 2.

mc.q:
What is printed?
s = "This is a book."
print(s.find("is", 3))
mc.e: Searching from index 3, the next "is" starts at 5.

mc.q:
What is printed?
s = "This is a book."
print(s.find("Is"))
mc.e: find() returns -1 when not found (case-sensitive).

mc.q:
What is printed?
s = "banana"
print(s.find("a", 2))
mc.e: From index 2, the next "a" is at 3.
mc.ez: 从索引 2 开始，下一个 a 在 3。

mc.q:
What is printed?
print("I am fine".split())
mc.e: split() with no argument splits on whitespace.

mc.q:
What is printed?
print(len("a,,b,c".split(",")))
mc.e: An explicit delimiter keeps empty items: ['a', '', 'b', 'c'].
mc.ez: 指定定界符会保留空项。

mc.q:
What is printed?
print(len("  hello   world  ".split()))
mc.e: split() with no argument ignores extra spaces: ['hello', 'world'].
mc.ez: 不带参数会忽略多余空格。

mc.q:
What is printed?
pets = "cat#dog#bird"
print(pets.split("#")[1])
mc.e: Index 1 of ['cat','dog','bird'].

ECC8.t: Applications of Programming in Real Life
ECC8.tz: 编程在现实生活中的应用
sec: 8.5 Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Smart Living

k: Maker culture encourages problem-solving through DIY , creating or adapting products with raw materials and technology (robots, electronic sensors, 3D printing). A prototype is an early model built to test an idea .

STEAM education integrates Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Mathematics so students apply them to tackle real-life issues , developing problem-solving and innovation skills through hands-on experience .
Input: the [sensor] detects/measures …; Process: the microcontroller compares the reading with a threshold …; Output: the [LED/buzzer/motor] …
Use a [name] sensor to detect/measure the [physical quantity] , e.g. “an ultrasonic sensor to measure the distance between the hand and the tap”.
Manual input devices require the user to adjust the data by hand , while sensors change data automatically according to the external environment .
A servo motor can rotate to a specific angle ; a DC motor rotates continuously at different speeds .

A programmable microcontroller is the main processor of an electronic device ; it is a small circuit board with ports and pins to connect input and output devices , and it executes the uploaded program to control them.
The code is in the setup / on start part, so it runs only once ; the condition is never checked again. Move it into a forever loop so the sensor is read and checked repeatedly .

items.tz: 实验：用 micro:bit 控制 LED 面板
k: Code in on start runs once after the micro:bit starts; code in forever runs repeatedly , so the heartbeat animation keeps repeating.

items.tz: 视觉化编程与文字编程
k: Visual programming is easy to read and write and lets beginners focus on concepts instead of syntax , but is less flexible ; textual programming is more flexible but must follow strict syntax .

items.tz: 引脚与 micro:bit 内置传感器
k: The higher the ambient brightness, the larger the light level reading ; the lower the brightness, the smaller the reading (range 0–255 ).
When the specified event occurs (e.g. button A pressed), the corresponding event handler is executed .
The accelerometer detects the tilt ; the microcontroller compares the x-value with the boundaries and the LED panel shows the matching pattern.
Automation lets a device make decisions by itself according to a preset program ; it can reduce manual work , enhance cost-effectiveness and operate continuously .
The light sensor measures the brightness ; if the brightness is lower than the threshold , the microcontroller turns on the LED , otherwise turns it off; this is repeated in a forever loop .

items.t: Designing an automated device: smart kettle
items.tz: 设计自动化设备：智能电热水壶
k: Sensor: water temperature sensor to measure the water temperature . Output: LED shows the status, buzzer emits a notification sound. Algorithm: repeat reading the temperature until it reaches 100°C , then stop heating.
The [sensor] detects …; the device automatically … (e.g. “a PIR sensor detects whether someone is in the room ; the air-conditioner switches off automatically when nobody is there”).

items.t: Integrated exercise: algorithms controlling a laser cutter
items.tz: 综合练习：激光切割机算法
k: The sub-program uses parameters x, y, w, h ; the nozzle moves to (x, y), starts cutting, moves clockwise through the corners and returns to (x, y) , then stops cutting .
To access sensor data remotely, add a Wi-Fi module to connect the device to the Internet and program it to send real-time sensor data to the cloud .

items.t: AIoT, big data and cloud computing
items.tz: 人工智能物联网、大数据与云端运算
k: IoT collects real-time data; the data forms big data ; cloud computing trains the model; AI analyses trends and patterns to predict …
Collect samples for each class, train the model , then test the model with new images ; more and more varied samples improve accuracy .
Speech recognition converts human speech into corresponding text ; the program then analyses the text (keywords) and performs the corresponding action .
Ask → Imagine → Plan → Create → Improve , and repeat the whole process to improve the product.

items.t: Integrated exercise: cinema seats, 2D array vs three arrays
items.tz: 综合练习：戏院座位，2D 数组 vs 三个数组
综合练习：fromMin / fromMax 检索

items.t: Integrated exercise: stack export(L) with a second stack
items.tz: 综合练习：用第二个 stack 的 export(L)

items.t: Integrated exercise: storing an image in a text file (run-length)
items.tz: 综合练习：用文本文件储存图像（连续编码）

items.t: Open-ended projects: Connect Four, 2048, Tower of Hanoi, Mastermind
items.tz: 开放式题目：四子棋、2048、河内塔、珠玑妙算

mc.q: Henry's smart garden must display sensor values in real time. Which output device?
mc.e: Display shows information.

mc.q: A plant grow light must emit light of a suitable spectrum. Which output device?
mc.e: RGB LED emits different colours.

mc.q: To monitor the moisture and pH of soil, use
o: Soil moisture sensor and pH sensor
mc.e: Name sensors by quantity measured.

mc.q: Kristy's station monitors noise and air pollution. Suitable sensors?
o: Sound intensity sensor and PM sensor
mc.e: Noise → sound intensity; pollution → PM.
mc.src: Textbook EC Ch8 Chapter Exercise Q1(a) (p.331)

mc.q: A fan program is in 'on start'. At 28°C the fan turns on; at 24°C it keeps rotating. Why?
o: The program runs only once, so the temperature is not checked again
mc.e: Need a repeat-forever loop.
mc.ez: 只执行一次，要用 forever 循环。
mc.src: Textbook EC Ch8 Chapter Exercise Q2 (p.331)

mc.q: Pedometer: on start steps ← 0; on shake ___; output steps. Fill the blank.
mc.e: Each shake adds a step.
mc.src: Textbook EC Ch8 Chapter Exercise Q3 (p.331)

mc.q: Which is NOT a benefit of automation listed in the chapter?
mc.e: Three benefits listed.

mc.q: Jessie's smart kettle needs which sensor?
mc.e: Measures water temperature.

mc.q: Which output devices suit the smart kettle (red/green lights, notification sound)?
mc.e: Lights and sound.

mc.q: Corridor lights turn on when someone walks in. Which sensor?
mc.e: PIR or ultrasonic.

mc.q: Kelly's device turns off the screen when the user is closer than 50 cm. Which sensor?
mc.e: Distance.
mc.src: Textbook EC Ch8 Chapter Exercise Q4(a) (p.331)

mc.q: rect(x,y,w,h) cuts clockwise from (x,y). The third point visited by rect(2,5,3,4) is
mc.src: Textbook EC Ch8 Integrated Exercise C Q1(b) (p.332)

mc.q: To view her station's data remotely, Kristy should
o: add a Wi-Fi module and send real-time data to the cloud
mc.e: Connect to the Internet.
mc.src: Textbook EC Ch8 Chapter Exercise Q1(b) (p.331)

mc.q: Which best describes maker culture?
o: Problem-solving through DIY, creating or adapting products with raw materials and technology
Writing programs only in textual languages
mc.e: Maker culture = DIY problem-solving with raw materials and technology.
mc.ez: 创客文化 = 用原材料和科技 DIY 解决问题。

mc.q: Which is NOT given as a typical maker technology?
mc.e: Robots, sensors and 3D printing are the examples.
mc.ez: 例子是机械人、传感器、3D 打印。

mc.q: A prototype is
o: an early working model used to test an idea
mc.e: Prototype = early test model.

mc.q: In STEAM, the letter A stands for
mc.e: Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, Mathematics.

mc.q: What does STEAM education mainly aim to nurture?
mc.e: Integrating subjects to tackle real-life issues builds problem-solving and innovation.

mc.q: According to the chapter, easy programming turns ordinary people from ___ into ___.
mc.e: Tool users → tool builders.
mc.ez: 由工具使用者变成工具制造者。

mc.q: In the IPO cycle, the 'Process' stage refers to
o: methods or procedures used to process data
mc.e: Process = methods/procedures processing data.
mc.ez: Process 是处理数据的方法。

mc.q: Which sensor measures distance by emitting and receiving waves?
mc.e: Ultrasonic sensor.

mc.q: Automatic doors usually use a
mc.e: PIR detects human movement by infrared radiation.

mc.q: Which sensor would a drone use for balancing?
mc.e: Acceleration and direction.

mc.q: An air quality monitoring station mainly needs a
mc.e: PM sensor measures particulate concentration.

mc.q: Which is a manual input device?
mc.e: Potentiometers are adjusted by hand.

mc.q: The difference between sensors and manual input devices is that sensors
o: change data automatically with the environment
need the user to adjust by hand
mc.e: Sensors are automatic input devices.
mc.ez: 传感器自动随环境改变。

mc.q: Which output device positions to a specific angle?
mc.e: Servo = specific angle; DC = continuous rotation.
mc.ez: 伺服马达转到指定角度。

mc.q: A fan should use which output device?
mc.e: DC motor rotates continuously at different speeds.

mc.q: A door bell mainly uses a
mc.e: Buzzer emits sound.

mc.q: The main processor on an electronic device is called a
mc.e: Programmable microcontroller.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following statements about clicking a hyperlink in a presentation file is correct?
o: The hyperlink needs to involve HTTP.
A browser will not open when the hyperlink is “http://hkeaa.edu.hk/abc.doc”.
A PDF reader will usually open when the hyperlink links to a PDF file.
The presentation file will close automatically when the hyperlink links to another presentation file.
dseWeb.e: The OS opens a linked file with its associated program, e.g. a PDF reader for .pdf.

dseWeb.q: At home, Mary cannot access the HKEAA's web site by entering http://www.hkeaa.edu.hk, but she can do it by entering http://210.0.205.228. Why?
o: The DNS server is out of service.
The web server is out of service.
Her web browser needs an extra plug-in.
The router used at home is out of order.
dseWeb.e: The IP works, so only domain-name resolution (DNS) fails.

dseWeb.q: John can view an online video on the computer at home but not on the computer in his school. Why?
o: The operating system does not support the video playback.
The browser does not support the video playback.
The video is not in HTML format.
The maximum data transfer rate of the school network is low.
dseWeb.e: The school browser may lack the needed plug-in/codec support for the video.

dseWeb.q: In a DBMS, a database designer designs a form for a clerk to use to enter data. Why does he choose to design a form?
o: More data can be entered at the same time.
The data entry uses less system computation time.
dseWeb.e: A form gives the clerk a simple, friendly interface for data entry.

dseWeb.q: When editing page numbers and hyperlinks in a document, which of the following statements is correct?
o: A browser must be open when clicking the hyperlinks.
The page numbers are printed as footnotes.
The hyperlinks facilitate the reading of the document.
The page numbers must start from 1.
dseWeb.e: Hyperlinks let readers jump to related places, helping reading.

dseWeb.q: A company develops an internal email system. It adopts HTML format instead of plain text for the email because
o: the POP protocol can be used.
dseWeb.e: HTML email supports fonts, colours, etc.; plain text can't.

dseWeb.q:
Peter can use the following two methods to download files. He chooses Method 1. Why?
Method 1: Direct download through HTTP
Method 2: Download using Peer-to-Peer (P2P) file sharing technology
o: The data transfer rate is higher.
It is illegal to use Method 2.
dseWeb.e: HTTP download just needs a browser; P2P needs a special client.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following statements about copyright protection in Hong Kong is correct?
o: Ideas are not protected unless they are in the form of expressions or products.
The Customs and Excise Department cannot take legal action against copyright piracy unless the copyright owners file a complaint.
A book cannot be protected unless it is published in Hong Kong.
Computer programs are not protected unless the copyright owners inform the Office of the Government Chief Information Officer (OGCIO).
dseWeb.e: Copyright protects expressions, not bare ideas; protection is automatic.

dseWeb.q: Mary creates a file in HTML format instead of text format. Why?
st: (3) Videos can be displayed when opening the file.
dseWeb.e: HTML can hold hyperlinks and embed video; plain text is also cross-platform, so (1) is false.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following functions is provided by a typical Internet browser?
o: Block unauthorised access to the computer.
Support the Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) in online transactions.
dseWeb.e: Browsers support SSL/HTTPS; blocking access and virus protection are firewall/antivirus jobs.

dseWeb.q:
Cathy receives an anonymous email about changing the password of her online banking account, as shown below. She clicks the hyperlink in the email and a malicious web site is displayed.

Kowloon Bank
Your password has expired. Please click the following link to update your password.
https://KLNbanks.ru

Which of the following security issues is/are mainly involved in the instance?
dseWeb.e: A fake bank email leading to a fake site is phishing; the malicious site may also intrude into her computer.

dseWeb.q: What is the major benefit of using a form in a database management system?
o: Filters data in a single database table.
dseWeb.e: Forms give a friendly layout for entering data.

dseWeb.q: A web page displays some images. In addition to the names of the image files, what other information will be included in the HTML code of the web page?
st: (1) The paths of the image files
(2) The size of the image files
(3) The IP address of the server that stores the HTML file
dseWeb.e: holds the path to the file; file size and the server's IP are not written in the HTML.

dseWeb.q:
The file sizes of the following original files are all 1 MB. Under normal circumstances, after compressing them, which compressed file has the largest file size?
Original filesCompressed files
A.testA.htmltestA.zip
B.testB.doctestB.zip
C.testC.txttestC.zip
D.testD.jpgtestD.zip
dseWeb.e: JPEG is already compressed, so zipping it barely reduces its size.

dseWeb.q: Amy can browse the web site of ABC School through its IP address, but not its URL. What is the possible reason for this?
o: The corresponding web pages have not been uploaded onto the web server.
The domain name system (DNS) server is temporarily out of service.
The browser in use is not the latest version.
Some plug-ins for the browser in use have not been installed.
dseWeb.e: The site works by IP, so only the name-to-IP lookup (DNS) is failing.

dseWeb.q: Why do we need Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) on the Internet?
o: An IP address includes at least four values.
The socket for power supply can be protected.
dseWeb.e: SSL encrypts data in transit.

dseWeb.q:
The following two URLs can be used to access the same web site:
'http://202.8.88.24' and 'http://www.hkedcity.net'
Which of the following statements about the two URLs is/are correct?
st: (1) The DNS server may translate 'www.hkedcity.net' to '202.8.88.24'.
(3) The web pages accessed through the IP address are more secure.
dseWeb.e: DNS maps the domain to the IP; URLs can use other protocols and using an IP is not more secure.

dseWeb.q: In HTML, which of the following are the attributes of a table (TABLE)?
st: (1) URLs of the contents of cells
(3) Media types of the contents of cells
dseWeb.e: TABLE has attributes such as cellspacing and bgcolor.

dseWeb.q:
ABC Coffee Shop offers free WiFi for customers. The details are:
ABC Coffee Shop
- A 30-minute session of free WiFi service
- SSID: abc; Password: YW$1818abc
- Unencrypted connection
- 128 Kbps maximum bandwidth
Customers should not use the WiFi connection for online banking because
o: the free session is too short.
the SSID is too short and easily guessed.
the data passing through the connection is not encrypted.
the maximum bandwidth is still too low.
dseWeb.e: Unencrypted traffic can be sniffed by others on the network.

dseWeb.q: A photographer posts his photos to a social media web site for the public to look at. Which of the following can be applied to the photo to protect his intellectual property?
dseWeb.e: A digital watermark marks the photo's ownership.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following protocols is/are involved when browsing https://www.gov.hk?
dseWeb.e: DNS resolves the name and IP carries the packets; FTP is not used.

dseWeb.q: What is/are the major advantage(s) of using a form for data entry in database software?
st: It shortens the execution time of SQL statements.
dseWeb.e: Forms give a friendly layout with controls/validation → fewer input errors. They don't speed up SQL or save storage.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following about HTTP is/are correct?
st: It is used to transfer hypertext documents.
It is used to translate URLs into IP addresses.
It is used to store the browsing history.
dseWeb.e: DNS translates domain names to IP. The browser stores history.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following describe(s) the URL, https://www.abc.edu.hk/en/ ?
st: en is a path on the web server.
The web site is registered as an educational institution in Hong Kong.
dseWeb.e: /en/ is a path, and .edu.hk means a Hong Kong education site. The domain name is www.abc.edu.hk, not just abc.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following regarding Unicode and Big-5 code is correct?
o: In a computer, the use of Big-5 code and Unicode depends on the operating system.
Big-5 code is used for representing characters in Chinese only.
Unicode is used for representing characters in English and other languages.
For web browsing, the use of a character set depends on the browser.
dseWeb.e: Unicode covers English and most other languages. Big-5 also has English letters, and the character set is set by the file, not the OS or browser.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following about the use of HTTP is correct?
o: It can convert a domain name into an IP address.
It can distinguish a wireless network from a wired network.
It can retrieve a web page from a web server.
It can encrypt and decrypt data through a secure channel.
dseWeb.e: HTTP transfers web pages. DNS converts names and HTTPS/SSL encrypts.

dseWeb.q: Mary uploads a photo to her social media account through a browser. Which of the following protocols will probably be involved?
dseWeb.e: DNS finds the server, HTTP(S) carries the upload and IP routes the packets: all three.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following is the common input and output of a domain name system (DNS) server?
o: Input: IP address, Output: MAC address
Input: Domain name, Output: MAC address
Input: Domain name, Output: IP address
dseWeb.e: DNS turns a domain name into an IP address.

dseWeb.q: What is/are the advantage(s) of using Secure Socket Layer (SSL) on web sites?
st: The data transfer rate is higher.
The IP addresses of the web sites can be hidden.
dseWeb.e: SSL encrypts data. It does not speed things up or hide IP addresses.

dseWeb.q:
Peter wants to replace the short form, ‘LAN’, with the full name, ‘Local Area Network’ in a document, as shown below.
Before: “The High Land School wants to build a LAN to ...”
After: “The High Land School wants to build a Local Area Network to ...”
Which of the following search options in the REPLACE function of a word processor should Peter choose?
dseWeb.e: Whole word stops 'Land' matching; match case stops 'lan' in other words. No wildcards or sounds-like needed.

dseWeb.q:
In the following HTML code, what are the six digits after ‘#’?

<BODY BGCOLOR="#112233">
st: They represent three values for the colours red, green and blue.
They are used to transfer to DNS for web browsing.
They refer to three hexadecimal values.
dseWeb.e: #RRGGBB: three hex values for red, green, blue. Nothing to do with DNS.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following is not open source software?
dseWeb.e: Internet Explorer is proprietary freeware, not open source.

dseWeb.q: Which of the following actions should not be carried out when constructing a web page?
o: Insert multimedia elements but not photos.
dseWeb.e: HTML is interpreted by the browser, never compiled.

dseWeb.q: Amy owns a domain name, 'amycomp.com'. Which of the following URLs is not owned by Amy?
dseWeb.e: amycomp.com.hk is a different domain.

dseDb.q: Peter and Mary share a database file X and execute database queries, T1 and T2, respectively. Which of the following activities should the database management system not do?
st: (1) When T1 is reading X, T2 is reading X.
(2) When T1 is writing records in X, T2 is writing records in X.
(3) When T1 is deleting records in X, T2 is reading X.
dseDb.e: Simultaneous reads are safe; any write/delete while another accesses X can cause inconsistent data, so it must be locked.

dseDb.q: Assume that every household has a residential telephone number. In which of the following database applications could the residential telephone number be used as a key field?
dseDb.e: A Towngas account is one per household, so the household phone number is unique; people in one home share it.

dseDb.q: In a DBMS, a database designer designs a form for a clerk to use to enter data. Why does he choose to design a form?
o: More data can be entered at the same time.
The data entry uses less system computation time.

The problem involves a document file.

while J <= 10000

Flag ← 0
J ← 1
while J <= 10000 and Flag = 0

When comparing the execution times of the two segments, which of the following statements is correct?
o: They are more or less the same.
dseDb.e: S2 stops as soon as the item is found; S1 always checks all 10000.

dseDb.q: A computer system uses the Hong Kong identity card (HKID) number as a key field for managing accounts. Its check digit is used to detect input errors made by users. Which of the following input errors can usually be found by the check digit?
st: (2) Swap two digits in the HKID number.
(3) Input a wrong digit in the HKID number.
dseDb.e: Check digits catch transpositions and single wrong digits; another person's real number is still valid.

dseDb.q: Mr Lee wants to set up a cleaning service company to serve thousands of clients. He needs to process data about the service and create a monthly report for each client. Which software should he buy?
dseDb.e: Thousands of related records plus per-client reports suit a database.

dseDb.q:

st: (1) There is only one record in EMPLOYEE.
(2) The content of NAME or PHONE in the remaining records is empty.
(3) There may be some other fields in EMPLOYEE.
dseDb.e: With no WHERE clause every record is returned (even empty ones), so the table must have one record; other fields may still exist.

dseDb.q: When creating a database table, what should be defined?
dseDb.e: Table structure = field names and data types; records are added later.

dseDb.q: In 2012, the US Government launched a project to explore how ‘big data’ could be used. ‘Big data’ refers to the huge amount of data collected which is difficult to process using database management systems. Which of the following are examples of ‘big data’?
st: (2) User behaviour in a social networking web site
(3) The total number of government officials in the US
dseDb.e: DNA and social-network behaviour are huge data sets; a headcount is one number.

dseDb.q: When using a database management systems tool, what is the major purpose of a query?
o: Adjust the layout of a database report.
dseDb.e: A query selects/extracts the data that meet given criteria.

dseDb.q: A company uses a smart card system to record the attendance records of its employees. When an employee enters the company's office, he puts his smart card on a card reader and a new record is generated and stored in a database table. Which of the following fields are essential in the new record?
dseDb.e: Card number identifies the employee (name/department can be looked up); the entry time must be recorded.

dseDb.q: Mary produces daily sales reports for a supermarket on a word processor, using the data and charts stored in several spreadsheet files. The data and charts are updated frequently. Which of the following is most helpful to her?
dseDb.e: Linked objects (OLE) update automatically in the report when the spreadsheets change.

dseDb.e: The public will use different devices, so the format must be cross-platform.

dseDb.q: When placing a table in a web page, which of the following is not a table setting?
dseDb.e: HTML tables have no formulas; that's a spreadsheet feature.

dseDb.q: What is the major benefit of using a form in a database management system?

dseDb.e: The number of records is limited by the unique staff numbers: 10 bits give 2^10 values.

dseDb.q: In order for a factory manager to decide on the number of machines to be bought to produce pencils, he needs to consider time and cost constraints. What spreadsheet feature should he use to do this?
dseDb.e: What-if analysis (e.g. Goal Seek/Solver) tests different inputs under constraints.

dseDb.q: When creating a database table in database software, what should users usually set?
st: The data type of each field
dseDb.e: You define field data types and a primary key. You do not normally fix a maximum number of records.

dseDb.q: Mary is a marketing manager and plans to send invitation letters to selected customers. She will extract data from a customer database. What information processes should she do?
dseDb.e: Filter to select customers, then mail merge to make letters. What-if analysis is for spreadsheet modelling.

dseDb.q: What is/are the major advantage(s) of using a form for data entry in database software?
st: It shortens the execution time of SQL statements.
dseDb.e: Forms give a friendly layout with controls/validation → fewer input errors. They don't speed up SQL or save storage.

dseDb.q:

SELECT FNAME
FROM FRUIT
WHERE QTY > 0
ORDER BY QTY DESC
o: Fruits are listed in descending order of fruit name.
Fruits are listed in ascending order of the quantity in stock.
Fruits with low quantities in stock are listed in ascending order of fruit name.
Fruits are listed in descending order of the quantity in stock.
dseDb.e: ORDER BY QTY DESC sorts by quantity, highest first. Only fruits in stock (QTY > 0) appear.

dseDb.q: A standalone computer runs slow when working on database software. Which of the following hardware components should be upgraded?
dseDb.e: More RAM helps. ROM is not upgraded for speed, and a standalone computer does not use the network.

dseDb.q: Which of the following clauses should be used in a SELECT SQL command for displaying information where salary is greater than 5000 in ascending order of salary?
o: WHERE salary > 5000 AND ORDER BY salary
HAVING salary > 5000 OR ORDER BY salary
dseDb.e: Row conditions go in WHERE (HAVING is for groups). ORDER BY is a separate clause, not joined with AND/OR; ascending is the default.

dseDb.q:

IF (MARKS >= 50) THEN
     OUTPUT 'PASS'
ELSE
     OUTPUT 'FAIL'
Which of the following sets of test values is appropriate?
dseDb.e: Good test data covers both outcomes and the boundary: 99 (pass), 0 (fail) and 50 (boundary).

dseDb.q: Which of the following is not required for a mail merge using a word processor?
dseDb.e: Mail merge needs a data source, a main document and merge fields. Field length is not needed.

dseDb.e: Online meetings are smooth, so the network is fine. Slow queries point to the CPU and weak 4K playback to the display card.

dseDb.q: Peter wants to extract records with a data item within a range of values from a database. Which of the following SQL operators should he use?
dseDb.e: BETWEEN x AND y selects values in a range.

o: Only small files can be stored.
The operating system requires less system memory to operate.
